status.description: Key-value pairs that report port status.  Supported status values are [type](#/Interface)-dependent; some interfaces may not have a valid [driver_name](#/Interface), for example.

driver_name.description: The name of the device driver controlling the network adapter.

driver_version.description: The version string of the device driver controlling the network adapter.

firmware_version.description: The version string of the network adapter's firmware, if available.

kernel_interface_error.description: Human readable kernel interface provisioning error description.

lldp_local_port_description.description: Description of LLDP port in alpha-numeric format.

lldp_pse_tlv_sent_type.description: LLDP TLV type sent by the Power Sourcing Equipment.

sflow_status.description: Status of sFlow on LAG member or physical interface. Only provided if sFlow is configured globally. OK: sFlow is operational. ERR_MIRROR_CONFLICT: Failed to apply sFlow in ASIC because ingress mirror config is already present ERR_ASIC: An error in ASIC and the cause is unknown ERR_OTHER: Any other error that may be returned before going to ASIC

traffic_manager_id.description: Identifier for the traffic manager used by the port.

type.description: The interface type, one of:  `system`:           Regular, physical interface of the system. `internal_bridge`:  A simulated network device that represents the bridge and is used.                     for providing L3 traffic to the control plane. `vlan`:             Generally represents SVI - L3 Vlan interfaces. `vlansubint`:       A sub-interface created for a physical interface based on dot1q encapsulation. `loopback`:         A loopback interface is a virtual interface, supporting                     ipv4/ipv6 address configuration, that remains up until it is deleted                     by administrator. Loopback interface ip address is used as router-id                     and source address by many protocols. `gre_ipv4`:         ipv4 GRE tunnel. `ipv6_in_ipv4`:     IPv6 in IPv4 tunnel. `ipv6_in_ipv6`:     IPv6 in IPv6 tunnel. `vxlan`:            VXLAN interface `vxlan_ipv6`:       IPv6 VXLAN interface `ubt`:              User Based Tunnel L2GRE interface `internal_l3vni`:   L3VNI interface.

udld_active.description: The running state of the UDLD protocol on this interface. For UDLD to be running, it has to be enabled and the link has to be up.

udld_enable.description: UDLD protocol is enabled or not on this interface.

udld_hpe_anw_compatibility_mode.description: Configured UDLD operation mode for HPE ANW. In `verify_then_forward` the interface starts out blocked and will not forward traffic until UDLD determines that the interface is bidirectional. With `forward_then_verify` the interface starts out unblocked.

udld_interface_state.description: Reports the current interface state defined by the internal finite state machine of the UDLD protocol.

udld_interface_status.description: Reports the current interface status defined by the UDLD protocol. In `block` the interface should not forward traffic. In `unblock` the interface can normally forward traffic.

udld_interval.description: The time interval in milliseconds to send UDLD packets.  If 'udld_compatibility' value is 'rfc5171' and time interval is below valid range for RFC 5171 (7000 - 90000), then it will be forced to 7000.

udld_remote_system_id.description: Remote system's ID. It corresponds to the remote bridge MAC address.

udld_retries.description: Number of retries before changing the UDLD interface status to `block`.

udld_rfc5171_compatibility_mode.description: Configured UDLD operation mode for RFC5171. In `normal` mode, once the link is determined to be in unidirectional state (after it was deemed bidireccional), and no "Echo" is received, it is set to "undetermined" state. However, if a a UDLD packet with an empty "Echo" is received the interface will be set to "errDisabled". In `aggressive` , once a link is determined to be in unidirectional state (after it was deemed bidirectional), and no "Echo" is received, it is set to "errDisabled" state. The interface will also be set to "errDisabled" if a UDLD packet with an empty "Echo" is received.

udld_port_transitions.description: Number of times the UDLD interface has changed from blocked to unblocked, or vice versa.

udld_rx_discarded.description: Number of UDLD packets received and discarded.

user_config.description: Key-value pairs that stores the user configuration of [Interface](#/Interface).

admin.description: The user-configured administrative state of Interface. If not configured, the default behavior depends on the 'type': 'vlan':                  'up' 'gre_ipv4 tunnel':       'down' 'ipv6_in_ipv4 tunnel':   'down' 'ipv6_in_ipv6 tunnel':   'down' 'loopback':              'up' 'system':              'down' 'vxlan':               'down' 'ubt':                 'down'

autoneg.description: The user-configured autonegotiation state of [Interface](Interface). The possible values are "on" and "off".

duplex.description: The user-configured duplex mode of [Interface](Interface). The possible values are "half" and "full".

error_control.description: The Ethernet error control, a.k.a Forward Error Correction (FEC), mode  to use for this interface. When set, this overrides the mode that would  normally be used based on the installed transceiver. When not set, the  standard mode for the installed transceiver is used.   'auto'      : use the transceiver default  'none'      : do not use any FEC  'base-r-fec': use IEEE BASE-R (Firecode) FEC  'rs-fec'    : use IEEE Reed-Solomon FEC

interpacket_gap.description: The gap between packets transmitted by this interface. This  setting only applies to interfaces that have the  `interpacket_gap_config` capability.   'default'     : use the system default gap  'high-average': use a higher average gap

lane_split.description: The user-configured split mode of the interface. This is only  applicable to multi-lane ports such as QSFP where each lane  can be used as a separate interface. When set to `split` the  parent interface is split and the `split_children` interfaces  can be enabled. All other values are treated as `no-split`.

leader_follower.description: For interfaces that support configurable leader-follower mode,  this is the configured mode.  'preferred-leader'  : advertise preference to be the leader  'preferred-follower': advertise preference to be the follower  'forced-leader'     : force the interface to be the leader  'forced-follower'   : force the interface to be the follower

link_clock_tolerance.description: For interfaces that support configurable link clock tolerance,  this is the mode to use.  'wide'  : use the widest tolerance setting available  'narrow': use the narrowest tolerance setting available

link_state_snmp_if_mib_trap.description: Enable the transmission of SNMP IF-MIB traps for link  state changes on this interface. Used to toggle  ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable to true or false.

link_state_snmp_trap.description: Enable the transmission of SNMP traps for link state changes on this interface.

pause.description: The user-configured Ethernet PAUSE (link-level flow control)  mode of [Interface](Interface). The possible values are  "none", "rx", "tx", "rxtx", and "pfc".

pause_override.description: When set, always use the configured pause mode and ignore the results of  autonegotiation with the link partner.

speeds.description: The list of user-configured interface speeds in megabits per second. When autonegotiation is disabled, the largest value in the list is applied.

split_count.description: When `lane_split` is `split`, this is the number of child  interfaces to activate. When not specified, the default is  4. This setting is ignored when the interface is not split.

split_speed.description: When `lane_split` is `split`, this is the preferred speed for  the child interfaces in megabits per second. When not  specified, the highest available speed is used. This setting  is ignored when the interface is not split.

system_lanes.description: The total number of SerDes lanes used by the installed  transceiver to communicate with the system. This setting only  applies to multi-lane port types such as QSFP-DD where a  transceiver may be installed that uses fewer lanes than the  port provides. It is ignored for other port types and for  split child ports. When not specified, the lane count defaults  to a value based on the port speed and maximum number of lanes  supported by the port.

vsx_force_shutdown.description: A value of 'true' implies VSX wants to shutdown the interface.

actor_key.description: The actor key in use (2 bytes) encoded as a string in which each byte value is separated by a colon. Example: 80:00

actor_port_id.description: Actor port ID is in the form of device priority (2 bytes) followed by port id (2 bytes) encoded as string in which each byte value is separated by a colon. Example: 00:08:00:12

actor_system_id.description: Actor system ID is in the form of device priority (2 bytes) followed by device MAC address (6 bytes) encoded as string in which each byte value is separated by a colon. Example: 00:08:00:02:82:1f:60:4a

xoff_limit_hw.description: Specifies the hardware-programmed XOFF limit value for ingress traffic. If the 'xoff_type_hw' is 'static', the value represents the hardware configuration in kilobytes. If the 'xoff_type_hw' is 'dynamic', the value represents the alpha factor used for the dynamic limit algorithm.

xoff_type_hw.description: Specifies the hardware-programmed XOFF limit type for ingress traffic. The limit type is either 'static' or 'dynamic'.

xon_delta_hw.description: Specifies the hardware-programmed XON delta amount for arriving traffic. The XON delta when subtracted from the XOFF limit gives the value of in-use kilobytes where an XON is sent to the peer to resume transmission.
