aclv6_routed_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv6_routed_in_cfg' column. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv6_routed_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv6_routed_out_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv6 ACL for routed egress traffic, potentially in flight desired to be applied to this VLAN interface, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). This configuration is applicable only when the port is a VLAN interface. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv6_routed_out_cfg_version.description: The version of the currently configured routed egress IPv6 ACL that corresponds to this configuration version vlaue. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the configured routed egress IPv6 ACL value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

admin.description: The administrative state of the Interface. If not configured, the default behavior depends on the 'type': 'mgmt':                'up' 'lag':                 'down' 'vlan':                'up' 'gre_ipv4 tunnel':     'down' 'ipv6_in_ipv4 tunnel': 'down' 'ipv6_in_ipv6 tunnel': 'down' 'loopback':            'up' 'system':              'down' 'vxlan':               'down' 'ubt':                 'down' When not set, the admin value will be based on the default behavior for the type of interface.

arp_timeout.description: Determines the time interval in seconds till when a neighbor entry is valid.

bfd_detect_multiplier.description: The number of negotiated min_rx_intervals that can occur before the BFD session is considered to be down. If not set, BFD detect-multiplier value configured at the system level will be used.

bfd_min_rx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can receive BFD control messages. Remote endpoints may send messages at a slower rate. If not present, the system value is used.

bfd_min_tx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can transmit BFD control messages. Messages will actually be transmitted at a slower rate if the remote endpoints cannot receive them as quickly as specified. If not present, the system value is used.

bond_active_slave.description: When configured, this represents the MAC address of the active member of LAG.

bond_mode.description: The type of bonding used for a bonded port. Bond mode controls the selection of a interface from a group of aggregate interfaces with which to transmit a frame. This selection is performed with a hash function using either source and destination mac addresses (l2), ip addresses (l3) or tcp/udp ports (l4) as parameters. Defaults to `l3-src-dst-hash` if not assigned.

cdp_disable.description: Disables reception and transmission of CDP packets on the interface, regardless of the system level configuration.

cdp_pre_standard_mode.description: Sets CDP pre standard mode in the interface : 'rx_only':If CDP voice VLAN query packet is received on this interface,           the switch responds with the voice VLAN TLV included in its advertisements. 'tx_rx'  :The switch includes voice VLAN TLV in its advertisements on this interface            regardless of whether it has received a query packet from the peer. 'disable':If CDP voice VLAN query packet is received on this interface, switch updates           CDP neighbor information received from the peer, but doesn't send any CDP           advertisements to it.

description.description: Description for the 'system' interfaces This column value can be empty.

mode.description: Indicates device-profile mode criteria to unblock the port. This is only applicable for L2 ports. 'block_until_profile_applied':   When set, the port is blocked                                   until a profile has been applied.

max_bindings.description: Indicates the maximum number of bindings allowed on the port. After reaching the limit, DHCP requests from new clients  on the port are dropped.

trusted.description: Indicates whether this port is trusted for DHCPv4 snooping. DHCPv4 packets received on untrusted ports are subject to  filtering and inspection prior to being forwarded out.

dhcpv4_snooping_guard_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCPv4_Snooping_Guard_Policy](#/DHCPv4_Snooping_Guard_Policy)
DHCPv4 Guard Policy for Port.

max_bindings.description: Indicates the maximum number of bindings allowed on the port. After reaching the limit, DHCP requests from new clients  on the port are dropped.

trusted.description: Indicates whether this port is trusted for DHCPv6 snooping. DHCPv6 packets received on untrusted ports are subject to  filtering and inspection prior to being forwarded out.

dhcpv6_snooping_guard_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCPv6_Snooping_Guard_Policy](#/DHCPv6_Snooping_Guard_Policy)
DHCPv6 Guard Policy for Port.

diagnostic_config.description: Key-value pairs used to perform interface diagnostics. Normally, this  map is empty. When an interface diagnostic is to be run, this column  is used to configure the interface in the correct mode and override  any user-configured settings that would affect the test.

admin.description: The administrative state of the [Interface](Interface) for  diagnostics. This value overrides the user-configured state.

allow_cpu_packet_tx_rx.description: Allow CPU packet ingress and egress operations.

diag_id.description: The diagnostic test ID that will be run once this configuration  is applied to the interface.

loopback_mode.description: The selected physical loopback mode: 'none':   Normal operation - no loopback 'packet': Loop back normal network packets 'prbs':   Loop back pseudo-random binary sequence data

dot1x_supplicant_macsec_enable.description: Enable MACsec via EAP for 802.1X supplicant.

dot1x_supplicant_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [Dot1X_Supplicant_Policy](#/Dot1X_Supplicant_Policy)
The 802.1X supplicant policy associated with the port. If a policy is not configured, the `default` policy will be used on the port.

icmp_redirect_disable.description: Disables ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 redirect messages. For the specific port, takes precedence over the same System configuration.

icmp_unreachable_disable.description: Disables ICMPv4 and ICMPv6 unreachable messages. For the specific port, takes precedence over the same System configuration.

icmp_unreachable_ratelimit.description: Rate limit (in milliseconds per message), that should be used for ICMP Unreachable  messages. For the specific port, takes precedence over the same System configuration.

igmp_router_alert_check_enable.description: Enable IGMP router-alert checking on this interface. This is only applicable to L3 interfaces.

interfaces.description:
Reference Resource: [Interface](#/Interface)
The port's interfaces. If there is more than one, this is a bonded Port. A maximum of 16 interfaces can be assigned to a port.

ip4_address.description: The IPv4 address and subnet mask in the address/mask format. This is the primary IP address.

ip4_address_secondary.description: This is a list of secondary IPv4 addresses and subnet mask in the address/mask format.

ip6_address_custom_link_local.description:
Reference Resource: [IP6_Address](#/IP6_Address)
References user configured link-local IPv6 address of the port.

ip_mtu.description: The user configured IP MTU of a port. This would be applicable for both IPv4 and IPv6.

ip_tcp_mss.description: TCP Maximum Segment Size (TCP MSS) specifies the largest amount of data, in bytes, that can be transmitted in a  single TCP segment without fragmentation.

ipv4.description: Indicates IPv4 TCP MSS value on this port.

ipv6.description: Indicates IPv6 TCP MSS value on this port.

ipv4_source_lockdown_enable.description: Enables IP Lockdown feature on the port. When set, IPv4 packets received from the clients on this port are forwarded only  if there is an associated IP binding entry.

ipv6_address_autoconfig_enable.description: Enable automatic configuration of the IPv6 addresses.

ipv6_address_linklocal_enable.description: Enables IPV6 link-local address when global unicast address is  not configured.

ipv6_nd_dad_attempts.description: The number of Neighbor discovery packets to be sent for duplicate address detection.

ipv6_nd_mtu.description: The MTU option is used in router advertisement messages to ensure that all nodes on a link use the same MTU value.

ipv6_nd_ns_interval.description: The interval (in milliseconds) between neighbor solicitation messages.

no-advertise.description: When set to `true`, the prefix will not be advertised.

no-autoconfig.description: When set to `true`, the prefix will not be used for address auto-configuration.

no-onlink.description: When set to `true`, router advertisement makes no statement about on-link or off-link properties of the prefix.

preferred_lifetime.description: This field sets the default preferred lifetime value to be used for RA prefixes. When used this will overwrite preferred lifetime value of all the prefixes. A value of `4294967295` seconds means infinite lifetime.

valid_lifetime.description: This field sets the default valid lifetime value to be used for RA prefixes. When used this will overwrite valid lifetime value of all the prefixes. A value of `4294967295` seconds means infinite lifetime.

ipv6_nd_ra_dnssl.description: Key-value pairs that maps DNS prefixes to their lifetime in seconds.

ipv6_nd_ra_hoplimit.description: The default value that will be used in RA message. If this value is not set,  then global ipv6 hoplimit value will be used in RA message.

ipv6_nd_ra_lifetime.description: The lifetime associated with the default router in units of seconds.

ipv6_nd_ra_managed_flag.description: When set it indicates that addresses are available via DHCPV6.

ipv6_nd_ra_max_interval.description: The maximum interval (in seconds) between sending router advertisements.

ipv6_nd_ra_min_interval.description: The minimum interval (in seconds) between sending router advertisements.

ipv6_nd_ra_other_config_flag.description: When set it indicates that other configuration information(DNS) is available via DHCPV6.

ipv6_nd_ra_rdnss.description: Key-value pairs that maps RDNS server addresses to their lifetime in seconds.

ipv6_nd_ra_reachable_time.description: The time, in milliseconds, that a node assumes a neighbor is reachable after having received a reachability confirmation.

ipv6_nd_ra_retransmit_timer.description: The value to be placed in retransmission timer field in router advertisement messages sent by router.

ipv6_nd_router_preference.description: The preference associated with the default router.

all.description: when set to `true`, router advertisement messages are not sent.

dnssl.description: when set to `true`, DNSSL field (ICMPv6 option type 31) is not included in the router advertisement messages.

mtu.description: when set to `true`, MTU field (ICMPv6 option type 5) is not included in the router advertisement messages.

rdnss.description: when set to `true`, RDNSS field (ICMPv6 option type 25) is not included in the router advertisement messages.

ipv6_neighbor_timeout.description: Determines the time interval in seconds till when an IPv6 neighbor entry is valid.

ipv6_source_lockdown_enable.description: Enables IP Lockdown feature on the port. When set, IPv6 packets received from the clients on this port are forwarded only  if there is an associated IP binding entry.

l3_counters_enable.description: Indicates which L3 counters are enabled for this Port

rx.description: When set to 'true', L3 RX Counters are enabled for this Port.

tx.description: When set to 'true', L3 TX Counters are enabled for this Port.

lacp.description: Configures LACP on this port.  LACP allows directly connected switches to negotiate which links may be bonded.  LACP may be enabled on non-bonded ports for the benefit of any switches they may be connected to.  `active` ports are allowed to initiate LACP negotiations.  `passive` ports are allowed to participate in LACP negotiations initiated by a remote switch, but not allowed to initiate such negotiations themselves.  If LACP is enabled on a port whose partner switch does not support LACP, the bond will be disabled. Defaults to `off` if unset.

lldp_auto_flush.description: Automatic flushing of LLDP neighbors on an interface.

link_down_enable.description: When set to `true`, LLDP neighbors will be flushed when the interface goes down and setting of `false` would disable it. The default value is `false`.

lldp_if_mgmt_addr_ipv4.description: IPv4 Address to be advertised in management address TLV.

lldp_if_mgmt_addr_ipv6.description: IPv6 Address to be advertised in management address TLV.

ca_type.description: A one octet descriptor of the data civic address value.

lldp_med_loc_civic_info.description: The civic info which includes 'country code' and 'what number' for advertisements specific to LLDP-MED. This column value can be empty.If not set civic info will not be advertise specific to LLDP-MED.

lldp_med_loc_elin_info.description: LLDP-MED Elin Location configured for this interface. This column value can be empty. If not set LLDP_MED Elin will not be configured for the interface

llfc_pool_id.description: Specifies the pool used for arriving packets, only applicable  for link-level flow-control modes 'Tx' and 'RxTx'.

loop_protect_action.description: This determines action for the Loop-protect feature.The value is set to "tx- port-disable" for disabling the sending port on detecting a loop, "tx-rx- disable" disables both sending and receiving ports when loop is detected and "do-not-disable" will not disable any port. Default value is `tx-port-disable`.

loop_protect_enable.description: When set to `true`, Loop-protect is enabled on this port. Default value is `false`.

loop_protect_stagger_count.description: This determines the number of loop protect PDUs to be received  before taking a receiver action.

mac.description: The MAC address to use for this port for the purpose of choosing the bridge's MAC address.  This column does not necessarily reflect the port's actual MAC address, nor will setting it change the port's actual MAC address.

mac_notify_type.description: Define the four events that the SNMP Trap will monitor 1 - learned (On this port a MAC learn occured) 2 - removed (On the enabled port a MAC was removed) 3 - aged    (On the enabled port a MAC has aged out) 4 - moved    (On the enabled port a MAC has moved) empty - Empty value will be treated as invalid

macsec_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [MACsec_Policy](#/MACsec_Policy)
MACsec policy associated with the port. When not set, MACsec is not operational on the port even if there is a MKA policy associated with it.

macsec_selftest_run_requested.description: The number of times a request was made by the user to run MACsec selftest for this interface. When MACsec selftest is enabled globally, incrementing this column will initiate a new selftest that will cause a loss of link for several seconds.

mgmd_acl.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Ingress ACL to filter processing of MGMD reports and leave messages received from hosts. When this is not configured, all MGMD reports and leave messages will be processed.

mgmd_enable.description: Enable or disable IGMP/MLD on the L3 Port.  By default, IGMP/MLD is disabled on the L3 Port.

mgmd_igmp_static_groups.description: List of IGMP static group and source IP addresses.  The entries are stored in the Source_Group format.Source is the Source IP Address and Group is the Group IP Address.

mgmd_igmp_version.description: The IGMP protocol version to use.  When IGMP is disabled, this field would be empty. If there is a version mismatch between L2 and L3 VLAN, it will pick the lowest version.

mgmd_last_member_query_interval.description: The time interval that the querier waits to receive a response from members to a group-specific query message. It also specifies the amount of time between successive group-specific query messages. The default value is 1 second.

mgmd_mld_static_groups.description: List of MLD static group and source IP addresses.  The entries are stored in the Source_Group format. Source is the Source IP Address and Group is the Group IP Address.

mgmd_mld_version.description: The MLD protocol version to use.  When MLD is disabled, this field would be empty. If there is a version mismatch between L2 and L3 VLAN, it will pick the lowest version.

mgmd_querier_enable.description: Enable/Disable the IGMP/MLD Querier Functionality on the L3 Port. The default value is disabled.

mgmd_querier_interval.description: Interval between successive IGMP/MLD All Host Queries that will be sent. The default value is 125 sec.

mgmd_querier_max_response_time.description: The time interval to wait for a response to a IGMP/MLD query. The default value is 10 seconds.

mgmd_querier_wait_time.description: The interval in seconds a device will wait to hear from a Querier before assuming Querier role. The default is 260 seconds.

mgmd_robustness.description: The number of times to retry a query.  The default value is 2.

mgmd_snoop_fastlearn_enable.description: Set this value to true to enable IGMP/MLD fastlearn for the port and false to disable IGMP/MLD fastlearn.  By default the feature is disabled for IGMP/MLD.

mgmd_strict_version_enable.description: Process only the configured version packets.  When a key-value is not specified, strict version is disabled.

mka_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [MKA_Policy](#/MKA_Policy)
MKA policy associated with the port.

mpls_admin.description: The administrative state of MPLS in the Interface.

mpls_ldp_admin.description: The administrative state of MPLS LDP in the Interface.

mpls_ldp_discovery_hold_time.description: MPLS LDP discovery hold time is duration (in seconds). LSR  will keep the peer in the discovered list without receiving  a Hello message. An empty entry indicates the interface is  configued with the global LDP table discovery hold time value.  A non-zero entry indicates the user wants to override the global  discovery hold time. This column value can be empty.

mpls_ldp_discovery_transport_address.description: IP address to be advertised as the transport address in  discovery hello messages. This column value can be empty.

mpls_ldp_explicit_null.description: The value `true` indicates Explicit Null label will be  advertised in situations where it would normally advertise  an Implicit Null label.

mpls_ldp_session_hold_time.description: MPLS LDP session hold time is duration (in seconds) an LDP  session will not be torn down in the absence of a keep alive  message. An empty entry indicates the interface is configued  with the global LDP table session hold time value. A non-zero  entry indicates the user wants to override the global session  hold time. This column value can be empty.

multicast_boundary_acl_in.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Ingress multicast boundary ACL desired to be applied on the current interface to filter all the multicast data and control packets.

multicast_boundary_acl_out.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Egress multicast boundary ACL desired to be applied on the current interface to filter IGMP and PIM control packets. This is used to control if the current interface can be added as an outgoing interface in a multicast route or not. If the ACL denies IGMP and PIM joins, this interface will not be added as an outgoing interface.

mvrp_enable.description: The value `true` indicates MVRP is enabled on this port.

mvrp_forbidden_vlans.description: Specifies the VLANs that should not be learned on the port. If the registration mode of the port is "forbidden" and there are no VLANs in the forbidden list , then none of the VLANs are learned on this port.

mvrp_registration.description: Defines the mode of operation of all the registrar state machines associated with the port. The different mode of operations are In "normal" mode, the Registrar responds to incoming MRP messages. In "fixed" mode, the Registrar ignores all MRP messages, and remains in the registered state. In "forbidden" mode, the Registrar ignores all MRP messages, and remains in the unregistered state.

mvrp_timers.description: Specifies the different timers and their corresponding  intervals in centiseconds. The MVRP standard defines all timer intervals in centiseconds(cs). 100 cs is 1 second.

join.description: The MVRP join time interval, in centiseconds.

leave.description: The MVRP leave time interval, in centiseconds.

leaveall.description: The MVRP leave all time, in centiseconds.

periodic.description: Interval at which the periodic transmission state machine of a MVRP instance generates transmission opportunities, in centiseconds.

max_bindings.description: Indicates the maximum number of bindings allowed on the port. After reaching the limit, ND packets from new clients on  the port are dropped.

trusted.description: Indicates whether this port is trusted for ND snooping. ND packets received on untrusted ports are subject to  filtering and inspection prior to being forwarded out.

local_ip.description: Local IP of the tunnel. Incoming packets must match it  in their destination IP. Number of unique local IPs is  limited and provided in tunnel_unique_local_ips capacity.   An IP address (not a DNS name), e.g. `192.168.12.3` or `1000::1.  Configuration of local IP addresses which do not correspond to the  tunnel type will be ignored (IPv6 addresses for GRE IPv4 tunnels, and IPv4 addresses for GRE IPv6 tunnels).

remote_ip.description: Required tunnel parameter.  The remote tunnel endpoint, one of:   An IP address (not a DNS name), e.g. `192.168.0.123` or `1920::2`. Only unicast endpoints are supported.  Configuration of remote IP addresses which do not correspond to the  tunnel type will be ignored (IPv6 addresses for GRE IPv4 tunnels,  and IPv4 addresses for GRE IPv6 tunnels).

ttl.description: TTL to use on the outgoing tunneled packets. Number of  unique tunnel TTL values on the system is limited and  provided in the tunnel_unique_ttls capacity.

tunnel_source_intf.description: Source interface to be used for the tunnel. If both local_ip and tunnel_source_intf are configured, local_ip will take precedence.

vxlan_dest_udp_port.description: Destination UDP port to be used for VXLAN encapsulation.

ospf_auth_keychain.description:
Reference Resource: [Keychain](#/Keychain)
The "Keychain" used for cryptographic authentication. Supports MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 algorithms. If not set, keychain authentication is not operational on that port.

ospf_auth_md5_keys.description: The authentication keys for OSPFv2 authentication type "md5".

ospf_auth_sha_keys.description: The authentication keys for OSPFv2 authentication type "sha".

ospf_auth_text_key.description: The authentication key for OSPFv2 authentication type "text". If not set, OSPFv2 authentication is not operational on that port.

ospf_auth_type.description: The type of OSPFv2 authentication. If not set, then parent area level authentication holds for the port.

ospf_bfd.description: Specifies whether OSPF router global BFD mode should be overridden for this particular interface: 'enable':  Enables BFD, regardless of OSPF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'disable': Disables BFD, regardless of OSPF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'default': Keeps BFD disabled or enabled according to OSPF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable.

ospf_if_out_cost.description: The output cost configured on the corresponding OSPFv2 interface. If not set, OSPF will calculate cost for this interface based on link speed and reference bandwidth. Any configured value will override the automatic cost calculation.

ospf_if_shutdown.description: Shut OSPF down on this interface.

ospf_if_type.description: The type of the OSPFv2 network interface. The default value is the type of the interface from the Interface table. If not set, OSPFv2 interface is not up or not configured on that interface.

dead_interval.description: The time duration, in seconds, that a neighbor should wait for a Hello packet before tearing down adjacencies with the local router. The dead_interval must be equal to or in multiples of the hello_interval.

hello_interval.description: The Hello packet will be sent every hello_interval timer value seconds. This value must be the same for all routers attached to a common network.

retransmit_interval.description: The number of seconds between LSA retransmissions. It is also used when retransmitting Database Description and Link State Request Packets.

transmit_delay.description: The estimated time in seconds to transmit an LSA to a neighbor. The transmit_delay timer increments the age of LSAs in the update packets to accommodate transmission and propagation delays for the interface. The timer is more important on very low speed links where the transmission delay is more significant.

ospf_priority.description: The router with the highest priority will be more eligible to become Designated Router. Setting the value to 0, makes the router ineligible to become Designated Router.

ospfv3_af_ipsec_ah.description: IPsec Authentication Header (AH) configuration. Specifies Security Parameters Index (SPI), authentication type and key to use. IPsec AH is preferred over IPsec  Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) if `ospfv3_af_ipsec_ah` and `ospfv3_af_ipsec_esp` both are configured.

ah_null.description: Disable OSPF IPsec AH authentication. This is used to override `OSPF_Area` level IPsec AH authentication. When IPsec AH is configured at `OSPF_Area`, set `true` to disable OSPF IPsec AH on this `Port`. When IPsec AH is configured at `OSPF_Area` and OSPF Interface, making `true` will remove OSPF Interface IPsec AH configuration and disable OSPF IPsec AH on this `Port`.

spi.description: Security Parameters Index (SPI) for the Security Association (SA). AH SPI must be unique on a router because it is carried in IPsec protocol packet to enable the receiving system to select the SA to process the packet.

ospfv3_af_ipsec_esp.description: IPsec Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) configuration. Specifies Security Parameters Index (SPI), encryption/authentication type and key to use. IPsec Authentication Header (AH) is preferred over IPsec ESP if `ospfv3_af_ipsec_ah` and `ospfv3_af_ipsec_esp` both are configured.

esp_null.description: Disable OSPF IPsec ESP encryption and authentication. This is used to override `OSPF_Area` level IPsec ESP encryption and authentication. When IPsec ESP is configured at `OSPF_Area`, set `true` to disable OSPF IPsec ESP on this `Port`. When IPsec ESP is configured at `OSPF_Area` and OSPF Interface, making `true` will remove OSPF Interface IPsec ESP configuration and disable OSPF IPsec ESP on this `Port`.

spi.description: Security Parameters Index (SPI) for the Security Association (SA). ESP SPI must be unique on a router because it is carried in IPsec protocol packet to enable the receiving system to select the SA to process the packet.

ospfv3_afv4_bfd.description: Specifies whether OSPFv3 AF router global BFD mode should be overridden for this particular interface: 'enable':  Enables BFD, regardless of OSPFv3 AF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'disable': Disables BFD, regardless of OSPFv3 AF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'default': Keeps BFD disabled or enabled according to OSPFv3 AF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable.

ospfv3_afv4_dead_interval.description: The time duration, in seconds, that a neighbor should wait for a Hello packet before tearing down adjacencies with the local router.

ospfv3_afv4_hello_interval.description: The Hello packet will be sent every hello interval timer value seconds. This value must be the same for all routers attached to a common network.

ospfv3_afv4_if_cost.description: The output cost configured on the corresponding OSPFv3 interface. If not set, OSPFv3 will calculate cost for this interface based on link speed and reference bandwidth. Any configured value will override the automatic cost calculation.

ospfv3_afv4_if_priority.description: The router with the highest priority will be more eligible to become Designated Router. Setting the value to `0`, makes the router ineligible to become Designated Router.

ospfv3_afv4_if_shutdown.description: Shutdown OSPFv3 IPv4 Address family on this interface.

ospfv3_afv4_if_type.description: The type of the OSPFv3 network interface. The default value is the type of the interface from the Interface table. If not set, OSPFv3 interface is not up or not configured on that interface.

ospfv3_afv4_retransmit_interval.description: The number of seconds between LSA retransmissions. It is also used when retransmitting Database Description and Link State Request Packets.

ospfv3_afv4_transmit_delay.description: The estimated time in seconds to transmit an LSA to a neighbor. The transmit delay timer increments the age of LSAs in the update packets to accommodate transmission and propagation delays for the interface. The timer is more important on very low speed links where the transmission delay is more significant.

ospfv3_afv6_bfd.description: Specifies whether OSPFv3 AF router global BFD mode should be overridden for this particular interface: 'enable':  Enables BFD, regardless of OSPFv3 AF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'disable': Disables BFD, regardless of OSPFv3 AF router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'default': Keeps BFD disabled or enabled according to OSPFv3 router bfd_all_interfaces_enable.

ospfv3_afv6_dead_interval.description: The time duration, in seconds, that a neighbor should wait for a Hello packet before tearing down adjacencies with the local router.

ospfv3_afv6_hello_interval.description: The Hello packet will be sent every hello interval timer value seconds. This value must be the same for all routers attached to a common network.

ospfv3_afv6_if_cost.description: The output cost configured on the corresponding OSPFv3 interface. If not set, OSPFv3 will calculate cost for this interface based on link speed and reference bandwidth. Any configured value will override the automatic cost calculation.

ospfv3_afv6_if_priority.description: The router with the highest priority will be more eligible to become Designated Router. Setting the value to `0`, makes the router ineligible to become Designated Router.

ospfv3_afv6_if_shutdown.description: Shutdown OSPFv3 IPv6 Address Family on this interface.

ospfv3_afv6_if_type.description: The type of the OSPFv3 network interface. The default value is the type of the interface from the Interface table. If not set, OSPFv3 interface is not up or not configured on that interface.

ospfv3_afv6_retransmit_interval.description: The number of seconds between LSA retransmissions. It is also used when retransmitting Database Description and Link State Request Packets.

ospfv3_afv6_transmit_delay.description: The estimated time in seconds to transmit an LSA to a neighbor. The transmit delay timer increments the age of LSAs in the update packets to accommodate transmission and propagation delays for the interface. The timer is more important on very low speed links where the transmission delay is more significant.

ospfv3_bfd.description: Specifies whether OSPFv3 router global BFD mode should be overridden for this particular interface: 'enable':  Enables BFD, regardless of OSPFv3 router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'disable': Disables BFD, regardless of OSPFv3 router bfd_all_interfaces_enable. 'default': Keeps BFD disabled or enabled according to OSPFv3 router bfd_all_interfaces_enable.

ospfv3_dead_interval.description: The time duration, in seconds, that a neighbor should wait for a Hello packet before tearing down adjacencies with the local router.

ospfv3_hello_interval.description: The Hello packet will be sent every hello interval timer value seconds. This value must be the same for all routers attached to a common network.

ospfv3_if_cost.description: The output cost configured on the corresponding OSPFv3 interface. If not set, OSPFv3 will calculate cost for this interface based on link speed and reference bandwidth. Any configured value will override the automatic cost calculation.

ospfv3_if_priority.description: The router with the highest priority will be more eligible to become Designated Router. Setting the value to `0`, makes the router ineligible to become Designated Router.

ospfv3_if_type.description: The type of the OSPFv3 network interface. The default value is the type of the interface from the Interface table. If not set, OSPFv3 interface is not up or not configured on that interface.

ospfv3_ipsec_ah.description: IPsec Authentication Header (AH) configuration. Specifies Security Parameters Index (SPI), authentication type and key to use. IPsec AH is preferred over IPsec  Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) if `ospfv3_ipsec_ah` and `ospfv3_ipsec_esp` both are configured.

ah_null.description: Disable OSPF IPsec AH authentication. This is used to override `OSPF_Area` level IPsec AH authentication. When IPsec AH is configured at `OSPF_Area`, set `true` to disable OSPF IPsec AH on this `Port`. When IPsec AH is configured at `OSPF_Area` and OSPF Interface, making `true` will remove OSPF Interface IPsec AH configuration and disable OSPF IPsec AH on this `Port`.

spi.description: Security Parameters Index (SPI) for the Security Association (SA). AH SPI must be unique on a router because it is carried in IPsec protocol packet to enable the receiving system to select the SA to process the packet.

ospfv3_ipsec_esp.description: IPsec Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) configuration. Specifies Security Parameters Index (SPI), encryption/authentication type and key to use. IPsec Authentication Header (AH) is preferred over IPsec ESP if `ospfv3_ipsec_ah` and ospfv3_`ipsec_esp` both are configured.

esp_null.description: Disable OSPF IPsec ESP encryption and authentication. This is used to override `OSPF_Area` level IPsec ESP encryption and authentication. When IPsec ESP is configured at `OSPF_Area`, set `true` to disable OSPF IPsec ESP on this `Port`. When IPsec ESP is configured at `OSPF_Area` and OSPF Interface, making `true` will remove OSPF Interface IPsec ESP configuration and disable OSPF IPsec ESP on this `Port`.

spi.description: Security Parameters Index (SPI) for the Security Association (SA). ESP SPI must be unique on a router because it is carried in IPsec protocol packet to enable the receiving system to select the SA to process the packet.

ospfv3_retransmit_interval.description: The number of seconds between LSA retransmissions. It is also used when retransmitting Database Description and Link State Request Packets.

ospfv3_transmit_delay.description: The estimated time in seconds to transmit an LSA to a neighbor. The transmit delay timer increments the age of LSAs in the update packets to accommodate transmission and propagation delays for the interface. The timer is more important on very low speed links where the transmission delay is more significant.

lacp-aggregation-key.description: The LACP aggregation key of this [Interface](Interface). [Interface](Interface)s with different aggregation keys may not be active within a given [Port](Port) at the same time.

lacp-port-id.description: The LACP port ID of this [Interface](Interface).  Port IDs are used in LACP negotiations to identify individual ports participating in a bond.

lacp-port-priority.description: The LACP port priority of this [Interface](Interface).  In LACP negotiations [Interface](Interface)s with numerically lower priorities are preferred for aggregation.

lldp_dot3_macphy_disable.description: Disables the transmission and reception of LLDP DOT3 MAC PHY TLV on this interface.

lldp_dot3_mfs_disable.description: Disables the transmission and reception of LLDP DOT3 MFS TLV on this interface.

lldp_dot3_poe_disable.description: Configurable flag to control whether LLDP dot3 PoE TLV type is exchanged on this [Interface](Interface). A setting of `true` would ignore the TLV type, and a setting of `false` would enable exchanges of this TLV type. The default value is `false`.

lldp_med_capability_disable.description: Disables the transmission and reception of LLDP MED Capability TLV on this interface.

lldp_med_network_policy_disable.description: Disables the transmission and reception of LLDP MED Network Policy TLV on this interface.

lldp_med_poe_disable.description: Configurable flag to control whether LLDP MED PoE TLV type is honored on this [Interface](Interface). A setting of `true` would ignore the TLV type, and a setting of `false` would honor it. The default value is `false`.

lldp_med_poe_priority_override.description: Configurable flag to control whether a powered device (PD) connected to this [Interface](Interface) is allowed to override user-configured port priority through an LLDP MED TLV. A value of `true` allows the the PD to override the configured priority. The default value is `false`.

lldp_med_topology_notification_disable.description: Disables the transmission of LLDP MED Topology change trap on this interface.

lldp_trap_enable.description: Enables the transmission of SNMP traps for LLDP neighbor changes on this interface.

config.description: User configured persona enum limited to access - access port - default uplink - uplink port as defined in ports.yaml custom - user defined custom value

custom.description: Custom persona value that user can input when config is custom

mode.description: Persona mode: attach - Row config is applied and follows the config          of its persona copy   - Row config is applied once

pfc_priorities_config.description: The user configured priorities for priority-based flow control. This field is only valid when interface_flowcontrol_pfc capability  is present and the "pause" key of the user_config  is set to "pfc".

pim_bfd.description: 'enable':  Enables BFD on this interface overriding the PIM router BFD configuration            [bfd_all_interfaces_enable](#/PIM_Router) in [PIM_Router](#/PIM_Router). 'disable': Disables BFD on this interface overriding the PIM router BFD configuration            [bfd_all_interfaces_enable](#/PIM_Router) in [PIM_Router](#/PIM_Router). 'default': Keeps BFD enabled or disabled on this interface based on the PIM router BFD configuration            [bfd_all_interfaces_enable](#/PIM_Router) in [PIM_Router](#/PIM_Router).

ipv4.description: When set to 'true', the router treats the interface as a boundary for PIM IPv4 Bootstrap messages.  BSMs received on the boundary interface will dropped and BSMs are not forwarded out of the boundary interface.

ipv6.description: When set to 'true', the router treats the interface as a boundary for PIM6 Bootstrap messages.  BSMs received on the boundary interface will dropped and BSMs are not forwarded out of the boundary interface.

ipv4.description: When set to 'true', the router forwards multicast data received on the vxlan  l3 VNI fabric to this interface regardless of whether a multicast join was received  on this interface or not. This allows for the VSX devices to be in the same  multicast datapath state. This is applicable for both SVI and ROP interfaces.

ipv6.description: When set to 'true', the router forwards multicast data received on the vxlan  l3 VNI fabric to this interface regardless of whether a multicast join was received  on this interface or not. This allows for the VSX devices to be in the same  multicast datapath state. This is applicable for both SVI and ROP interfaces.

pim_dense_graft_retry_interval.description: Time (in seconds) that this port waits for a PIM graft  acknowledgement from its peer before it retransmit  another graft datagram.

pim_dense_max_graft_retries.description: Number of times the port will re-transmit PIM graft datagrams.

pim_dense_ttl_threshold.description: This is the minimum TTL value that state refresh messages received from a peer must have, to be eligible for forwarding to other peers.

pim_dr_priority.description: Designated Router(DR) Priority for this port.

pim_hello_interval.description: Interval (in seconds) at which PIM Hello messages are transmitted on this port.

pim_lan_prune_delay_disable.description: This entry specifies whether LAN prune delay option is enabled on this port.

pim_override_interval.description: Override Interval (in milliseconds) on this port.

pim_propagation_delay.description: Propagation Delay (in milliseconds) on this port.

pim_source_address.description: IP address used as the source address for the PIM protocol packets outbound on this port. If the value is not specified or empty then the primary IP of the port will be used as the source IP.

pim_trig_hello_interval.description: Maximum time (in seconds) before this port transmits the initial PIM hello message on bootup or a triggered Hello message to a rebooting neighbor.

policy_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [Policy](#/Policy)
Ingress Classifier Policy, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this port, as identified in the policy. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

policy_in_cfg_version.description: The version of 'policy_in_cfg'. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'policy_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

policy_routed_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [Policy](#/Policy)
Classifier policy for routed ingress traffic, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this port, as identified in the policy. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

policy_routed_in_cfg_version.description: The version of 'policy_routed_in_cfg'. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'policy_routed_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

port_access_allow_bpdu.description: Enables LLDP and/or CDP BPDU to be accepted before authentication.

port_access_allow_flood_traffic.description: Enables transmission of flood-traffic (broadcast, multicast and unknown unicast) out ports that are security blocked. A port is security blocked when authentication is enabled for that port and no client has yet been authenticated on this port.

port_access_allow_proxy_logoff.description: Proxy logoff the client based on port status in protocol packet. Switch will clear authentication session of the host, if switch receives port down status in protocol packet. When not configured, no action is taken. This is only applicable when port-access authentication is enabled for this port.

port_access_auth_configurations.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Auth_Configuration](#/Port_Access_Auth_Configuration)
Authentication method specific port-access configurations on this interface.

port_access_auth_mode.description: Indicates, whether each individual client on the port needs to be authenticated separately to gain access to the network. `client-mode`: every client needs to be authenticated to be                granted network access. `device-mode`: only one of the attached clients must be                authenticated for all clients to be granted                network access. `multi-domain`:limit the number of authenticated clients to one                 'voice' client and a configured number of 'data'                 clients. By default allowed 'data' client is                 also one.

port_access_auth_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role to be applied for clients that have been authenticated but not received any specific role or attribute from the authentication server. When not set, no role is applied for clients that successfully authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

port_access_clients_limit.description: Maximum number of clients that can be authenticated on this port.

port_access_concurrent_onboarding.description: Enable authentication methods to start concurrently for faster onboarding. If not set, clients are onboarded based on the order specified by `port_access_onboarding_precedence`.

port_access_critical_auth_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication due to unreachable authentication servers. When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

port_access_critical_voice_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role to be applied to 'voice' client that have failed re-authentication due to servers being unreachable. When not set, no role will be applied for voice clients when they fail re-authentication due to server being unreachable.

port_access_disable_cdp_auth.description: Disable BPDU triggered authentication for CDP.  This is only applicable when port access authentication is  enabled for this port.

port_access_disable_lldp_auth.description: Disable BPDU triggered authentication for LLDP.  This is only applicable when port access authentication is  enabled for this port.

final_authentication_failure_enable.description: When set to 'true', the switch automatically logs-off a port-access client if it fails authentication with all the enabled authentication methods. The authentication failure reason should not be one of server-reject or server-timeout.

port_access_fallback_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role that will be applied to clients that have not been assigned a role via any of the onboarding methods. When not set, no role is applied for the client.

port_access_lldp_authentication_mac.description: MAC address to use when authentication is triggered by an LLDP frame. `chassis-mac`: Use the chassis MAC in LLDP TLV `source-mac`:  Use the source MAC in LLDP frame This is only applicable when port access authentication is enabled on this port.

port_access_mda_data_clients_limit.description: Maximum number of 'data' clients that can be authenticated  on this port when multi-domain is enabled. If the number of  'data' clients on this port exceeds this client limit, it will  be considered as a port-access violation and the configured  threshold-violation action will be performed.

port_access_onboarding_precedence.description: Precedence order for Port Access Authentication:  `aaa`:   Onboard clients based on AAA authentication.  `device-profile`: Onboard clients based on device-profile                     configuration. If empty, the default precedence order of aaa followed by  device-profile will be used.

port_access_pre_auth_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role to be applied for clients that are yet to be authenticated. When not set, no role is applied for clients while the authentication is in progress for the client.

port_access_reject_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role to be applied for clients that failed authentication When not set, no role is applied for clients that fail authentication.

action.description: Port access security violation actions: `notify`:   Send an SNMP trap and log an event when a violation occurs. `shutdown`: Send an SNMP trap, log an event and shutdown the port              when a violation occurs. This is only supported on physical ports.

recovery_timer.description: Time in seconds after which the port will be re-enabled  if it was shutdown in response to a violation event. This is only applicable if shutdown recovery is enabled.

shutdown_recovery_enable.description: Enable auto-recovery for the port. This is only relevant when  the violation action is set to shutdown. The port is re-enabled after the recovery timer has expired.

port_access_ubt_fallback_role.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
The role that will be applied to clients when corresponding UBT zone is not reachable. When not set, no role is applied for the client when the UBT zone is not reachable.

client_limit.description: Maximum number of clients that can be authorized on this port. Functionality is effective only if port security is enabled.

enable.description: Indicates whether port security is enabled or not on this port. Supported only on physical ports. 'true':  allows only authorized clients to access the network          on this port. 'false': disables port security on this port.

sticky_mac_learning_enable.description: Indicates whether port security sticky MAC learning is enabled on this port. This is only supported on physical ports.

port_security_static_client_mac_addr.description: MAC addresses of the clients that should be authorized on this port.

port_security_static_sticky_client_mac_a.description: MAC addresses of the sticky clients that should be authorized on this port.

portfilter.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
Set of ports that must not egress packets that were received on this port.

process_grat_arp.description: Disable processing gratituous ARP packets received on this port. This is only applicable to Layer-3 interfaces (SVIs, Routed ports or L3 LAG).

pvlan_port_type.description: Specifies the port's type in the context of Private VLANS. When not set, the port functions as an Inter Switch Link  if it is carrying traffic for PVLANs.

q_profile.description: References queue profile for this port. If this is unspecified, then the queue profile referenced in [System](#/System)) table q_profile will be used.

qos.description: References schedule profile for this port. If this is unspecified, then the schedule profile referenced in [System](#/System)) table qos will be used.

cos_override.description: Specifies an optional port PCP (Priority Code Point, formerly 802.1p CoS field) remark value on arriving packets. This will occur only when the port's effective trust mode is `none`. The new PCP is used when the packet is transmitted out a trunk with a VLAN tag. If the key is not specified, then no remark will occur.

dscp_override.description: Specifies an optional port DSCP remark to use for IP packets. This will occur only when the port's effective trust mode is `none`. If the key is not specified, then no override will be enabled.

qos_trust.description: Specifies the individual port QoS Trust Mode.  `none` - no fields are inspected on arriving packets. The initial local-priority and color meta-data values are taken  from the PCP 0 entry of the PCP-to-local-priority mapping (see [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry)).  `cos` - will use the PCP of the outermost 802.1 VLAN tag to index the  COS Map entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values  of the packet. For untagged packets, the initial local-priority  and color meta-data values are taken from the PCP 0 entry of the  PCP-to-local-priority mapping. (see [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry)).  `dscp` - will use the DSCP value of IP packets to index the DSCP Map entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.  For non-IP packets, what meta-data values are assigned is hardware dependent.  If the key is not specified, then the qos_trust value configured globally  will be used. (see [System](System))

ra_guard_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [RA_Guard_Policy](#/RA_Guard_Policy)
RA Guard policy associated with this Port. RR/RA packets received on this port will be inspected and permitted per the policy specification if the port is untrusted.

rate_interval.description: Interval in seconds to calculate interface rate statistics.

broadcast.description: Ingress broadcast rate-limit bandwidth value.  The type of unit is specified by 'rate_limits.broadcast_units'.

broadcast_units.description: For broadcast rate-limit value: kbps - the units are in kilobits per second. pps - the units are in packets per second. percent - the units are in percent of port speed.

egress_shape_burst.description: The burst size (in kilobytes) to apply to egress traffic.

egress_shape_rate.description: The bandwidth limit to apply to egress traffic.

egress_shape_rate_units.description: Units of the egress shape rate: kbps: kilobits per second. percent - the units are in percentage of port speed.

multicast.description: Ingress multicast rate-limit bandwidth value.  The type of unit is specified by 'rate_limits.multicast_units'.

multicast_units.description: For multicast rate-limit value: kbps - the units are in kilobits per second. pps - the units are in packets per second. percent - the units are in percent of port speed.

unknown-unicast.description: Ingress unknown unicast rate-limit bandwidth value.  The type of unit is specified by 'rate_limits.unknown-unicast_units'.

unknown-unicast_units.description: For unknown-unicast rate-limit value: kbps - the units are in kilobits per second. pps - the units are in packets per second. percent - the units are in percent of port speed.

rdisc_irdp_broadcast.description: Specifies whether router advertisements should be sent using broadcast, 255.255.255.255 address. If the value is false (which is a default) the packets would be sent to multicast 224.0.0.1 address.

rdisc_irdp_enable.description: When set to `true`, IRDP is enabled on the port. The default value is `false`.

rdisc_irdp_preference.description: Specifies the preference level of this routing switch. Higher value indicates higher router preference. The default preference value is `0`.

irdp_hold_time.description: Specifies how long in seconds a host receiving a Router Advertisement considers it to be valid. The value must be no less than 'irdp_maxadv_interval'. The default is three times 'irdp_maxadv_interval'.

irdp_maxadv_interval.description: Specifies the maximum amount of time in seconds, router waits between sending Router Advertisements. Value cannot exceed 'irdp_hold_time'. The default is `600` seconds.

irdp_minadv_interval.description: Specifies the minimum amount of time in seconds, router waits between sending Router Advertisements. Value cannot exceed 'irdp_maxadv_interval'. The default is three-fourths the value of 'irdp_maxadv_interval'.

routing.description: Indicates whether the interface is routing or Layer 2. For routing interfaces, 'vrf' has to be properly populated. If not configured, default behavior depends on interface 'type': 'vlan':                  'true' 'gre_ipv4 tunnel':       'true' 'ipv6_in_ipv4 tunnel':   'true' 'ipv6_in_ipv6 tunnel':   'true' 'loopback':              'true' 'system':              'true' 'lag':                 'true' 'vxlan':                'false' 'ubt':                  'false'

selftest_disable.description: Specify *true* to disable and *false* to enable  for the respective interface

ssm_map_acl.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
ACL to maintain group-source mapping for SSM group addresses. IGMPv1/IGMPv2/MLDv1 join and leave packets destined to SSM group address in the SSM map will be converted to (source, group) channels, for all the sources part of respective SSM map.

static_ip6_addresses.description:
Reference Resource: [IP6_Address](#/IP6_Address)
Stores the statically configured IPv6 addresses and prefixes.

stp_config.description: This represents information regarding stp port level configuration.

admin_edge_port_enable.description: The port should not be participating in root election if this value is 'true'

admin_path_cost.description: The path cost for the port to reach spanning-tree root.

bpdu_filter_enable.description: When set to 'true', the port will stop sending and receiving IEEE STP BPDUs.

bpdu_guard_enable.description: The port shuts down if it receives a STP BPDU if this value is 'true'

bpdus_rx_disable.description: The port stops reception of STP BPDUs if this value is 'true'

bpdus_tx_disable.description: The port will not transmit the STP BPDUs if this value is 'true'

link_type.description: Set connected link type. 'point-to-point' treat the port as if it were one end of a point-to-point connection on the network segment. 'shared' treat the port as if it were a node on a shared network segment. 'auto' automatically determine the status of the port on the network segment.

loop_guard_enable.description: The port stops sending and receiving BPDUs if this value is 'true'

port_priority.description: The priority of the port in multiples of 16.

protocol_migration_disable.description: This is protocol migration control on this port When the STP BPDU received on this port the switch migrate to STP mode If this value is 'true'.

restricted_port_role_disable.description: The port will not be selected as Root Port for any instance if this value is 'true'

restricted_port_tcn_disable.description: The port will not propagate topology changes to other ports if this value is 'true'

root_guard_enable.description: The device participate in STP as long as the device does not try to become the root if this value is 'true'

rpvst_filter_enable.description: When set to 'true', the port will stop sending and receiving RPVST BPDUs.

rpvst_guard_enable.description: When set to 'true', the port will shut down upon receiving an RPVST BPDU.

subintf_vlan.description: Specifies VLAN ID for the subinterface. This VLAN ID is used to send and receive 802.1Q tagged packets on a subinterface. Without an associated VLAN ID, a subinterface will remain in down state.

threshold_profile.description:
Reference Resource: [Threshold_Profile](#/Threshold_Profile)
Specifies the threshold-profile name for this port. If it is unspecified, the name (if present) of the threshold_profile_default column in [System](#/System) table will be used.

udld_enable.description: UDLD protocol is enabled or not on this interface.

udld_hpe_anw_compatibility_mode.description: Configured UDLD operation mode for HPE ANW. In `verify_then_forward` the interface starts out blocked and will not forward traffic until UDLD determines that the interface is bidirectional. With `forward_then_verify` the interface starts out unblocked.

udld_interval.description: The time interval in milliseconds to send UDLD packets.  If 'udld_compatibility' value is 'rfc5171' and time interval is below valid range for RFC 5171 (7000 - 90000), then it will be forced to 7000.

udld_retries.description: Number of retries before changing the UDLD interface status to `block`.

udld_rfc5171_compatibility_mode.description: Configured UDLD operation mode for RFC5171. In `normal` mode, once the link is determined to be in unidirectional state (after it was deemed bidireccional), and no "Echo" is received, it is set to "undetermined" state. However, if a a UDLD packet with an empty "Echo" is received the interface will be set to "errDisabled". In `aggressive` , once a link is determined to be in unidirectional state (after it was deemed bidirectional), and no "Echo" is received, it is set to "errDisabled" state. The interface will also be set to "errDisabled" if a UDLD packet with an empty "Echo" is received.

unnumbered.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
Enables IP-unnumbered support for this port. Once set, this port will borrow the user-configured 'primary' IPv4 address from an 'owner' interface and use in its L3 control plane exchange. This is only applicable when the borrowing interface is a routed port or a layer-3 LAG.

urpf_check.description: Mode of unicast reverse path forwarding verification: 'loose':   drop packets that are destined to the device itself and that have source IP that is not reachable. 'strict':  drop packets that are destined to the device and that have source IP that is not reachable through the interface that the packet arrived on. 'disable': no reverse path verification.

user_config.description: Key-value pairs that stores the user configuration of [Interface](#/Interface).

admin.description: The user-configured administrative state of Interface. If not configured, the default behavior depends on the 'type': 'vlan':                  'up' 'gre_ipv4 tunnel':       'down' 'ipv6_in_ipv4 tunnel':   'down' 'ipv6_in_ipv6 tunnel':   'down' 'loopback':              'up' 'system':              'down' 'vxlan':               'down' 'ubt':                 'down'

autoneg.description: The user-configured autonegotiation state of [Interface](Interface). The possible values are "on" and "off".

duplex.description: The user-configured duplex mode of [Interface](Interface). The possible values are "half" and "full".

error_control.description: The Ethernet error control, a.k.a Forward Error Correction (FEC), mode  to use for this interface. When set, this overrides the mode that would  normally be used based on the installed transceiver. When not set, the  standard mode for the installed transceiver is used.   'auto'      : use the transceiver default  'none'      : do not use any FEC  'base-r-fec': use IEEE BASE-R (Firecode) FEC  'rs-fec'    : use IEEE Reed-Solomon FEC

interpacket_gap.description: The gap between packets transmitted by this interface. This  setting only applies to interfaces that have the  `interpacket_gap_config` capability.   'default'     : use the system default gap  'high-average': use a higher average gap

lane_split.description: The user-configured split mode of the interface. This is only  applicable to multi-lane ports such as QSFP where each lane  can be used as a separate interface. When set to `split` the  parent interface is split and the `split_children` interfaces  can be enabled. All other values are treated as `no-split`.

leader_follower.description: For interfaces that support configurable leader-follower mode,  this is the configured mode.  'preferred-leader'  : advertise preference to be the leader  'preferred-follower': advertise preference to be the follower  'forced-leader'     : force the interface to be the leader  'forced-follower'   : force the interface to be the follower

link_clock_tolerance.description: For interfaces that support configurable link clock tolerance,  this is the mode to use.  'wide'  : use the widest tolerance setting available  'narrow': use the narrowest tolerance setting available

link_state_snmp_if_mib_trap.description: Enable the transmission of SNMP IF-MIB traps for link  state changes on this interface. Used to toggle  ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable to true or false.

link_state_snmp_trap.description: Enable the transmission of SNMP traps for link state changes on this interface.

pause.description: The user-configured Ethernet PAUSE (link-level flow control)  mode of [Interface](Interface). The possible values are  "none", "rx", "tx", "rxtx", and "pfc".

pause_override.description: When set, always use the configured pause mode and ignore the results of  autonegotiation with the link partner.

speeds.description: The list of user-configured interface speeds in megabits per second. When autonegotiation is disabled, the largest value in the list is applied.

split_count.description: When `lane_split` is `split`, this is the number of child  interfaces to activate. When not specified, the default is  4. This setting is ignored when the interface is not split.

split_speed.description: When `lane_split` is `split`, this is the preferred speed for  the child interfaces in megabits per second. When not  specified, the highest available speed is used. This setting  is ignored when the interface is not split.

system_lanes.description: The total number of SerDes lanes used by the installed  transceiver to communicate with the system. This setting only  applies to multi-lane port types such as QSFP-DD where a  transceiver may be installed that uses fewer lanes than the  port provides. It is ignored for other port types and for  split child ports. When not specified, the lane count defaults  to a value based on the port speed and maximum number of lanes  supported by the port.

virtual_gw_l3_src_mac_enable.description: Enables the interface to use the virtual gateway MAC address as the source MAC for routed traffic. This is only applicable for SVI interfaces.

virtual_ip4_routers.description:
Reference Resource: [VRRP](#/VRRP)
The port's VRRP groups (or VR instances) for IPv4 address family. A maximum of `32` VRRP groups can be assigned to a port.

virtual_ip6_routers.description:
Reference Resource: [VRRP](#/VRRP)
The port's VRRP groups (or VR instances) for IPv6 address family. A maximum of `32` VRRP groups can be assigned to a port.

vlan_mode.description: VLAN mode for ports with 'routing' being 'false'. For those ports, it has to be set, otherwise the port will be held down. When vlan_mode is not set, it indicates that the port is in access mode.  `access`: Port can carry traffic for only one VLAN and the VLAN            is specified as part of vlan_tag. Packets ingressing            and egressing this port will not have an 802.1Q VLAN tag.  When the port is trunked, mode must be either native-tagged or native-untagged, value contained in vlan_trunks refers to the list of VLANs which have to be trunked, if it is empty then all VLANs have to be trunked.  `native-tagged`:    Port can carry traffic for multiple VLANs.                      One of the VLANs is designated as native                      and is specified as part of vlan_tag.                      Traffic for all VLANs on this port                      including the native VLAN will be 802.1Q                      VLAN tagged.  `native-untagged`:  Port can carry traffic for multiple VLANs.                      One of the VLANs is designated as native                      and the VLAN ID is specified as part of                      vlan_tag. Traffic for all VLANs except the                      native VLAN will be 802.1Q VLAN tagged                      Traffic for the native VLAN will not have                      an 802.1Q tag.

vlan_tag.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
Specifies the Access or Native VLAN for this port. When vlan_tag is not set, it indicates that VLAN-1 is the Access or Native VLAN. For a non-SVI, 'routing' interface, the value must be kept empty. For SVI, the value must reference the VLAN of the SVI.

vlan_trunks.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
List of VLANs that this port is allowed to pass traffic for. When the list is empty, it means that the port will be allowed to pass traffic for all VLANs configured on the device. This is only relevant if 'vlan_mode' is 'native-tagged' or 'native-untagged' and ignored for 'access'. 'native-tagged' or 'native-untagged' port always trunks its native ('vlan_tag') VLAN, regardless of whether it's included in 'vlan_trunks'.

vlans_per_protocol.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
The list of protocol VLANs configured on the port.

vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
Indicates the VRF to which the port belongs if the port is routing. If not configured and if the port is routing, the port belongs to 'default' vrf.

vsx_active_forwarding_enable.description: Determines whether this port has VSX active-forwarding enabled or not.  This should be set on Upstream SVIs only and not on downstream SVIs  that have active-gateway enabled.

vsx_linkup_delay_timer_disable.description: A value of 'true' disables vsx linkup delay timer for this port.

vsx_shutdown_on_split.description: Determines whether the port will be shutdown when VSX split occurs. This is only applicable to the ports that are not configured as MCLAG   and SVIs that do not have any MCLAGs as members.

vsx_sync.description: Controls which attributes should be synchronized between VSX peers. '^acl.*'        : all attributes that control the association with the ACLs will be synchronized. '.irdp.*'       : all attributes that control the IRDP will be synchronized. '^qos.*'        : all attributes that control the Quality of Service will be synchronized. 'rate_limits'   : all attributes that control rate-limits will be synchronized. '^vlan.*'       : all attributes that control the association with the VLANs will be synchronized. '^vsx_virtual.*': all attributes that control the association with the VSX active-gateways will be synchronized. 'virtual_gw_l3_src_mac_enable': attribute that controls the active-gateways l3 source MAC will be synchronized '^policy.*'     : all attributes that control the association with the Policies will be synchronized. 'portfilter'    : attribute that controls static portfiltering will be synchronized. 'client_ip_track_configuration' : attribute that controls the client track ip will be synchronized. 'device_fingerprint_configuration' : attribute controls device fingerprinting will be synchronized. 'mgmd_acl' : Attribute that associates ACL with IGMP/MLD will be synchroized. 'mgmd_enable' : Attribute that controls the multicast IGMP/MLD will be synchroized. 'mgmd_robustness' : Attribute that controls number of retries for query will be synchronized. 'mgmd_querier_max_response_time' : Attribute that controls time interval for response of IGMP/MLD query will be synchronized. 'mgmd_mld_version' : Attribute that controls mld version will be synchronized. 'mgmd_querier_interval' : Attribute that controls interval between IGMP/MLD queries will be synchronized. 'mgmd_last_member_query_interval' : Attributes that control time interval that querier waits to receive response will be synchronized. 'mgmd_querier_enable' : Attribute that controls querier enable/disable will be synchronized. 'mgmd_mld_static_groups' : Attribute that controls list of static MLD groups will be synchronized. 'mgmd_igmp_static_groups' : Attribute that controls list of static IGMP groups will be synchronized. 'mgmd_igmp_version' : Attribute that controls IGMP L3 Interface Version will be synchronized. 'mgmd_querier_wait_timer' : Attribute that controls wait time before querier role will be synchronized. 'macsec_policy' : Attribute that controls the MACsec policy association to a port will be synchronized. 'mka_policy'    : Attribute that controls the MKA policy association to a port will be synchronized. 'pvlan_port_type' : Attribute that specifies the port's type in pvlan context will be synchronized. 'pim_mode' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM will be synchroized. 'pim_trig_hello_interval' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM hello delay will be synchroized. 'pim_hello_interval' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM hello interval will be synchroized. 'pim_lan_prune_delay_disable' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM lan prune delay will be synchroized. 'pim_override_interval' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM override interval will be synchroized. 'pim_propagation_delay' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM propagation delay will be synchroized. 'pim_vsx_virtual_neighbor' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM vsx virtual neighbor will be synchroized. 'pim_source_address': Attribute that controls the multicast PIM source ip will be synchroized. 'pim_bfd' : Attribute that controls the multicast PIM bfd will be synchroized. 'dhcp-snooping' : Attribute that controls the dhcp-snooping on a port will be synchronized. 'pim_bsr_boundary' : Attribute that controls PIM Bootstrap messages on boundary interface 'multicast_boundary_acl_in' : Attribute that controls Ingress multicast boundary as per ACL 'multicast_boundary_acl_out' : Attribute that controls Egress multicast boundary as per ACL 'ssm_map_acl' : Attribute that associates ssm-map ACL with IGMP/MLD will be synchroized.

vsx_virtual_gw_mac_v4.description: VSX virtual gateway MAC address for the corresponding virtual gateway IPv4 addresses. If virtual gateway MAC is not configured, then device system MAC will be used as the gateway MAC.

vsx_virtual_gw_mac_v6.description: VSX virtual gateway MAC address for the corresponding virtual gateway IPv6 addresses. If virtual gateway MAC is not configured, then device system MAC will be used as the gateway MAC.

vsx_virtual_ip4.description: List of active gateway IPv4 addresses.

vsx_virtual_ip6.description: List of active gateway IPv6 addresses.

parameters.name: Interface.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [Interface](#/Interface)
The interface name. For non-bonded ports, the interface name is the same as the associated port name. The name must otherwise be unique across all ports and interfaces of the system.

aaa_auth_precedence.description: Precedence order for Port Access Authentication:  `dot1x`:   IEEE 802.1X Authentication Protocol   `mac-auth`: MAC Authentication Protocol. If empty, the default precedence order of dot1x followed by  mac-auth will be used.

aaa_auth_priority.description: Priority order for Port Access Authentication:  `dot1x`:   IEEE 802.1X Authentication Protocol   `mac-auth`: MAC Authentication Protocol. If not set, priority will follow the 'aaa_auth_precedence' order.

aaa_port_access_cached_critical_role_dis.description: Disables caching authenticated clients and their associated role information. When not set, the globally configured port_access_cached_critical_role configuration will be used.

aaa_port_access_radius_override_enable.description: Enables RADIUS override support. With this enabled, RADIUS attributes received from server will override corresponding client role attributes.

aclmac_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Ingress MAC ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this port, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclmac_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclmac_in_cfg' column. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclmac_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclmac_out_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Egress MAC ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this port, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclmac_out_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclmac_out_cfg' column. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclmac_out_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv4_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Ingress IPv4 ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this port, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv4_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv4_in_cfg' column. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv4_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv4_routed_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv4 ACL for routed ingress traffic, potentially in flight desired to be applied to this VLAN interface, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). This configuration is applicable only when the port is a VLAN interface. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv4_routed_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv4_routed_in_cfg' column. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv4_routed_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv4_routed_out_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv4 ACL for routed egress traffic, potentially in flight desired to be applied to this VLAN interface, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). This configuration is applicable only when the port is a VLAN interface. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv4_routed_out_cfg_version.description: The version of the currently configured routed egress IPv4 ACL that corresponds to this configuration version value. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the configured routed egress IPv4 ACL value.  An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv6_in_cfg.description:

Ingress IPv6 ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this port, as identified in the [ACL](#/ACL). An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.
