adv_router.description:
Reference Resource: [OSPFv3_LSA](#/OSPFv3_LSA)
The Router ID of the advertising router. The Router ID is in IPv4 address format.

dest_router.description: The Router ID of the destination router. This is in the IPv4 address format.

interface_name.description: Name of the interface to which the LSA belongs. This is applicable in case of Link LSA.

ls_birth_time.description: The OSPFv3 LSA birth time, number of seconds elapsed since Epoch, which can be used to compute LSA age.

ls_id.description:
Reference Resource: [OSPFv3_LSA](#/OSPFv3_LSA)
The OSPFv3 Link State ID.

ls_seq_num.description: The sequence number of the LSA.

lsa_prefix.description: The IPv6 prefix to which this LSA belongs. This is applicable in case of Inter Area Prefix LSA, External LSA and NSSA External LSA.

lsa_type.description:
Reference Resource: [OSPFv3_LSA](#/OSPFv3_LSA)
The type of the OSPFv3 LSA.

num_network_links.description: Total number of network links. This is applicable in case of Network LSA.

num_router_links.description: Total number of router links. This is applicable in case of Router LSA.

ospf_area.description:
Reference Resource: [OSPFv3_LSA](#/OSPFv3_LSA)
Area to which the LSA belongs.

ospf_router.description:
Reference Resource: [OSPFv3_LSA](#/OSPFv3_LSA)
OSPFv3 Router to which the LSA belongs.

ref_ls_id.description: The OSPFv3 Link State ID to which this particular link is referring to. This is applicable in case of Intra Area Prefix LSA. This referrered LSA Id should refer to existing LSA Id of Router LSA or Network LSA.

ref_ls_type.description: The OSPFv3 Link State type to which this particular link is referring to. This is applicable in case of Intra Area Prefix LSA. The referred Link State type should be Router LSA or Network LSA.

router_lsa_bits.description: The Router LSA Bits denotes different flags set for this particular Router LSA. These flags could be: Bit V: the router is an endpoint of one or more fully adjacent virtual links. Bit E: the router is an AS boundary router. Bit B: the router is an area border router. Bit x :The bit is unused should be set to 0. Bit Nt: the router is an NSSA border router.

active_active.description: Enables PIM active-active feature on the PIM router which is part of VSX pair. If the value is true, then the VSX peer which is not forwarding the multicast traffic, acts as proxy-DR and learns multicast routes. The multicast routes in proxy-DR would be written as bridge entries in the hardware. If the value is false, then PIM active-active feature would be turned off. In this case, if the VSX peer which is forwarding the multicast stream goes down, other peer would send joins only after the neighbor expiry. So it takes time to resume multicast traffic.

anycast_rp_source_directly_connected.description: To allow same multicast source to be directly connected to two or more Anycast RP routers. This is optional when the source is directly connected to a single Anycast RP or when the source is at least one hop away from the RP.

bfd_all_interfaces_enable.description: Enables BFD on all PIM interfaces.

bidir_software_routing.description: Indicates if multicast data packets need to be routed in software by BIDIr  until flows are programmed in hardware.

bsm_last_received_time.description: The epoch time at which the last BSM is received on this router.

bsr_elected_time.description: The epoch time at which the E-BSR is elected as known by this router.

bst_last_expired_time.description: The epoch time at which the Bootstrap Timer last expired on this router.

candidate_bsr_bsm_interval.description: Periodic interval(in seconds) at which the BSMs are originated from this router.

candidate_bsr_hash_mask_length.description: Candidate-BSR's hash mask length on this router. If this is not set, then default value 30 is used for IPv4 PIM-SM and default value 126 for IPv6 PIM-SM.

candidate_bsr_port.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
Candidate Bootstrap Router (Candidate-BSR) port on this router. Candidate-BSR [Port](#/Port) must be specified to enable BSR operations. IP address of this port will be advertised as the Candidate-BSR address. If this is not set, then Candidate-BSR will not be operational.

candidate_rp_adv_interval.description: Periodic interval(in seconds) at which the Candidate-RP advertisements are originated from this router.

candidate_rp_group_prefix.description: Multicast group prefix associated with this Candidate-RP. The entries are valid only when [candidate_rp_port](#/PIM_Router) is configured. An empty value with a valid Candidate-RP port in [candidate_rp_port](#/PIM_Router) means that this Candidate-RP is handling all the possible multicast groups. This entries will take the format IP-ADDR/MASK-LEN.

candidate_rp_holdtime.description: Candidate-RP's Holdtime (in seconds) on this router.

candidate_rp_port.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
Candidate Rendezvous Point (Candidate-RP) port on this router. Candidate-RP [Port](#/Port) must be specified to enable Candidate-RP operations. If this is not set, then Candidate-RP will not be operational.

clear_mroute_request.description:
Reference Resource: [PIM_Clear_Mroute_Request](#/PIM_Clear_Mroute_Request)
List of clear requests associated with Multicast route entries.

delayed_dr_interval.description: Delay (in seconds) before the router advertises the DR priority.

elected_bsr_address.description: IP Address of the elected BSR on this router.

elected_bsr_hash_mask_length.description: Hash mask length of the elected BSR on this router.

elected_bsr_priority.description: Priority of the elected BSR on this router.

ip_version.description:
Reference Resource: [PIM_Router](#/PIM_Router)
PIM router entries keyed by IP version. This can have one [PIM_Router](#/PIM_Router) entry per IP version. If this is not set, then PIM will be disabled on this VRF.

ivrl_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
List of VRFs on which the Multicast Source is present. Multicast traffic from these list of VRFs will be leaked to the VRF on which the receivers are present.

join_prune_interval.description: Frequency (in seconds) at which this router sends PIM Join/Prune messages.

mroutes_limit.description: Limit on the maximum number of multicast route entries that can be programmed. If this is not set, then the limit specified in the system capacities will be honored. When the limit is configured, multicast route entries created because of IGMP or MLD membership reports and multicast route entries created because of multicast streams are restricted under the configured limit.

pim_static_rps.description:
Reference Resource: [PIM_Static_RP](#/PIM_Static_RP)
Static RPs for the specified multicast prefixes expressed as (IP-ADDR/MASK-LEN) and [PIM_Static_RP](#/PIM_Static_RP) entry. There can exist only one RP address for a unique group prefix.

redistribute_static_mroute.description: If redistributing static multicast route to PIM is enabled, the static multicast routes configured are sent as PIM joins to the upstream connected PIM router.

register_acl.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Ingress ACL to filter processing of PIM register messages received from peer devices. When this is not configured, all PIM register messages will be processed.

register_messages_limit.description: Limit on the maximum number of register messages sent per second for every unique (S,G) entry. If this is not set, then there is no maximum rate set. When the limit is configured, register messages generated exceeding the configured limit will be suppressed.

router_enable.description: Enables PIM protocol on this router.

rp_group_acls.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Ingress ACL to filter PIM join and prune messages received from peer devices based on the RP address and its associated (S, G) information specified in those messages. When this is not configured, all PIM join and prune messages will be processed.

rpf_override.description:
Reference Resource: [Static_Multicast_Nexthop](#/Static_Multicast_Nexthop)
Overrides normal RPF lookup mechanism for multicast routes matching ip_prefix IP-ADDR/MASK-LEN with the gateway ip/port

sources_per_group.description: Total number of sources allowed for a group on this router. If this is not set, then there is no limit on the number of sources for a group. When the number of sources for a group exceeds the configured limit multicast traffic from additional sources will be dropped.

spt_threshold_disable.description: Enables Shortest Path Tree(SPT) switching on this router.

ssm_enable.description: Enables PIM SSM protocol on this router.

ssm_range_acl.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
ACL to indicate the SSM range. If this is not configured, default SSM range will be used.

state_refresh.description: Periodic interval (in seconds) at which state refresh datagrams are  transmitted by this router. This is applicable when PIM mode is set to 'dense'.

static_rp_acls.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
ACL to filter the group addresses for this RP Address. On the source DR, only group addresses which are permitted will be registered to RP. When applied on other routers, PIM (*,G) join and prune messages will be filtered.

PEM_certificate.description: Installed certificate or generated CSR in PEM format.

common_name.description: Common name for the subject of the certificate.  Default value is the device serial number.

country.description: Country name for the subject of the certificate.  ISO Alpha-2 country code is expected, but we only enforce  it to be two letters both uppercase, do not enforce its  correctness, which is users' responsibility. It can be empty  when it is not configured.

est_profile.description:
Reference Resource: [PKI_EST_Profile](#/PKI_EST_Profile)
The EST profile that enrolled this certificate, if applicable. This field should be null (not set) if this certificate is not enrolled from an EST service.

est_status.description: EST processing status: 'not_applicable':          certificate is not enrolled by EST                            service. 'enroll_reenroll_success': certificate was successfully                            enrolled or reenrolled through EST                            service, is valid and in normal use. 'enroll_pending':          user requested EST enrollment and                            CSR has been created. 'reenroll_pending':        certificate has been in re-enrollment                            lead time, waiting for re-enrollment.                            The current certificate is still                            valid and in normal use. 'enroll_waiting_retry':    EST enrollment failed and waiting                            to retry. 'reenroll_waiting_retry':  EST re-enrollment failed and                            waiting to retry. The current                            certificate is still valid and                            in normal use. 'enroll_reenroll_failed':  EST enrollment or re-enrollment                            failed and retry count also ran                            out. Certificate status should be                            expires_soon, expired or csr_pending.                            Note that when the status is                            expires_soon, the certificate will                            continue to be used by associated                            applications; if status is expired,                            associated applications will turn to                            use local-cert instead.

clientAuth.description: Indicate whether the public key of the certificate can be  used for TLS WWW client authentication purpose. Key usage  may be digitalSignature and/or keyAgreement.

serverAuth.description: Indicate whether the public key of the certificate can be  used for TLS WWW server authentication purpose. Key usage  may be digitalSignature, keyEncipherment or keyAgreement.

file_status.description: CSR or certificate file status: 'nonexistent':  CSR or certificate file doe not exist 'installed':    CSR or certificate file is installed 'mismatch_subject': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but some subject field(s) of the certificate in                  file is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired subject values. 'mismatch_keyusage': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but key usage field of the certificate in                  file is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired key usage values. 'mismatch_xkusage': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but extended key usage field of the certificate                  in file is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired extended key                  usage values. 'mismatch_san': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but subject alternative name field of the                  certificate in file is different from the user                  configuration. It is still valid and usable if                  certificate status is 'installed', but user may                  want to update the configuration or re-enroll                  the certificate with the desired                  subject alternative name value. 'mismatch_keytype': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but the key type of the certificate in file                  is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired key type. 'mismatch_keysize': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but the key size of the certificate in file                  is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired key size.

key_type.description: key-type:  'RSA-2048':   RSA keypair with key size to be 2048 bits 'RSA-3072':   RSA keypair with key size to be 3072 bits 'RSA-4096':   RSA keypair with key size to be 4096 bits 'ECDSA-256':  ECDSA keypair with curve size to be 256 bits 'ECDSA-384':  ECDSA keypair with curve size to be 384 bits 'ECDSA-521':  ECDSA keypair with curve size to be 521 bits

dataEncipherment.description: Indicate whether the public key in certificate can be  used for encrypting data other than cryptographic keys.

digitalSignature.description: Indicate whether the public key in certificate can be  used to validate digital signature for entity  authentication or data origin authentication, but not  certificate signing, CRL signing, or non-repudiation.

keyAgreement.description: Indicate whether the public key in certificate can be  used to encrypt and decrypt keys between the sender and  receiver.

keyEncipherment.description: Indicate whether the public key in certificate can be  used with a protocol that encrypts keys.

keyRestriction.description: Indicate how the public key in certificate is used in a  keyAgreement protocol. This value is ignored if          keyAgreement value is not true;                          otherwise it can take one of these values:                 unrestricted: no restriction to encipher or decipher;    encipherOnly: key is used for encipher only;    decipherOnly: key is used for decipher only.

nonRepudiation.description: Indicate whether the public key in certificate can be  used to validate digital signature to provide a  non-repudiation service.

locality.description: Locality name for the subject of the certificate.  It can be empty when it is not configured.

name.description:
Reference Resource: [PKI_X509_Certificate](#/PKI_X509_Certificate)
Certificate name.

org.description: Organization name for the subject of the certificate.  It can be empty when it is not configured.

org_unit.description: Organization unit name for the subject of the certificate.  It can be empty when it is not configured.

origin.description: Indicator of whether the cert is built-in (system-created) or user-configured. Unlike user-configured certs,  built-in certs cannot be modified or deleted.

san_dnsname.description: A dNSName type of entry (or entries) for subject alternative  name of the certificate. A dNSName is a domain name system  label in the preferred name syntax as specified by Section  3.5 of RFC 1034 and modified by Section 2.1 of RFC 1123.  Subject alternative name is a X509 certificate extension  specified in RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.6.

san_ip.description: An ipAddress type of entry (or entries) for subject alternative  name of the certificate. It supports both IPv4 and IPv6  addresses. Subject alternative name is a X509 certificate  extension specified in RFC 5280 Section 4.2.1.6.

state_or_province.description: State or province name for the subject of the certificate.  It can be empty when it is not configured.

status.description: Certificate status: 'installed':     certificate can be associated with an                   application. 'csr_pending':   a CSR has been generated, but the signed cert                   has not yet been installed. 'malformed':     certificate is malformed. 'expired':       certificate is expired. 'expires_soon':  certificate will be expiring within 60 days. 'not_installed': certificate has just been created and is                   still pending status check.

est_profile.description:
Reference Resource: [PKI_EST_Profile](#/PKI_EST_Profile)
The EST profile that enrolled this certificate, if applicable. This field should be null (not set) if this certificate is not enrolled from an EST service.

est_status.description: EST processing status: 'not_applicable':          certificate is not enrolled by EST                            service. 'enroll_reenroll_success': certificate was successfully                            enrolled or reenrolled through EST                            service, is valid and in normal use. 'enroll_pending':          user requested EST enrollment and                            CSR has been created. 'reenroll_pending':        certificate has been in re-enrollment                            lead time, waiting for re-enrollment.                            The current certificate is still                            valid and in normal use. 'enroll_waiting_retry':    EST enrollment failed and waiting                            to retry. 'reenroll_waiting_retry':  EST re-enrollment failed and                            waiting to retry. The current                            certificate is still valid and                            in normal use. 'enroll_reenroll_failed':  EST enrollment or re-enrollment                            failed and retry count also ran                            out. Certificate status should be                            expires_soon, expired or csr_pending.                            Note that when the status is                            expires_soon, the certificate will                            continue to be used by associated                            applications; if status is expired,                            associated applications will turn to                            use local-cert instead.

clientAuth.description: Indicate whether the public key of the certificate can be  used for TLS WWW client authentication purpose. Key usage  may be digitalSignature and/or keyAgreement.

serverAuth.description: Indicate whether the public key of the certificate can be  used for TLS WWW server authentication purpose. Key usage  may be digitalSignature, keyEncipherment or keyAgreement.

file_status.description: CSR or certificate file status: 'nonexistent':  CSR or certificate file doe not exist 'installed':    CSR or certificate file is installed 'mismatch_subject': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but some subject field(s) of the certificate in                  file is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired subject values. 'mismatch_keyusage': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but key usage field of the certificate in                  file is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired key usage values. 'mismatch_xkusage': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but extended key usage field of the certificate                  in file is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired extended key                  usage values. 'mismatch_san': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but subject alternative name field of the                  certificate in file is different from the user                  configuration. It is still valid and usable if                  certificate status is 'installed', but user may                  want to update the configuration or re-enroll                  the certificate with the desired                  subject alternative name value. 'mismatch_keytype': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but the key type of the certificate in file                  is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired key type. 'mismatch_keysize': CSR or certificate file is installed,                  but the key size of the certificate in file                  is different from the user configuration.                  It is still valid and usable if certificate                  status is 'installed', but user may want to                  update the configuration or re-enroll the                  certificate with the desired key size.

properties.description:
Reference Resource: [PoE_Interface](#/PoE_Interface)
Reference to the [PoE interface](#/PoE_Interface) associated with this [Interface](#/Interface).

config.description: All PoE configuration made at a per-[Interface](#/Interface) level are listed here as a series of key-value pairs.

admin_disable.description: Configurable flag to control PoE power delivery on this [Interface](Interface). A value of `true` would disable PoE power delivery on this [Interface](Interface). By default, the flag is set to `false` for all PoE capable [Interfaces](Interface), i.e., PoE is enabled.

allocate_by_method.description: Allows control over the power allocation strategy used for this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface). Two power allocation strategies are supported: `class` and `usage`. When allocating by `usage`, power is delivered as requested by a PD. When allocating by `class`, the PSE uses the power ramp-up signature of the PD to identify the PD's power class, and use the power level for the specified class.

cfg_assigned_class.description: Allows the user to limit the power delivered to a PD connected on this [Interface](Interface). If configured, the power delivered to a PD would be restricted to the limit of the configured class, rather than the class advertised by the PD itself. Possible values are: 'class3': PD would be limited to 13W 'class4': PD would be limited to 25.5W

cfg_power_pairs.description: Allows the user to limit power delivery for Single signature PDs of classes 4 and  below to ALT-A only on this interface  'alt-a': Power delivery should be limited ALT-A only 'alt-a-and-alt-b': Power delivery should be allowed on ALT-A and ALT-B both These are only applicable for single signature PDs of class 4 and below.

pd_class_override.description: A configurable flag to control PoE class override on this  [Interface](Interface). When set to 'true' the switch will  ignore the PD class advertised by the device and allow it  to draw more power.  Warning: Allowing a device to exceed its advertised limit  could result in a non-compliant device drawing more power  than it is designed to handle and possibly cause damage to  the device.  Warning: allocate_by_method should be set to 'class' when  override is enabled to prevent the device from drawing  unlimited power. Failure to do so could exceed the total  power capacity of the switch and cause it to reboot.  'true': Ignore the PD class advertised by the device. 'false': Use the PD class advertised by the device.  The default value is `false`.

pre_standard_detect.description: Some PoE powered devices hit the market before the PoE 802.3af standard was ratified. These devices are technically non-compliant with the standard, but we do have the capability to detect these devices and supply power to them. This capability needs to be enabled individually on each [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface). This boolean value specifies the pre-standard detect configuration on this interface.  'true':  Pre-802.3af-standard devices are detected and powered. 'false': Only 802.3af compliant devices are powered.  The default value is `false`.

priority.description: If a power-sourcing equipment (PSE) can supply power to all connected powered devices (PD), the priority configuration is unused. The priority configuration comes into play when there is more power requested by PDs than available on the PSE. In such a scenario, power allocation is prioritized to [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface) that have a higher priority. This can potentially cause loss of power on one or more lower-priority [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface) to meet the power demand on other higher-priority [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface). This operation occurs regardless of the order in which PDs connect to the PSE's [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface). Possible values:  'critical': Highest priority. 'high':     High priority. 'low':      Low priority  There are two ways in which PoE power is prioritized. In addition to the PoE priority configured here, a lower-numbered [Interface](Interface) has higher priority than a higher-numbered one.

effective_allocate_by_method.description: Arbitrated value of PoE power allocation method associated with this interface. When multiple sources request for an update to the interface's POE allocation method, the order of evaluation will be port_access assigned method followed by the user configured value of POE allocation method. The possible values are: 'class': Power is delivered based on PD's power class. 'usage': Power is delivered as requested by PD.

effective_priority.description: Arbitrated value of PoE priority associated with this interface. When multiple sources request for an update to the interface's POE priority, the order of evaluation will be port_access assigned priority followed by LLDP MED priority and then the user configured value of POE priority. The possible values are: 'critical': Highest priority. 'high':     High priority. 'low':      Low priority.

measurements.description: Power measurements made at this [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface).

average_power.description: This field specifies the average power, in Watts drawn by the powered device (PD) on this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface).

current.description: Numeric value indicating the current, in amperes (A), supplied at this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface).

peak_power.description: This field specifies the peak power supplied, in Watts, to the powered device (PD) connected to this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface).

power_drawn.description: Numeric value indicating the actual power, in Watts, drawn by the powered device (PD) on this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface). This field is not valid when powering_status is absent.

voltage.description: Numeric value indicating the Voltage supplied at this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface). This value is specified in volts (V).

pd_information.description: Powered device (PD) specific information for PD connected at this [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface). If the PD is either a 2-pair compliant device, or is a single-signature device, PD information is specified with key `port`. If the PD is a 4-pair dual signature compliant device, the PD information is specified independently for each pair with keys of `pair-a` and `pair-b`.

power_classification.description: Indicates the class detected on the PD connected to this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface).  The powered device (PD) is classified based on a combination of physical layer classification (PLC) and data layer classification (DLC), the latter of which is done through LLDP protocol.  The result of the classification process indicates the power limits that the PD is capable of drawing. When the power allocation mode is set to 'allocate by class', the classification is used to set the limits for the power that can be drawn by the PD. The limits, in Watts, are:               PSE     PD 'class 0':    15.4    13 'class 1':    4       3.84 'class 2':    7       6.49 'class 3':    15.4    13 'class 4':    30      25.5 'class 5':    45      35.5 'class 6':    60      51 'class 7':    75      60 'class 8':    90      71  For single-signature devices, the power_classification will be specified with the key of `port`. For dual-signature power devices, the power_classification will be specified independently for each pair, with keys of `pair-a` and `pair-b`.

pd_signature.description: In 802.3af and 802.3at standards, the power controller on the PSE uses two of the four pairs of wires in the RJ45 connector to supply power to a power controller on the PD. With 802.3bt standard, the controller on the PSE uses all four pairs. On the PD side, there can either be single power controller, or two distinct power controllers connected to each of the two pairs, and each of the two controllers would negotiate and draw power independently from the PSE.  The Controller on the PSE is capable of detecting the PD signature, which will indicate whether the PD comprises a single controller, or two independent controllers. Possible values:  not set : 2-pair mode 'single': 4-pair mode, and one controller on the PD side 'dual':   4-pair mode, and two contollers on the PD side

pd_type.description: Indicates the powered device (PD) type detected on this port.  PDs are categorized into different types based on the PoE standard adhered to. The power supplied by the power sourcing equipment (PSE) shall typically be higher than the power requested at PD side to accommodate for line losses & as per standard, maximum of 100m cable is supported.  'Type1': 802.3af standard. PSE supplies up to 15.4W, and PD draws up to 13W 'Type2': 802.3at standard. PSE supplies up to 30W, and PD draws up to 25.5W 'Type3': 802.3bt standard. PSE supplies up to 60W, and PD draws up to 51W 'Type4': 802.3bt standard. PSE supplies up to 90W, and PD draws up to 71W  Type 2 and higher PDs support LLDP classification. If LLDP is enabled on PSE & a Type 2 PD is connected, PD is allowed to draw maximum power of 13W only. This is called Physical Layer Classification (PLC). Any further power needs to be negotiated through LLDP & this is called Data Link Layer Classification (DLC).

poe_cycle_timeout.description: Configurable timeout value in units of seconds to control PoE power delivery on this [Interface](#/Interface). This would disable PoE power delivery on this [Interface](#/Interface). Then after a timeout of the value, the PoE is enabled on this [Interface](#/Interface), i.e., PoE is disabled and enabled with a timeout.

poe_port_power_consumed_average.description: Specifies the average power in Watts consumed by the powered device (PD) on this [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) for a configured period of time.

port_access_allocate_by_method.description: Policy based assignment of PoE power allocation method. When set, this will override user configured 'config.allocate_by_method'. The possible values are: 'class': Power is delivered based on PD's power class. 'usage': Power is delivered as requested by PD.

port_access_priority.description: Policy based assignment of PoE priority. When set, this will override user configured 'config.priority': `critical`: Highest priority. `high`:     High priority. `low`:      Low priority

power_down.description: Power down related information on this [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface).

power_down_request_type.description: This indicates the current power down request of port. `poe_cycle`- PoE cycle requested `pd_power_down` - LLDP PD Power down requested.

request_timestamp.description: Specifies the time in seconds from Epoch when PSE has processed the power down request.

state.description: This indicates the current state of port in Power Down Request. `inactive`- Not in power down state. `request` - Power down requested. `active`  - Power down active `timeout` - Power down timeout. `remove`  - Power down remove.

timeout.description: Specifies the power down timeout request in seconds.

power_mgmt.description: Power management information, used to control the power delivery to the powered device (PD) which is connected on this `port` or pair.

cutoff_power.description: This is the quantum of power which will be used to calculate the over-current threshold on this `port`, or pair. The numeric value indicates the cutoff power in Watts.

pse_allocated_power.description: Numeric value indicating the power allocated, in Watts, to the PD on this [Poe Interface](PoE_Interface). This value is published to the PD via LLDP, indicating to the PD the quantum of power available to be drawn. This allows the PD to change its class based on the available power.

pse_assigned_class.description: Class demotion allows the PSE to allocate less than the PD requested power based on the PD requested power and PSE available power. This field indicates the actual class assigned by PSE to the PD. This information is published to the PD via the LLDP protocol. Depending on whether the PD is single or dual signature, the key used will be either `port`, or `pair-a`/`pair-b` respectively.

reserved_power.description: This is the quantum of power which has been reserved for the PD at this `port`, or pair, by the PSE. The numeric value is specified in Watts.

pre_std_device_status.description: This indicates the current status of pre-standard detection on the port. This is designed  to also accommodate any powered device which is powered through pre standard detect process. 'not_pre_std' :   The Powered device on [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) is not a pre-standard. 'pre_std'     :   The Powered device on [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) is a pre-standard. 'pwr_on_verif_fault_pd' :   The Powered device on [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) exhibited  power on verification fault initially, was then powered on through pre-standard detect process 'class_oc_pd' :   The Powered device on [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) exhibited class overcurrent and was then powered on through pre-standard detect.

rpd_status.description: Rapid Power Down is executed by the hardware in the event of a power-supply failure. It quickly cuts power to a PD to prevent an over-current scenario in the PSE. This field indicates whether the interface will go down in the event of any PSU failure or not. If this field is non-zero, it indicates that a power supply failure will cause the power delivery to be cut on supply failure. A value of zero indicates this [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) is unaffected by the failure of any single PSU.

self_test_status.description: The PoE subsystem runs self tests on the [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface) on boot. This field, when set, indicates the results of the self test.

statistics.description: PoE statistics information on the `port` or pair.

invalid_sig.description: Number of times the PSE detected a PD with an invalid signature.

mps_absent.description: Number of times a detected PD has skipped request for power.

overload.description: Number of times the PD attempted to draw more than the reserved power.

power_denied.description: Number of times the PD has been denied requested power due to insufficient available power.

short.description: Number of times the switch provided less than the requested power to the PD.

status.description: State of [PoE Interface](#/PoE_Interface). For single-signature devices, the state will be specified with the key of `port`. For dual-signature power devices, the state fields will be specified independently for each pair, with keys of `pair-a` and `pair-b`.

fault_reason.description: Fault status for the port, valid only if powering_status is `fault`.
enum: An external Supply FET has likely failed
UVLO3 Digital Supply Under Voltage Lockout (UVLO)
UVLO48 Analog Supply Under Voltage Lockout (UVLO)

powering_status.description: This indicates the current state of port in PoE state machine. 'disabled':   The admin_status of the [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface) is `false`. 'searching':  The [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface) is enabled, but no PD is connected yet. 'delivering': A PD is connected, and the PSE is supplying power. 'denied':     A PD is connected, but the PSE does not have sufficient power balance               to power this port. 'power_down': A PD is connected and it requested the PSE to disable power. 'fault':      A PD is connected, but the PSE detected a fault. 'absent':     Interface is not physically present or its not active interface.

config.description: All PoE configuration made at a per-[Interface](#/Interface) level are listed here as a series of key-value pairs.

admin_disable.description: Configurable flag to control PoE power delivery on this [Interface](Interface). A value of `true` would disable PoE power delivery on this [Interface](Interface). By default, the flag is set to `false` for all PoE capable [Interfaces](Interface), i.e., PoE is enabled.

allocate_by_method.description: Allows control over the power allocation strategy used for this [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface). Two power allocation strategies are supported: `class` and `usage`. When allocating by `usage`, power is delivered as requested by a PD. When allocating by `class`, the PSE uses the power ramp-up signature of the PD to identify the PD's power class, and use the power level for the specified class.

cfg_assigned_class.description: Allows the user to limit the power delivered to a PD connected on this [Interface](Interface). If configured, the power delivered to a PD would be restricted to the limit of the configured class, rather than the class advertised by the PD itself. Possible values are: 'class3': PD would be limited to 13W 'class4': PD would be limited to 25.5W

cfg_power_pairs.description: Allows the user to limit power delivery for Single signature PDs of classes 4 and  below to ALT-A only on this interface  'alt-a': Power delivery should be limited ALT-A only 'alt-a-and-alt-b': Power delivery should be allowed on ALT-A and ALT-B both These are only applicable for single signature PDs of class 4 and below.

pd_class_override.description: A configurable flag to control PoE class override on this  [Interface](Interface). When set to 'true' the switch will  ignore the PD class advertised by the device and allow it  to draw more power.  Warning: Allowing a device to exceed its advertised limit  could result in a non-compliant device drawing more power  than it is designed to handle and possibly cause damage to  the device.  Warning: allocate_by_method should be set to 'class' when  override is enabled to prevent the device from drawing  unlimited power. Failure to do so could exceed the total  power capacity of the switch and cause it to reboot.  'true': Ignore the PD class advertised by the device. 'false': Use the PD class advertised by the device.  The default value is `false`.

pre_standard_detect.description: Some PoE powered devices hit the market before the PoE 802.3af standard was ratified. These devices are technically non-compliant with the standard, but we do have the capability to detect these devices and supply power to them. This capability needs to be enabled individually on each [PoE Interface](PoE_Interface). This boolean value specifies the pre-standard detect configuration on this interface.  'true':  Pre-802.3af-standard devices are detected and powered. 'false': Only 802.3af compliant devices are powered.  The default value is `false`.

priority.description: If a power-sourcing equipment (PSE) can supply power to all connected powered devices (PD), the priority configuration is unused. The priority configuration comes into play when there is more power requested by PDs than available on the PSE. In such a scenario, power allocation is prioritized to [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface) that have a higher priority. This can potentially cause loss of power on one or more lower-priority [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface) to meet the power demand on other higher-priority [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface). This operation occurs regardless of the order in which PDs connect to the PSE's [PoE Interfaces](PoE_Interface). Possible values:  'critical': Highest priority. 'high':     High priority. 'low':      Low priority  There are two ways in which PoE power is prioritized. In addition to the PoE priority configured here, a lower-numbered [Interface](Interface) has higher priority than a higher-numbered one.

poe_cycle_timeout.description: Configurable timeout value in units of seconds to control PoE power delivery on this [Interface](#/Interface). This would disable PoE power delivery on this [Interface](#/Interface). Then after a timeout of the value, the PoE is enabled on this [Interface](#/Interface), i.e., PoE is disabled and enabled with a timeout.

Reference Resource: [Policy_Action_Set](#/Policy_Action_Set)

acl_drop.description: Drop packets matching the criteria specified in an associated class entry. If drop is specified, then all other actions will be ignored.

cbs.description: Set the Committed Burst Size for matching packets. Associated with cir An empty column value indicates that this action will not be taken on matched packets.

cir.description: Set the Committed Information Rate for matching packets. An empty column value indicates that this action will not be taken on matched packets.

authentication_method.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Auth_Configuration](#/Port_Access_Auth_Configuration)
Authentication method specific port-access configurations on this interface.

cached_reauth_enable.description: Enables cached re-authentication on this port.

cached_reauth_period.description: Time in seconds, during which cached re-authentication is allowed on the port.

canned_eap_success_enable.description: Allow the switch to send a canned EAP success packet to the supplicant to indicate a successful authentication when:  1. The authentication fails due to a RADIUS server reject, but the port on which the client on-boarded has a reject-role configured. 2. The authentication fails due to a RADIUS server timeout, but the port on which the client on-boarded has a critical-role configured.

discovery_period.description: Time period(in seconds) to wait before an EAPOL request identity frame re-transmission on an 802.1X enabled port with no authenticated client. Applicable for 802.1X only.

eapol_timeout.description: Time period(in seconds) to wait for a response from a client before retransmitting an EAPOL PDU. If the value is not set the time period is calculated as per RFC 2988. Applicable for 802.1X only.

initial_auth_response_timeout.description: Time period(in seconds) to wait for the first EAPoL frame from a client before deeming the client to be incapable of 802.1X and start authentication using the next configured authentication method, if any. Applicable for 802.1X only. If not set, the next configured authentication method is attempted only after the authentication cycle of the current method is complete.

macsec_enable.description: Enable MACsec via EAP for 802.1X authenticator.

max_requests.description: Number of EAPOL requests to supplicant before authentication fails. Applicable for 802.1X only.

max_retries.description: Number of authentication attempts before authentication fails.

mka_cak_length.description: The length (in bytes) of the Connectivity Association Key (CAK) to derive for EAP MACsec.  `16`: Generate a 16 byte CAK.  `32`: Generate a 32 byte CAK.

config.description: User configured persona enum limited to access - access port - default uplink - uplink port as defined in ports.yaml custom - user defined custom value

custom.description: Custom persona value that user can input when config is custom

mode.description: Persona mode: attach - Row config is applied and follows the config          of its persona copy   - Row config is applied once

quiet_period.description: Time period(in seconds) to wait before processing an authentication request from a client that failed authentication.

radius_server_group.description: RADIUS server group to use for authentication. When not set, the RADIUS server group configured for the authentication method at the system level is used.

reauth_enable.description: Enables periodic re-authentication on this port.

reauth_period.description: Time period(in seconds) to enforce periodic re-authentication of clients.

initial_auth_response_timeout.description: Time period(in seconds) to wait for the first EAPoL frame from a client before deeming the client to be incapable of 802.1X and start authentication using the next configured authentication method, if any. macsec_enable.description: Enable MACsec via EAP for 802.1X authenticator.

max_requests.description: Number of EAPOL requests to supplicant before authentication fails. Applicable for 802.1X only.

max_retries.description: Number of authentication attempts before authentication fails.

mka_cak_length.description: The length (in bytes) of the Connectivity Association Key (CAK) to derive for EAP MACsec.  `16`: Generate a 16 byte CAK.  `32`: Generate a 32 byte CAK.

config.description: User configured persona enum limited to access - access port - default uplink - uplink port as defined in ports.yaml custom - user defined custom value

custom.description: Custom persona value that user can input when config is custom

mode.description: Persona mode: attach - Row config is applied and follows the config          of its persona copy   - Row config is applied once

quiet_period.description: Time period(in seconds) to wait before processing an authentication request from a client that failed authentication.

radius_server_group.description: RADIUS server group to use for authentication. When not set, the RADIUS server group configured for the authentication method at the system level is used.

reauth_enable.description: Enables periodic re-authentication on this port.

auth_attributes.description: The RADIUS attributes cached for the client.  Outer key: the `attribute_id` is derived from a combination of            RADIUS attribute type and the vendor ID separated by a            `:`.            For standard attribute types, the vendor ID is 0.             Example: For standard attribute `Egress-VLAN-Name`            with type 58, attribute_id will be 58:0.            For vendor specific attributes from Aruba (Vendor-ID            14823) such as `aruba-user-role` and            `aruba-cppm-user-role` the attribute_id will be            26:14823.  Inner key: the `vendor_type_instance` is derived from a            combination of the vendor type associated with a            RADIUS attribute and the nth instance of the            attribute appearing in the same RADIUS message            separated by a `:`.            The value associated with this key is the value            received for that instance of the vendor type.            For standard attributes, the vendor_type is 0.             Example: For standard attribute `Egress-VLAN-Name`,            the first instance of this attribute in a RADIUS            message will have vendor_type_instance as 0:1, the            second instance (if exists) as 0:2 and so on. auth_mode.description: Indicates, whether each individual client on the port needs to be authenticated separately to gain access to the network. `client-mode`: every client needs to be authenticated to be                granted network access. `device-mode`: only one of the attached clients must be                authenticated for all clients to be granted                network access. `multi-domain`:limit the number of authenticated clients to one                 'voice' client and a configured number of 'data'                 clients. By default allowed 'data' client is                 also one. If empty, then port_access_auth_mode of the `Port` is used.

base_role_name.description: Name of the role from which this role has been derived. This will be published for the roles that are derived from a combination of user-role and RADIUS attributes.

cached_reauth_period.description: Duration in seconds until when cached re-authentication is allowed for clients on-boarded via this role. If empty, then Port_Access_Auth_Configuration.cached_reauth_period of the `Port` is used.

captive_portal_profile.description:
Reference Resource: [Captive_Portal_Profile](#/Captive_Portal_Profile)
Captive portal profile associated with this access role.

client_inactivity_monitor.description: Sets the inactivity mode  `configured_timeout`: value set by `client_inactivity_time` will be used for                        tracking inactivity  `dynamic_timeout`:    client will expire after global dynamic ageout value  `no_timeout`:         client will never ageout and stays in system.                        Example: mac-pinning

client_inactivity_timeout.description: Time in seconds after which a client will be removed from the port for lack of activity. This is only applicable when client_inactivity_monitor mode is set to 'configured_timeout'.

creation_time.description: Time in seconds since epoch when this role was created.

description.description: Free text description of role.

device_traffic_class.description: Specifies the class of client this role is associated with.

failure_reason.description: Response for the download request:  `server_not_reachable`:             server not reachable.  `authentication_failure`:           invalid user-id or password.  `certificate_invalid`:              server certificate not valid.  `certificate_missing`:              server certificate not configured.  `invalid_role_name`:                role name specified not found on server.  `parsing_failed`:                   failed to parse the downloaded file.  `server_timed_out`:                 server failed to respond.  `credentials_missing`:              server credentials not configured.  `internal_error`:                   error while downloading or                                      installing role.  `failed_during_issu`:               failed to install while issu is in                                      progress. Applicable for downloadable roles only.

state.description: Determines role state. Applicable for downloadable roles only. The states are:  `completed`:    role has been downloaded successfully.  `in_progress`:  role is being downloaded from the server.  `failed`:       role could not be downloaded from the server.

gateway_zone.description: Gateway zone associated with this user role.

in_gbp.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_GBP](#/Port_Access_GBP)
Ingress port-access Group Based policy.

in_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Policy](#/Port_Access_Policy)
Ingress port-access policy, to be applied when this role is assigned.

macsec_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [MACsec_Policy](#/MACsec_Policy)
MACsec policy associated with this user role. When not set, if the client is authenticated by 802.1X with this role on a port where MACsec is enabled for the 802.1X authenticator, traffic ingressing this port will be dropped.

max_session_time.description: The maximum number of seconds of service to provide to the client before termination of session. If empty, the maximum session time is indefinite.

mtu.description: The MTU (maximum transmission unit); i.e. the largest amount of data that can be transmitted in an IP packet. If empty, then active_ip_mtu value of the `Port` is used.

name.description:
Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
Name of the role.

origin.description: Origin of the access role, i.e., how the access role  is created.  `local`:           access role is configured locally on the switch.  `downloaded`:      downloaded from Clearpass Policy Manager (CPPM) server.  `radius`:          translated from the attributes assigned by RADIUS server.

poe_allocate_by_method.description: PoE power allocation method associated with this role Allows control over the power allocation strategy used. Two power allocation strategies are supported:  `class`:    the PSE uses the power ramp-up signature of the PD              to identify the PD's power class and use the power              level for the specified class.  `usage`:    power is delivered as requested by a PD. If empty, then config.allocate_by_method value of the `PoE_Interface` is used.

poe_priority.description: If the PoE demand exceeds the PoE budget, the switch will deny power to some ports. PoE prioritization is the way the switch  determines which ports are to receive power. The priorities are:  `critical`: the active PoE ports at this level are provisioned              before the PoE ports at any other level are provisioned.  `high`:     the active PoE ports at this level are provisioned              before the low priority PoE ports are provisioned.  `low`:      the active PoE ports at this level are provisioned              only if there is power available after provisioning              any active PoE ports at the higher priority levels. If empty, then config.priority value of the `PoE_Interface` is used.

pvlan_port_type.description: Specifies the port's type in the context of Private-VLAN. If empty, the pvlan_port_type value of the 'Port' is used.

qos_trust_mode.description: Specifies the individual port QoS Trust Mode.  `none`: no fields are inspected on arriving packets. The initial local-         priority and color meta-data values are taken from PCP 0 entry of the COS Map. `cos`:  will use the PCP of the outermost 802.1 VLAN tag to index the COS Map         entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.         For untagged packets, the initial local-priority and color meta-data values are         taken from code_point 0 entry of the COS Map. `dscp`: will use the DSCP value of IP packets to index the DSCP Map entry to         initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.  For         non-IP packets, what meta-data values are assigned is hardware dependent. If empty, then qos_config.qos_trust value of the `Port` is used.

radius_overridden_attributes.description: List of attributes in Source role that are overridden by RADIUS attributes.

reauth_period.description: Time period in seconds to enforce periodic re-authentication of the clients. If empty, then Port_Access_Auth_Configuration.reauth_period of the `Port` is used.

stp_admin_edge_port.description: Specifies whether the port will operate as an STP admin_edge port. If empty, then [stp_config].admin_edge_port_enable of the `Port` is used.

ubt_gateway_clearpass_role.description: Indicates the role name that will be communicated to the UBT  cluster. The cluster needs to download the role definition from  ClearPass.

ubt_gateway_role.description: Role to be assigned to tunneled clients on the UBT cluster side.

vlan_group_name.description: VLAN group name associated with this user role via RADIUS.

vlan_mode.description: When empty, default mode is selected as follows:  `access`:           if the vlan_tag contains a value, role contains an access vlan                      and the vlan_trunks will be empty.  `trunk`:            if the vlan_tag is empty, and the vlan_trunks is non-empty,                      then role has no-native vlan specified. If the mode is explicitly configured:  `native-tagged`:    value contained in vlan_tag refers to native vlan                      and that vlan has to be tagged.  `native-untagged`:  value contained in vlan_tag refers to native vlan                      and that vlan has to be untagged.

vlan_name_tag.description: The untagged VLAN, identified by name, to which users of this access role are assigned. If empty, VLAN identifier corresponding to the vlan_tag is used if set. Otherwise, vlan_tag of the 'Port' is used.

vlan_name_trunks.description: The tagged VLAN(s), identified by their names, to which users of this access role are assigned. If empty, VLAN identifier corresponding to the vlan_trunks is used if set. Otherwise, vlan_trunks of the 'Port' is used.

vlan_tag.description: The untagged VLAN identifier to which users of this access role are assigned. If empty, VLAN identifier corresponding to the vlan_name_tag is used if set. Otherwise, vlan_tag of the 'Port' is used.

vlan_trunks.description: The tagged VLAN identifier(s) to which users of this access role are assigned. If empty, VLAN identifier corresponding to the vlan_name_trunks is used if set. Otherwise, vlan_trunks of the 'Port' is used.

Example: mac-pinning

Reference Resource: [MACsec_Policy](#/MACsec_Policy)
MACsec policy associated with this user role. When not set, if the client is authenticated by 802.1X with this role on a port where MACsec is enabled for the 802.1X authenticator, traffic ingressing this port will be dropped.

max_session_time.description: The maximum number of seconds of service to provide to the client before termination of session. If empty, the maximum session time is indefinite.

Reference Resource: [Port_Access_Role](#/Port_Access_Role)
Name of the role.

origin.description: Origin of the access role, i.e., how the access role  is created.  `local`:           access role is configured locally on the switch.  `downloaded`:      downloaded from Clearpass Policy Manager (CPPM) server.  `radius`:          translated from the attributes assigned by RADIUS server.

poe_allocate_by_method.description: PoE power allocation method associated with this role Allows control over the power allocation strategy used. Two power allocation strategies are supported:  `class`:    the PSE uses the power ramp-up signature of the PD              to identify the PD's power class and use the power              level for the specified class.  `usage`:    power is delivered as requested by a PD. If empty, then config.allocate_by_method value of the `PoE_Interface` is used.

poe_priority.description: If the PoE demand exceeds the PoE budget, the switch will deny power to some ports. PoE prioritization is the way the switch  determines which ports are to receive power. The priorities are:  `critical`: the active PoE ports at this level are provisioned              before the PoE ports at any other level are provisioned.  `high`:     the active PoE ports at this level are provisioned              before the low priority PoE ports are provisioned.  `low`:      the active PoE ports at this level are provisioned              only if there is power available after provisioning              any active PoE ports at the higher priority levels. If empty, then config.priority value of the `PoE_Interface` is used.

pvlan_port_type.description: Specifies the port's type in the context of Private-VLAN. If empty, the pvlan_port_type value of the 'Port' is used.

qos_trust_mode.description: Specifies the individual port QoS Trust Mode.  `none`: no fields are inspected on arriving packets. The initial local-         priority and color meta-data values are taken from PCP 0 entry of the COS Map. `cos`:  will use the PCP of the outermost 802.1 VLAN tag to index the COS Map         entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.         For untagged packets, the initial local-priority and color meta-data values are         taken from code_point 0 entry of the COS Map. `dscp`: will use the DSCP value of IP packets to index the DSCP Map entry to         initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.  For         non-IP packets, what meta-data values are assigned is hardware dependent. If empty, then qos_config.qos_trust value of the `Port` is used.

reauth_period.description: Time period in seconds to enforce periodic re-authentication of the clients. If empty, then Port_Access_Auth_Configuration.reauth_period of the `Port` is used.

stp_admin_edge_port.description: Specifies whether the port will operate as an STP admin_edge port. If empty, then [stp_config].admin_edge_port_enable of the `Port` is used.

ubt_gateway_role.description: Role to be assigned to tunneled clients on the UBT cluster side.

vlan_mode.description: When empty, default mode is selected as follows:  `access`:           if the vlan_tag contains a value, role contains an access vlan                      and the vlan_trunks will be empty.  `trunk`:            if the vlan_tag is empty, and the vlan_trunks is non-empty,                      then role has no-native vlan specified. properties.description:
Reference Resource: [Power_supply](#/Power_supply)
References to the power supplies which are part of this subsystem.

instantaneous_current.description: Total instantaneous current drawn from the power supply in Amps.

instantaneous_power.description: Total instantaneous power supplied by the power supply in Watts.

instantaneous_voltage.description: Total instantaneous input voltage of the power supply in volts (V).

maximum_power.description: Total maximum power capacity that can be supplied by the power supply in Watts.

power_monitor_read_timestamp.description: The time in seconds since the switch booted when the power monitoring data for the power supply was last read.

airflow.description: Power supply airflow direction. Valid values are: 'F2B': Power supply has front-to-back airflow 'B2F': Power supply has back-to-front airflow

description.description: Short description of the power supply.

hardware_rev.description: Revision number of the hardware for the power supply.

input_voltage_high.description: Higher threshold of the power supply input voltage range for the given operating wattage. This is not set when the threshold is unknown.

input_voltage_low.description: Lower threshold of the power supply input voltage range for the given operating wattage. This is not set when the threshold is unknown.

product_name.description: Power supply product name identification.  This field is  used to determine if the power supply is supported.

serial_number.description: Power supply serial number to uniquely identify the power  supply.

voltage_type.description: Power supply input voltage type. Valid values are: 'AC': Power supply has AC voltage input 'DC': Power supply has DC voltage input This is not set when the voltage type is unknown.

name.description: Reference Resource: [Power_supply](#/Power_supply)

redundant_psu.description: List of redundant power supplies that are compatible with the power supply.

statistics.description: Various statistics about the power supply.

failures.description: Number of failures the power supply has experienced since the most recent insertion of the power supply and boot of the system.  The number of failures for a power supply will be cleared if the power supply is removed from the system or if the system is rebooted.  For non removable power supplies, the number of failures will not clear until the system reboots.  Failures are any events where power delivery from the power supply did not occur when expected.  This includes unsupported power supply types since their power delivery is not considered valid even though the power supply itself may not have an internal failure. Some examples of failures are over current, invalid input power, and unsupported power supply type.

warnings.description: Number of warnings the power supply has experienced since the most recent insertion of the power supply and boot of the system.  The number of warnings for a power supply will be cleared if the power supply is removed from the system or if the system is rebooted.  For non removable power supplies, the number of warnings will not clear until the system reboots.  Warnings are any events that do not impair the power delivery from the power supply but require notification that service may be needed.  Some examples of warnings are fan failures and over temperature.

status.description: Current status for the power supply.  Valid value are: 'ok':                power supply is operating normally 'fault_absent':      no power supply is installed when one is expected 'fault_input':       there is a fault condition on the input of the power supply 'fault_output':      there is a fault condition on the output of the power supply 'fault_poe':         there is a fault condition on the PoE output of the power supply 'fault_norecov':     power supply has experienced a non recoverable fault condition 'alert':             power supply has experienced an abnormal event but it is still operational 'unknown':           power supply has experienced an unknown fault condition 'unsupported':       power supply is not of a known supported type 'warning':           there is an internal fault condition but the power supply is still operational 'overvoltage':       power supply's input voltage has exceeded the normal input voltage range 'undervoltage':      power supply's input voltage has dipped below the normal input voltage range 'init':              power supply is initializing 'empty':             no power supply is installed 'fault_airflow':     airflow direction does not match the airflow direction for the chassis 'fault_redundancy':  type or capacity does not match the redundancy type and capacity for the chassis 'fault_mixed_input': input type of the inserted power supplies does not match

code_point.description:
Reference Resource: [QoS_DSCP_Map_Entry](#/QoS_DSCP_Map_Entry)
The identifier for an entry in the DSCP map that represents the Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value for this entry.

color.description: It may be used later in the pipeline in packet-drop decision points. The default is 'green'.

description.description: Used for customer documentation. When empty, the default_description key value from the hw_defaults column will be used.

default_code_point.description: The identifier for an entry in the DSCP map that represents the Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value for this entry.

default_description.description: Contains the description of the given Traffic  Type (e.g. AF23).

default_local_priority.description: When missing, the default local_priority is obtained from the [hw_defaults](QoS_DSCP_Map_Entry.hw_defaults) of the [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry) row indexed by the top 3-bits of this row's code_point (i.e. class selector bits cs0 through cs7).

default_priority_code_point.description: When missing, the default is not to remark packet 802.1Q priorities.

local_priority.description: This is a switch internal meta-data value that will be associated with the packet. This value will be used later to select the egress queue for the packet. When empty, the default_local_priority key value from the hw_defaults column will be used.

priority_code_point.description: The 802.1Q Priority Code Point (PCP) that will be assigned to any IP packet with the specified DSCP codepoint, if that packet's ingress port has an effective trust mode of `trust dscp`.  The new PCP is used when the packet is transmitted out a port or trunk with a VLAN tag.  If the key is not specified, then no remark will occur.

algorithm.description: This parameter selects the scheduling behavior of the queue:  * `strict` - Strict Priority will service all packets in the queue before any packets in lower numbered queues as long as there are no packets in any higher number queue. `dwrr` - Deficit Weighted Round Robin will apportion available bandwidth among all non-empty dwrr queues in relation to their queue weights. `wfq` - Weighted Fair Queuing will apportion available bandwidth among all non-empty wfq queues in relation to their queue weights.  If this parameter is missing, it is assumed to be 'strict'.

bandwidth.description: The bandwidth limit to apply to egress queue traffic. If no bandwidth value is applied, the bandwidth will not be limited per queue. If the algorithm configured on this queue does not support a bandwidth limit, this  value will be ignored. Bandwidth limits to configure per-queue shaping are  supported on queues which use the following algorithms: - Strict Configuration can be validated by referring to [egress_shape_hw_rate] (Port.rate_limits_status.egress_shape_hw_rate).

bandwidth_units.description: Units of the egress queue bandwidth: kbps: kilobits per second. percent - the units are in percentage of port speed.

burst.description: The burst size (in kilobytes) allowed per bandwidth-limited queue. If no burst is specified, the default burst of 32 KB will be applied. Per-queue burst is supported on queues which use the following algorithms: - Strict Configuration can be validated by referring to [egress_burst_hw_rate] (Port.rate_limits_status.egress_burst_hw_rate).

hw_default.description: When true, this row contains the hardware default schedule profile parameters for this queue.

queue_number.description:
Reference Resource: [Queue](#/Queue)
Schedule parameters for individual queues. Queues are numbered in *priority order*, with zero being the lowest priority. The maximum number of queues is hardware dependent.

weight.description: The weight value for this queue. The maximum weight is hardware dependent.

There must be a user-defined name of the schedule profile.

algorithm.description: This parameter selects the scheduling behavior of the queue:  * `strict` - Strict Priority will service all packets in the queue before any packets in lower numbered queues as long as there are no packets in any higher number queue. `dwrr` - Deficit Weighted Round Robin will apportion available bandwidth among all non-empty dwrr queues in relation to their queue weights. `wfq` - Weighted Fair Queuing will apportion available bandwidth among all non-empty wfq queues in relation to their queue weights.  If this parameter is missing, it is assumed to be 'strict'.

bandwidth.description: The bandwidth limit to apply to egress queue traffic. If no bandwidth value is applied, the bandwidth will not be limited per queue. If the algorithm configured on this queue does not support a bandwidth limit, this  value will be ignored. Bandwidth limits to configure per-queue shaping are  supported on queues which use the following algorithms: - Strict Configuration can be validated by referring to [egress_shape_hw_rate] (Port.rate_limits_status.egress_shape_hw_rate).

bandwidth_units.description: Units of the egress queue bandwidth: kbps: kilobits per second. percent - the units are in percentage of port speed.

burst.description: The burst size (in kilobytes) allowed per bandwidth-limited queue. If no burst is specified, the default burst of 32 KB will be applied. Per-queue burst is supported on queues which use the following algorithms: - Strict Configuration can be validated by referring to [egress_burst_hw_rate] (Port.rate_limits_status.egress_burst_hw_rate).

hw_default.description: When true, this row contains the hardware default schedule profile parameters for this queue.

queue_number.description:
Reference Resource: [Queue](#/Queue)
Schedule parameters for individual queues. Queues are numbered in *priority order*, with zero being the lowest priority. The maximum number of queues is hardware dependent.

weight.description: The weight value for this queue. The maximum weight is hardware dependent.

match_access_list.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
Inbound ACL to filter packets received from specific routers sending Router Advertisement packets. If not set, inbound filtering will be disabled.

manage_flag.description: When set, this enables verification of the 'managed config' flag in RA packets. on: Verify that the flag is set to 'On'. off: verify that the flag is set to 'Off'. If not set, validation of the 'managed config' flag is not done.

other_flag.description: When set, this enables verification of the 'other config' flag in RA packets. on: Verify that the flag is set to 'On'. off: verify that the flag is set to 'Off'. If not set, validation of the 'other config' flag is not done.

enable.description: Enables hop-limit verification.

maximum.description: When set, the RA/RR packet is discarded if the advertised hop-limit is greater than the specified max-hop limit.

minimum.description: When set, the RA/RR packet is discarded if the advertised hop limit is lesser than the specified min-hop limit.

match_prefix_list.description:
Reference Resource: [Prefix_List](#/Prefix_List)
List of IPv6 prefixes that are allowed to be processed from Router Advertisement packets. If not set, validation of the 'prefix-list' is not done.

match_router_preference.description: When set, router preference value advertised in the RA packet is matched and the packet is discarded if the match conditions are not met. high    Set the maximum router preference to high. low     Set the maximum router preference to low. medium  Set the maximum router preference to medium. If not set, validation of the 'router preference' value is not done.

framed_ip_addr.description: The Framed-IP-Address attribute sent in  RADIUS packets indicates the address configured for the user. The value of this attribute is taken from the IP binding table or Client IP Tracker table (In the same order). Both request type and service type should be configured to include this attribute in RADIUS packets.

request_type.description: The request-type for which Framed-IP-Address (RADIUS attribute type 8) will be included.

service_type.description: The service-type for which Framed-IP-Address attribute 8 will be included in RADIUS access request.

request_type.description: The request-type for which NAS-Id attribute will be included.

service_type.description: The service-type for which NAS-Id attribute will be included.

value.description: The unique string to identify the Network Access Switch. This will be included in the RADIUS request packet as part of NAS-Id attribute.

nas_ip_addr.description: NAS-IP address will be Source IP of the switch. If Source IP is not configured, Outgoing interface IP will be sent as NAS-IP. Both request-type and service-type should be set to include the NAS-IP-Address attribute in User Management RADIUS access request packet.

request_type.description: The request-type for which NAS-IP address attribute will be included.

service_type.description: The service-type for which NAS-IP address attribute will be included in RADIUS access request.

address.description:
Reference Resource: [Radius_Dynamic_Authorization_Client](#/Radius_Dynamic_Authorization_Client)
IPV4/IPV6 address or FQDN of the RADIUS DAC.

connection_type.description:
Reference Resource: [Radius_Dynamic_Authorization_Client](#/Radius_Dynamic_Authorization_Client)
Specify the connection_type of RADIUS DAC.

replay_protection_enable.description: Enables replay protection for the client.

resolved_ip_addr.description: IP address resolved for this Dynamic Authorization Client. It can be IPv4 or IPv6. This is only set if the configured RADIUS Dynauth Client is in FQDN format.

rfc5176_enforcement_mode.description: Enforcement mode of RFC5176. 'strict': authorization attributes are not allowed as part of           disconnect requests. 'loose' : authorization attributes are allowed as part of           disconnect requests.

secret_key.description: The secret key used to communicate with this RADIUS DAC. If not set, then all requests from DAC will be silently discarded.

statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RADIUS dynamic authorization (CoA or disconnect) packets communicated with the DAC. This statistics will be updated every 5 seconds.

coa_ack.description: Number of RADIUS CoA-ACKs sent towards this DAC.

coa_authorize_only_reqs.description: Number of RADIUS CoA-requests received from this DAC with service-type attribute set to 'Authorize only'.

coa_malformed_reqs.description: Number of malformed RADIUS CoA-Requests received from this DAC (exluding the one's with bad authenticators and unknown types).

coa_nak.description: Number of RADIUS CoA-NAK's sent towards this DAC including the one's with Service-Type attribute set to 'Authorize Only' and also because of non established session context.

coa_nak_session_no_context.description: Number of RADIUS CoA-NAKs sent towards this DAC because no session context was found.

coa_nak_user_session_changed.description: Number of user session's authorization changed due to RADIUS CoA-Requests received from this DAC.

coa_packets_dropped.description: Number of incoming RADIUS CoA packets discarded silently from this DAC for the reasons other than malforming, bad authenticators or unknown types.

coa_reqs.description: Number of RADIUS CoA-requests received from this DAC.

coa_reqs_bad_authenticators.description: Number of RADIUS CoA-Requests received with bad authenticator from this DAC.

disc_ack.description: Number of RADIUS Disconnect-ACKs sent to this DAC.
