accounting_statistics.description: Contains statistical information relating to accounting packets exchanged with the server.

bad_authenticator.description: Number of Accounting-Response packets received from this server with invalid authenticator information.

dropped_pkts.description: Number of Accounting packets from this server that have been dropped by the switch.

malformed_responses.description: Number of malformed response packets received from this server.

pending_requests.description: Number of accounting requests that the server has not yet responded back to. This does not include requests that have been timed out.

requests.description: Number of accounting requests sent to this server (excluding retransmissions).

responses.description: Number of accounting responses received from this server.

retransmits.description: Number of accounting requests re-transmitted to this server.

round_trip_time.description: Time interval in seconds between the most recent accounting-request sent to this server and the corresponding response received from the server.

timed_out_requests.description: Number of accounting requests to this server that have been timed out.

unknown_type.description: Number of packets of unknown type received from  this server.

accounting_udp_port.description: UDP port to be used for the communication to RADIUS accounting.

address.description:
Reference Resource: [Radius_Server](#/Radius_Server)
IPV4/IPV6 address or FQDN of the RADIUS server.

auth_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of authentication packets communicated with the server. These statistics  will be updated every 5 seconds.

access_accepts.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Accept packets received from this server.

access_challenge.description: Number of RADIUS Access-challenge packets reveived from this server.

access_rejects.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Reject packets received from this server.

access_request.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Request packets sent to this server (excluding retransmissions).

access_response_malformed.description: Number of malformed RADIUS Access-Response packets received from this server.

access_retransmits.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Request retransmitted from this server.

bad_authenticator.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Response Packets containing invalid authenticators or signature attributes received from this server.

dropped_pkt.description: Number of RADIUS packets dropped from this server on the authentication port.

malformed_pkt.description: Number of malformed authentication packets received from this server.

pending_requests.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Request packets destined for this server that have not yet timed out or received a response.

round_trip_time.description: Time interval between the most recent Access-Reply/ Access-Challenge and the Access-Request that matched it from this server.

timeout.description: Number of timed out RADIUS Access-Request packets destined for this server.

unknown_types.description: Number of RADIUS packets of unknown type received from this server on the authentication port.

auth_type.description: Specifies the server specific authentication method (pap/chap) to be used. If not set, the globally configured authentication method (pap/chap) will be used.

password.description: Password to be used for authentication.

user_id.description: User name to be used for authentication.

ipsec_ah.description: IPSec Authentication Header configuration. If both AH and ESP are configured, then ESP will be ignored and AH will be used. If both System level and Radius_Server AH configuration is provided then Radius_Server configuration will be used for the specific Radius server.

SPI.description: Security Parameters Index (SPI) for the Security Association (SA). AH SPI must be unique on a router because it is carried in IPsec protocol packet to enable the receiving system to select the SA to process the packet.

ah_null.description: Disables AH configuration for the Radius server.

ipsec_esp.description: IPSec Encapsulating Security Protocol configuration. If both AH and ESP are configured, then ESP will be ignored and AH will be used. If both System level and Radius_Server ESP configuration is provided then Radius_Server configuration will be used for the specific Radius server.

SPI.description: Security Parameters Index (SPI) for the Security Association (SA). ESP SPI must be unique on a router because it is carried in IPsec protocol packet to enable the receiving system to select the SA to process the packet.

esp_null.description: Disables ESP configuration for the Radius server.

last_tracking_attempted_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when the most recent reachability tracking request was sent to the RADIUS server.

last_tracking_status_changed_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when RADIUS Server status last changed from reachable to unreachable or vice versa.

last_tracking_status_refreshed_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when the tracking status was last refreshed.

msg_authenticator_check.description: Specifies whether Message-Authenticator attribute must be presented in Radius Server Responses.

passkey.description: Specifies the passkey between RADIUS client and RADIUS server for authentication. If not set, the globally configured passkey will be used.

port.description:
Reference Resource: [Radius_Server](#/Radius_Server)
Specifies the port number for authentication.

port_access.description: Configures the message type sent in RadSec sessions created for port-access authentication for keeping the session active 'status-server' : status-server messages are sent for keeping the session active. 'keep-alive'    : keep-alive messages are be sent for keeping the session active

port_type.description:
Reference Resource: [Radius_Server](#/Radius_Server)
Specifies the type of port (tcp/udp) for authentication.

reachability_status.description: Specifies the reachability of Configured RADIUS Server. 'reachable':              tracking for this server is enabled and                           the server is reachable. 'unreachable':            tracking for this server is enabled and                           the server is not reachable. 'reachability_unhealthy': tracking for this server is enabled and                           the server is momentarily down in                           between tracking interval. An empty value means the reachability of this server is unknown.

resolved_ip_address.description: IP address resolved for this server. It can be IPv4 or IPv6. This is only set if the configured RADIUS server address is in FQDN format.

retries.description: Specifies the server specific number of retries to the RADIUS server if there is no response. If not set, the globally configured retries will be used.

server_group.description:
Reference Resource: [AAA_Server_Group](#/AAA_Server_Group)
Key specifies the RADIUS server-group that it belongs to. It would belong to a family group 'radius' group and the user defined AAA server group Value specifies the priority of the RADIUS server in the associated AAA server group. A server with lower priority in a server group is reached out first. Servers with equal priority in a group will be reached out as follows: Those belonging to VRF where vrf_name appears alphabetically earlier than the others are reached out first. If that's a tie, servers with address appearing alphabetically earlier than the others is reached out first. If that too is a tie, servers with smaller UDP port are reached out first.

status_server_port_access_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RadSec status-server-request-reponse packets communicated in the RadSec session used for port-access authentication. These will be updated every 5 seconds.

status_server_requests.description: Number of status server request packets sent in RadSec session used for port-access authentication (excluding retransmissions).

status_server_responses.description: Number of status server response packets received in RadSec session used for port-access authentication.

status_server_tracking_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RadSec status-server-request-reponse packets communicated in the RadSec session used for server tracking. These will be updated every 5 seconds.

status_server_requests.description: Number of status server request packets sent in RadSec session used for server tracking (excluding retransmissions).

status_server_responses.description: Number of status server response packets received in RadSec session used for server tracking.

timeout.description: Specifies the server specific timeout between authentication requests to the RADIUS server. If not set, the globally configured timeout will be used.

tls_connection_status.description: Status of the TLS connection 'tls_connection_established': RADIUS server TLS connection                               successfully established. 'tls_connection_closed':      RADIUS server TLS connection has                               been closed. 'tcp_connection_failed':      RADIUS server TCP connection could                               not be established. 'tls_connection_failed':      RADIUS server TLS connection could                               not be established. 'tcp_connection_in_progress': RADIUS server TCP connection is in                               progress. 'tls_connection_in_progress': RADIUS server TLS connection is in                               progress.

tls_initial_connection_timeout.description: RADIUS over TLS initial connection timeout value in seconds. If not specified, the globally configured initial connection timeout value will be used.

tracking_enable.description: Specifies whether tracking should be enabled on this server.

tracking_method.description: Configures the tracking method used for tracking server reacchability. Tracking method configuration is applicable only when tracking is enabled for the server. 'status-server'  : status-server messages are sent for server tracking. 'keep-alive'     : keep-alive messages are sent for server tracking. 'access-request' : access-request messages are sent for server tracking

tracking_mode.description: Specifies the tracking mode to be set for this server and is only applicable when tracking is enabled for this server. 'any'       : Server reachability is monitored regardless of               whether the server was responsive or non-responsive               to prior RADIUS client requests. 'dead-only' : Server reachability is monitored only if it is               deemed dead (based on non-responsiveness for RADIUS               client requests sent to this server earlier).

tracking_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RADIUS Access-Request-Response packets communicated with the server for tracking purpose. These will be updated every 5 seconds

access_requests.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Request packets sent to this server for tracking(excluding retransmissions).

access_responses.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Response packets received for tracking packets from this server.

last_tracking_attempted_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when the most recent reachability tracking request was sent to the RADIUS server.

last_tracking_status_changed_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when RADIUS Server status last changed from reachable to unreachable or vice versa.

last_tracking_status_refreshed_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when the tracking status was last refreshed.

Reference Resource: [Radius_Server](#/Radius_Server)
Specifies the type of port (tcp/udp) for authentication.

reachability_status.description: Specifies the reachability of Configured RADIUS Server. 'reachable':              tracking for this server is enabled and                           the server is reachable. 'unreachable':            tracking for this server is enabled and                           the server is not reachable. 'reachability_unhealthy': tracking for this server is enabled and                           the server is momentarily down in                           between tracking interval. An empty value means the reachability of this server is unknown.

resolved_ip_address.description: IP address resolved for this server. It can be IPv4 or IPv6. This is only set if the configured RADIUS server address is in FQDN format.

retries.description: Specifies the server specific number of retries to the RADIUS server if there is no response. If not set, the globally configured retries will be used.

server_group.description:
Reference Resource: [AAA_Server_Group](#/AAA_Server_Group)
Key specifies the RADIUS server-group that it belongs to. It would belong to a family group 'radius' group and the user defined AAA server group Value specifies the priority of the RADIUS server in the associated AAA server group. A server with lower priority in a server group is reached out first. Servers with equal priority in a group will be reached out as follows: Those belonging to VRF where vrf_name appears alphabetically earlier than the others are reached out first. If that's a tie, servers with address appearing alphabetically earlier than the others is reached out first. If that too is a tie, servers with smaller UDP port are reached out first.

status_server_port_access_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RadSec status-server-request-reponse packets communicated in the RadSec session used for port-access authentication. These will be updated every 5 seconds.

status_server_requests.description: Number of status server request packets sent in RadSec session used for port-access authentication (excluding retransmissions).

status_server_responses.description: Number of status server response packets received in RadSec session used for port-access authentication.

status_server_tracking_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RadSec status-server-request-reponse packets communicated in the RadSec session used for server tracking. These will be updated every 5 seconds.

status_server_requests.description: Number of status server request packets sent in RadSec session used for server tracking (excluding retransmissions).

status_server_responses.description: Number of status server response packets received in RadSec session used for server tracking.

timeout.description: Specifies the server specific timeout between authentication requests to the RADIUS server. If not set, the globally configured timeout will be used.

tls_connection_status.description: Status of the TLS connection 'tls_connection_established': RADIUS server TLS connection                               successfully established. 'tls_connection_closed':      RADIUS server TLS connection has                               been closed. 'tcp_connection_failed':      RADIUS server TCP connection could                               not be established. 'tls_connection_failed':      RADIUS server TLS connection could                               not be established. 'tcp_connection_in_progress': RADIUS server TCP connection is in                               progress. 'tls_connection_in_progress': RADIUS server TLS connection is in                               progress.

tls_initial_connection_timeout.description: RADIUS over TLS initial connection timeout value in seconds. If not specified, the globally configured initial connection timeout value will be used.

tracking_enable.description: Specifies whether tracking should be enabled on this server.

tracking_method.description: Configures the tracking method used for tracking server reacchability. Tracking method configuration is applicable only when tracking is enabled for the server. 'status-server'  : status-server messages are sent for server tracking. 'keep-alive'     : keep-alive messages are sent for server tracking. 'access-request' : access-request messages are sent for server tracking

tracking_mode.description: Specifies the tracking mode to be set for this server and is only applicable when tracking is enabled for this server. 'any'       : Server reachability is monitored regardless of               whether the server was responsive or non-responsive               to prior RADIUS client requests. 'dead-only' : Server reachability is monitored only if it is               deemed dead (based on non-responsiveness for RADIUS               client requests sent to this server earlier).

tracking_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of RADIUS Access-Request-Response packets communicated with the server for tracking purpose. These will be updated every 5 seconds

access_requests.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Request packets sent to this server for tracking(excluding retransmissions).

access_responses.description: Number of RADIUS Access-Response packets received for tracking packets from this server.

action.description: 'permit': User operation will be allowed. 'deny':   User operation will be denied. RBAC rule will only be activated when an associated action is provided. If `action` is not provided, the RBAC rule will be ignored as only comment is provided.

cli.description: If `command` is not provided, the RBAC rule will be ignored  during the authorization of the CLI commands.

command.description: POSIX compliant regular expression that matches  one or more CLI commands.

comment.description: Comment associated with the RBAC rule. If not set, there is no comment associated to the RBAC rule and only action is set.

invalid_reason.description: Indicates the reason why the RBAC rule is invalid. Empty when  the RBAC rule is `valid` or `not_processed`. 'missing_action'           : The `action` field is missing. 'missing_regex'            : The `command` regex in `cli` field is missing. 'invalid_cli_command_regex': The `command` regex in `cli` field is invalid.

sequence_number.description:
Reference Resource: [RBAC_Rule_Entry](#/RBAC_Rule_Entry)
Role Based Access Control rules applicable to a user group. When local authorization is added to AAA authorization list, these rules will be traversed in an ascending order of the sequence number to find a rule that matches the user operation on the switch. The matching rule determines whether the user operation is allowed or denied. If no rule matches, user operation will be denied.

status.description: Indicates the status of the RBAC rule. Only the valid RBAC rules  are used during local authorization. 'valid'        : An RBAC rule is valid if one of the conditions are met.                  - Only `comment` is provided.                  - `action` and `cli` are provided with a valid                      POSIX compliant `command` regex.                  - `comment`, `action` and `cli` are provided with a                      valid POSIX compliant `command` regex. 'invalid'      : The RBAC rule is invalid. 'not_processed': The RBAC rule is not processed yet.

parameters.name: User_Group.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [User_Group](#/User_Group)
Name of the user group. Built-in user groups are as follows: `administrators`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 15. Members have access to: All the CLI commands and bash shell. All the REST Methods through REST APIs. `operators`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 1. Members have access to: All "show" CLI commands (except those that display sensitive information). All "GET" requests through REST APIs. `auditors`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 19. Members have access to: All "show" CLI commands to display and copy security logs. All "GET" requests for security logs through REST APIs. Only users belonging to the above three default groups will be allowed access to REST APIs.

parameters.name: RBAC_Rule_Entry.sequence_number
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [RBAC_Rule_Entry](#/RBAC_Rule_Entry)
Role Based Access Control rules applicable to a user group. When local authorization is added to AAA authorization list, these rules will be traversed in an ascending order of the sequence number to find a rule that matches the user operation on the switch. address_family.description: Represents the address family for this entry. Default value is `ipv4`.

attributes.description: Indicates any special attributes this Route entry has.

is_host_route.description: `is_host_route`:  When this route attribute is set to true, it is programmed in the host table instead of the route table.

distance.description: Administrative distance for the route entry. This value is populated every time a protocol or a user adds a new entry. The default value is 1 which is the default distance for static routes.

from.description: Protocol that is responsible for this entry: `bgp`:       the route is created by BGP protocol `ospf`:      the route is created by OSPF protocol `static`:    the route is configured by the user `connected`: the route is for a directly connected subnet 'local':     route for the IP address configured on the device itself 'bgp-unnumbered': route for the IP address configured on the unnumbered interface `bgp-unnumbered` : route for the IP address configured on unnumbered interface `rip`: the route is created by RIP protocol

metric.description: This is the BGP Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) attribute used in best path selection. The MED provides a dynamic way to influence another AS in the way to reach a certain route when there are multiple entry points for that AS.  BGP decision process takes weight, local preference, AS path, Origin and MED into account.  For selection, if all other factors are equal, the exit point with the lowest MED is preferred. Default value is 0

nexthops.description:
Reference Resource: [Nexthop](#/Nexthop)
List of all the nexthops for this entry. This will be empty in case of nullroute.

prefix.description:
Reference Resource: [Route](#/Route)
IPv4 or IPv6 destination prefix and mask in the address/mask format. Example: 192.168.0.0/16

protocol_private.description: Indicates that this row is a protocol specific route entry. The entries which have this value set, should not participate in routing. Example: BGP can store routes for reference and future selection but should not currently be used for forwarding. Default is `false`.

route_age.description: Time (in seconds from Epoch) when this route was added.

selected.description: Route table can have entries which may not be selected for forwarding. This flag indicates if this entry is selected as an active route for forwarding. Default is `false`.

source_vrfs.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
List of VRFs that this route originated from. This is only set for routes that have been leaked from one VRF to another.

sub_address_family.description: Represents more information regarding this entry. Default is `unicast`.

sub_protocol_type.description: Specifies the sub-protocol type of the route: ospf_intra_area : OSPF Intra Area route ospf_inter_area : OSPF Inter Area route ospf_type1_ext  : OSPF Extrenal Type-1 route ospf_type2_ext  : OSPF External Type-2 route ospf_type1_nssa : OSPF Type-1 NSSA route ospf_type2_nssa : OSPF Type-2 NSSA route bgp_int         : BGP Internal route bgp_ext         : BGP External route bgp_vpn         : BGP VPN route bgp_evpn        : BGP EVPN route

tag.description:
Reference Resource: [Nexthop](#/Nexthop)
Tag value associated with this route.

type.description: Specifies whether the route is of type nullroute, reject, forward or local: `forward`:   the packets that match the route for destination will be forwarded              based on the nexthop entry. `reject`:    the packets that match the route for destination will be discarded              and an ICMP unreachable message is sent to the sender. `nullroute`: the packets that match the route for destination will be silently              discarded without sending any ICMP message to the sender. `nullroute`: the packets that match the route for destination will be silently              discarded without sending any ICMP message to the sender. 'local':     the packets that match the route for destination will be consumed by              the device and will not be forwarded.

vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [Route](#/Route)
VRF that the route belongs to.

action.description: There are three types, permit, deny, and any.

call.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map_Entry](#/Route_Map_Entry)
If call command is used, nextrm indicate which route map to goto. This is optional.

half_life.description: Amount of time (in minutes) that must elapse to reduce the penalty by one half.

max_suppress_time.description: The longest amount of time (in minutes) that a route can be suppressed.

reuse.description: If the penalty is less than the reuse limit, a suppressed route that is up will no longer be suppressed.

suppress.description: If the penalty is greater than the suppress limit, the route is suppressed.

description.description: Free form description of the filter, this is optional.

exitpolicy.description: Rather than normal exiting, route map can continue on processing next route map, or goto N route map and continue on processing. This is optional.

goto_target.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map_Entry](#/Route_Map_Entry)
If exitpolicy is goto, nextpref is the route map to jump to. This is optional.

match.description: The match rule for route map. Default is deny.

ipv4_next_hop_address.description: Matches routes based on next hop IPv4 address.

ipv6_next_hop.description: Matches routes based on next hop IPv6 address.

local_preference.description: Matches routes with the specific local preference value.

metric.description: Matches routes with the specific metric value.

origin.description: Matches BGP routes based on the origin of the specified route. The allowed values are below.  1. <mark>EGP</mark> - Indicates that the route is learned through EBGP. 1. <mark>IGP</mark> - Indicates that the route is learned through IBGP. 1. <mark>incomplete</mark> - Indicates that the origin of route is unknown. This occurs when a route is redistributed into BGP.

probability.description: Randomly match specified percentage of the routes.

route_type.description: Match the specified route type.  1. <mark>local</mark> - Locally generated Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routes. 2. <mark>internal</mark> - Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) intra-area and interarea routes or Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) internal routes. 3. <mark>external type-1</mark> - For OSPF, the external type-1 keyword matches only Type 1(OSPF) external routes. 4. <mark>external type-2</mark> - For OSPF, the external type-2 keyword matches only Type 2(EIGRP) external routes. 'evpn-type-1' : Ethernet Auto-discovery Route 'evpn-type-2' : MAC/IP Advertisement Route 'evpn-type-3' : Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag Route 'evpn-type-4' : Ethernet Segment Route 'evpn-type-5' : IP Prefix Route

ipv6_next_hop_global.description: + Sets the BGP-4 + global IPv6 next hop address. The value is the IPv6 address.

local_preference.description: Sets the BGP local preference and the local preference value of an IBGP route.

metric.description: Sets the metric which is used with BGP route advertisement.

metric_type.description: Set the specified metric type.  1. <mark>internal</mark> - Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) intra-area and interarea routes or Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) internal routes. 2. <mark>external type-1</mark> - For OSPF, the external type-1 keyword matches only Type 1(OSPF) external routes. 3. <mark>external type-2</mark> - For OSPF, the external type-2 keyword matches only Type 2(EIGRP) external routes.

origin.description: Sets the origin attribute of a local BGP route. The allowed values are below.  1. <mark>EGP</mark> - Indicates that the route is learned through EBGP. 1. <mark>IGP</mark> - Indicates that the route is learned through IBGP. 1. <mark>incomplete</mark> - Indicates that the origin of route is unknown. This occurs when a route is redistributed into BGP.

weight.description: Sets the weight of a BGP route.

set_community_list_delete.description:
Reference Resource: [BGP_Community_Filter](#/BGP_Community_Filter)
Removes communities from the specified community list for BGP route advertisements.

set_tag.description: Set the specified tags in the route.

parameters.name: Route_Map.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map](#/Route_Map)
Name of the routemap.

parameters.name: Route_Map_Entry.preference
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map_Entry](#/Route_Map_Entry)
Route map entries keyed by preference value.

action.description: There are three types, permit, deny, and any.

call.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map_Entry](#/Route_Map_Entry)
If call command is used, nextrm indicate which route map to goto. This is optional.

half_life.description: Amount of time (in minutes) that must elapse to reduce the penalty by one half.

max_suppress_time.description: The longest amount of time (in minutes) that a route can be suppressed.

reuse.description: If the penalty is less than the reuse limit, a suppressed route that is up will no longer be suppressed.

suppress.description: If the penalty is greater than the suppress limit, the route is suppressed.

description.description: Free form description of the filter, this is optional.

exitpolicy.description: Rather than normal exiting, route map can continue on processing next route map, or goto N route map and continue on processing. This is optional.

goto_target.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map_Entry](#/Route_Map_Entry)
If exitpolicy is goto, nextpref is the route map to jump to. This is optional.

match.description: The match rule for route map. Default is deny.

ipv4_next_hop_address.description: Matches routes based on next hop IPv4 address.

ipv6_next_hop.description: Matches routes based on next hop IPv6 address.

local_preference.description: Matches routes with the specific local preference value.

metric.description: Matches routes with the specific metric value.

origin.description: Matches BGP routes based on the origin of the specified route. The allowed values are below.  1. <mark>EGP</mark> - Indicates that the route is learned through EBGP. 1. <mark>IGP</mark> - Indicates that the route is learned through IBGP. 1. <mark>incomplete</mark> - Indicates that the origin of route is unknown. This occurs when a route is redistributed into BGP.

probability.description: Randomly match specified percentage of the routes.

route_type.description: Match the specified route type.  1. <mark>local</mark> - Locally generated Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routes. 2. <mark>internal</mark> - Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) intra-area and interarea routes or Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) internal routes. 3. <mark>external type-1</mark> - For OSPF, the external type-1 keyword matches only Type 1(OSPF) external routes. 4. <mark>external type-2</mark> - For OSPF, the external type-2 keyword matches only Type 2(EIGRP) external routes. 'evpn-type-1' : Ethernet Auto-discovery Route 'evpn-type-2' : MAC/IP Advertisement Route 'evpn-type-3' : Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag Route 'evpn-type-4' : Ethernet Segment Route 'evpn-type-5' : IP Prefix Route

source_protocol.description: Match the specified source protocol of the routes.  1. <mark>static</mark> - Indicates that the route's source is static route. 2. <mark>connected</mark> - Indicates that the route's source is connected interfaces. 3. <mark>ospf</mark> - Indicates that the route's source is OSPF protocol. 4. <mark>static</mark> - Indicates that the route's source is BGP protocol.

vni.description: Matches routes with the specific Virtual Network-ID value.

match_as_path.description:
Reference Resource: [BGP_ASPath_Filter](#/BGP_ASPath_Filter)
Match routes based on AS path. This is optional.

match_community_list.description:
Reference Resource: [BGP_Community_Filter](#/BGP_Community_Filter)
Maps the community list that should be matched to whether it should be matched exactly or based on the presence of any community from the list.

match_extcommunity_list.description:
Reference Resource: [BGP_Community_Filter](#/BGP_Community_Filter)
Extended community list name to be matched.

match_interface.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
Match the specified interface in the route's next hop.

match_ipv4_next_hop_prefix_list.description:
Reference Resource: [Prefix_List](#/Prefix_List)
Match IPv4 next hop routes based on Prefix list. This is optional.

match_ipv4_prefix_list.description:
Reference Resource: [Prefix_List](#/Prefix_List)
Match routes based on IPv4 prefix list. This is optional.

match_ipv4_route_source_prefix_list.description:
Reference Resource: [Prefix_List](#/Prefix_List)
Match IPv4 source routes based on Prefix list. This is optional.

match_ipv6_next_hop_prefix_list.description:
Reference Resource: [Prefix_List](#/Prefix_List)
Match IPv6 next hop routes based on Prefix list. This is optional.

match_ipv6_prefix_list.description:
Reference Resource: [Prefix_List](#/Prefix_List)
Match routes based on IPv6 prefix list. This is optional.

match_tag.description: Match the specified tags in the route.

preference.description:
Reference Resource: [Route_Map_Entry](#/Route_Map_Entry)
Route map entries keyed by preference value.

route_map_continue.description: Specifies the route-map entry's sequence number that will be executed next if the current entry's match clause is successful If the specified entry does not exist, route-map processing will be terminated at the current sequence number if its clause is matched. Note that the 'continue' sequence number must be higher than the current route-map sequence number for it to take effect. This is optional.

set.description: The set rule for route map.

aggregator_as.description: Sets the originating AS of an aggregated route. The value is the Autonomous System  number.

as_path_exclude.description: Excludes AS numbers from the AS path. The value is a comma delimited list of autonomous system numbers to be excluded for incoming routes.

as_path_prepend.description: Prepends AS numbers to the AS path. The value is a list of AS numbers separated by a space.

atomic-aggregate.description: If set to 'true', upstream routers will be notified that route is aggregated. Default is false.

community.description: Sets the community list of the route.The value is community list name.

evpn_router_mac.description: Sets the Router MAC in the EVPN updates. An example of usage is, if the next-hop of a EVPN route is modified then the relevant Router MAC is updated with this option.

extcommunity_rt.description: Sets the route target extended community of a BGP route. The value is the community attribute in the form AA:NN where AA can be either AS number or IP address and NN is the community identifier.

extcommunity_soo.description: Sets the site-of-origin extended community of a BGP route. The value is the community attribute in the form AA:NN where AA can be either AS number or IP address and NN is the community identifier.

ipv6_next_hop_global.description: + Sets the BGP-4 + global IPv6 next hop address. The value is the IPv6 address.

'nullroute':  the packets that match the route for destination will be silently               discarded without sending any ICMP message to the sender. 'local':      the packets that match the route for destination will be consumed by               the device and will not be forwarded.

count.description: Maximum number of times the schedule can trigger. If not set, no limit is applied on the number of triggers. This is not applicable for 'one-shot' schedule type. Once schedule is triggered *count* number of times, the status changes to *expired*.

days_of_week.description: Specify the days of the week associated with this schedule. This is only applicable when the schedule type is set to 'calendar' type. Note: If both *days_of_month* and *days_of_week* are specified, then only *days_of_week* is considered.

Schedule name.

next_trigger_timestamp.description: Epoch timestamp of the next trigger corresponding to this schedule.

periodicity.description: Specify the periodic interval associated with this schedule. This is only applicable when the schedule type is set to 'periodic' type.

day.description: Periodicity of this schedule represented in days.

hour.description: Periodicity of this schedule represented in hours.

minute.description: Periodicity of this schedule represented in minutes.

persistence_type.description: Enable schedule persistence across device reboots.

schedule_type.description: Type of the schedule. 'calendar'   : Triggered at a specific calendar date and time. 'one-shot'   : Triggered only once at a specific calendar date and time. 'periodic'   : Triggered at specific periodic intervals.

start_date.description: Specify the start date in format YYYY-MM-DD for the schedule.

status.description: Status of the schedule. `active`    : Schedule is active `inactive`  : Schedule is not started yet `expired`   : Schedule is expired or the *count* is reached. `failed`    : Schedule is failed

time.description: Specify the time in HH:MM format. This indicates the schedule time, if the schedule type is set to 'calendar' or 'one-shot'. And this indicates the start time, if the schedule type is set to 'periodic'. Note that 'time' needs to be specified in conjunction with either 'days_of_month' or 'days_of_week' if the schedule type is set to 'calendar'. And 'time' needs to be specified in conjunction with 'periodicity', if the schedule type is set to 'periodic'.

trigger_count.description: Number of times this schedule has been triggered.

SNMP_oid.description: The object identifier to be monitored. Only variables that resolve to an ASN.1 primitive type of INTEGER (INTEGER, Integer32,Counter32, Counter64, Gauge32, or TimeTicks) will be monitored.

absolute_value.description: The value of the variable at the end of the sampling period.

delta_value.description: The delta of the variable between the beginning and the end of the sampling period. Applicable only for the sample type 'delta'.

falling_threshold.description: Falling threshold to be compared against the current value to trigger the SNMP alarm.

index.description:
Reference Resource: [SNMP_Alarm](#/SNMP_Alarm)
An index that uniquely identifies the SNMP alarm.

interval.description: The interval in seconds, over which the SNMP_oid is sampled and compared with the rising and falling thresholds.

last_update_time.description: Time (in seconds from epoch) when the last sample was processed.

rising_threshold.description: Rising threshold to be compared against the current value to trigger the SNMP alarm.

sample_type.description: The method of sampling of the variable. 'absolute': Absolute value of the variable will be compared             with the thresholds. 'delta':    The difference between the current and previous             sample of the variable will be compared with the thresholds.

state.description: Current state of the alarm: 'rising':  Value has once crossed the rising threshold and            is still above the falling threshold. 'falling': Value has once crossed the falling threshold and            is still below the rising threshold. 'off':     Value neither crossed the falling nor the rising threshold.

status.description: The status of this alarm entry 'valid':          SNMP_oid is valid. 'invalid':        SNMP_oid is invalid. 'under_creation': Initial state when configuring alarm entry.

port_inconsistent.description: This represents information regarding STP instance port level inconsistency.

bpdu_guard.description: Indicates whether BPDU guard finds the port inconsistent.

loop_guard.description: Indicates whether LOOP guard finds the port inconsistent.

pvid_mismatch.description: Indicates whether PVID-mismatch check finds the port inconsistent.

root_guard.description: Indicates whether ROOT guard finds the port inconsistent.

rpvst_guard.description: Indicates whether RPVST guard finds the port inconsistent.

port_priority.description: The priority value used along with the switch MAC address to determine which device is root. Configured as a multiple of 16. The lower a priority value, the higher the priority. For LAGs, the default is 4. For other interfaces the default is 8

port_role.description: The role of the port in the active Spanning tree topology. The possible port roles and their definitons are: 'Root' port provides the best path (lowest cost) when the switch forwards packets to the root bridge. 'Designated' port connects to the designated switch, which incurs the lowest path cost when  forwarding packets from that LAN to the root bridge. The port through which the designated switch  is attached to the LAN is called the designated port. 'Alternate' port offers an alternate path towards the root bridge to the one provided by the current root port. 'Backup' port acts as a backup for the path provided by a designated port towards the leaves of the  spanning tree. 'Conductor' (MSTP only) port provides the best possible path to reach the common internal spanning-tree (CIST) root  bridge from any MSTP region. 'Disabled' port has no role within the operation of the spanning tree.

port_state.description: The state of the port in the active topology. The possible port states and their definitons are: 'Blocking' means the Layer 2 LAN port does not participate in frame forwarding. 'Learning' means the Layer 2 LAN port prepares to participate in frame forwarding. 'Forwarding' means the Layer 2 LAN port forwards frames. 'Disabled' means the Layer 2 LAN port does not participate in STP and is not forwarding frames.

reset_at.description: Epoch time of the last port reset.

forward_transition_count.description: The number of times this port has transitioned to the forwarding state.

data_plane_state.description: Current data plane state of the subsystem row including all the possible initialization and failover phases. Valid values are: `uninitialized`:                  Subsystem is not yet initialized. `initializing_local_data_plane`:  Subsystem is performing initialization process. `waiting_for_control_plane`:      Subsystem is waiting to be connected to the control plane. `connecting_control_plane`:       Subsystem is connecting to the control plane for initialization or failover. `control_plane_connected`:        Subsystem has already established a connection to the control plane. `initialized`:                    Subsystem has completed its initialization process. `connecting_self_to_others`:      Subsystem is connecting to other ready subsystems. `first_run`:                      Subsystem is applying system configuration. `running`:                        Subsystem is available for all the system. `reconfiguring`:                  Subsystem is executing split port reconfiguration. `reconfigured`:                   Subsystem has completed split port reconfiguration. `recovery`:                       Subsystem is undergoing an error recovery. `remote_recovery:`                Subsystem is processing a recovery from a remote subsystem `enhanced_recovering`:            Subsystem is undergoing an enhanced recovery `disconnecting_self_from_others`: Subsystem's configuration is being removed from other ready subsystems. `warmbooting`:                    Subsystem is preparing failover caches `ready_for_failover`:             Subsystem is ready to apply failover caches. `sweeping`:                       Subsystem is applying sweep configuration. `error`:                          Subsystem is in failure condition, when it is connected to other subsystems.                                   Failure details are given in the data_plane_error field `crash`:                          Subsystem is in failure condition, when it isn't connected to other subsystems. `down`:                           Subsystem is being shutdown and it has been deinitialized.

interface_group_applied_speed.description: The applied speed setting for each interface group used by this  subsystem.

interface_group_default_speed.description: The default speed setting for each interface group that does not  have a value configured in `interface_group_speed`. Note that not  all defined group and speed names are used on all subsystems. Only  groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info` are used on a  given subsystem.

interface_group_info.description: The set of link speeds that are valid for each interface group speed  setting. The values are comma-separated lists of speeds in megabits  per second, for example, `10000,25000`. Note that not all defined  group and speed names are available on all subsystems.

interface_group_speed.description: The allowed link speeds configuration for each interface group of a  subsystem.    Interface groups are blocks of ports for which only a subset of link  speeds are usable at the same time due to hardware limitations. For  example, a group of ports might support 10 Gbps and 25 Gbps  transceivers, but not at the same time. When configured for `25g`,  any ports in the group with a 10 Gbps transceiver inserted cannot  link.    Groups are configured with a name describing a subset of link  speeds. The speeds allowed by each name are defined by  `interface_group_info`. Groups with no configuration default to the  name defined in `interface_group_default_speed`. The currently  applied name is available in `interface_group_applied_speed`.    Note that not all defined group and speed names are available on all  subsystems. Only groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info`  are used on a given subsystem. Any configured groups not listed are  not used by the subsystem and are ignored. Groups configured with a  speed setting that is not valid for the subsystem use the default  instead.

pac_gbp_init_status.description: This enum is used to represent the initialization status of a line card subsystem from the group based policy feature perspective. 'none':    subsystem is still initializing. 'success': group based policy is successfully applied on            the line card subsystem during initialization or there            is no group based policy on the line card subsystem. 'failure': group based policy is not successfully applied            on the line card subsystem during initialization.

part_number_cfg.description: User configurable part number for the subsystem.  When this column is empty:  + The subsystem is not explicitly configured yet and any compatible, supported subsystem is allowed to boot. + If an existing subsystem is physically replaced with a subsystem of a different part number, the interfaces associated with the existing subsystem will be removed prior to adding interfaces of the newly inserted subsystem.  When this column is configured with a part number:  + The subsystem is explicitly configured to only allow a subsystem with that specific part number to boot. + Physically replacing the existing subsystem with a subsystem of a different part number will require adjusting this column to match the new subsystem. Otherwise subsystem won't boot. + To configure the device for a new subsystem, the user can change this column with a different part number.  The interfaces associated with the existing subsystem will be removed and the interfaces of the specified subsystem part number will be created.

poe_persistency_disable.description: PoE persistency configuration for this subsystem. Persistent PoE provides the ability to continue power delivery during a soft reboot of the switch. This feature is applicable to subsystems of type `chassis` in non-modular switches, and to subsystems of type `line-card` in modular switches. This configuration is ignored on a non-PoE capable subsystems.

poe_power.description: Power fields for PoE from power supply for chassis subsystem.

available_power.description: Quantum of power, in Watts in the switch available for PoE power delivery. This power is available only for subsystems of type `chassis` as power supplies are associated with chassis subsystem.

drawn_power.description: Quantum of power, in Watts, actually drawn by all the Powered Devices connected to the chassis subsystem.

failover_power.description: Quantum of power, in Watts, in the switch available for PoE power delivery when a single power supply failure happens. Failover power is avaialble only for subsystems of type `chassis` as power supplies are associated with chassis subsystem.

reserved_power.description: Quantum of power, in Watts, allocated by PoE to all the Powered Devices connected to the chassis subsystem.

endurance.description: Indicates the average wear out of the storage part as a percentage  of its maximum estimated lifetime.

endurance_step_size.description: Indicates the step increment at which the endurance values are reported.

storage_health.description: Indicates the current storage health status.  `not_reported`      : Component does not report its health.  `normal`            : Component is operationally healthy.  `health_alert`      : Component is approaching the end of its estimated useful life.  `failure_imminent`  : Component has reached the end of its estimated useful life.  `failed`            : Component has failed.

temp_sensors.description:
Reference Resource: [Temp_sensor](#/Temp_sensor)
References to the temperature sensors which are part of this subsystem.

thermal_state.description: Temperature status of this subsystem: 'safe':     Normal operating temperature conditions.  All sensors             associated with this subsystem are within nominal             range. 'nodata':   Subsystem is initializing and awaiting temperature             state or there is no temperature data acquired for             the subsystem.  This is the default value set during             initialization. 'emergency': Temperature has reached a critical level that will              result in a hardware shutdown. 'critical': Temperature has reached a critical level and it is             recommended to take an immediate action. 'overtemp': Temperature has reached an over temperature condition             and it is recommended to take action if the             temperature does not return to the safe operating             conditions after a time.  The amount of time is             dependent upon the HW configuration. 'low':      Temperature has reached a low temperature condition             and it is recommended to take action if the             temperature does not return to the safe operating             conditions after a time.  The amount of time is             dependent upon the HW configuration. 'crit_low': Temperature has reached a low critical level and it             is recommended to take an immediate action. 'low_emergency': Temperature has reach a low critical level that will                  result in a hardware shutdown. Indicates whether the subsystem is within normal operating temperature ranges or if an action is required to prevent damage to the HW.

usb_status.description: Current USB port status: `disabled`:       The USB port is disabled. `empty`:          The USB port is enabled and no device is inserted. `unknown_device`: The USB port is enabled and an unknown device is inserted. `mass_storage`:   The USB port is enabled and a USB mass storage device is inserted. `bluetooth`:      The USB port is enabled and a USB Bluetooth adapter is inserted.

acl_init_status.description: This enum is used to represent the initialization status of a line card subsystem from the ACL feature perspective. 'none':    subsystem is still initializing. 'success': ACL is successfully applied on            the line card subsystem during initialization or            there is no ACL on the line card subsystem. 'failure': ACL is not successfully applied            on the line card subsystem during initialization.

admin_state.description: User configurable admin state of the subsystem. Valid values are:  + __diagnostic__:   Put the subsystem into diagnostic mode. + __down__:   Disable/power down the subsystem. + __up__:   Enable/power on the subsystem.

airflow_direction.description: Type of system airflow. Valid values are: F2B: Front to Back B2F: Back to Front

bist_passed.description: BIST test result: `true`   : Early BIST passed. `false`  : Early BIST failed.

reason.description: Boot reason history. Management module role active, standby subsystem types to store the last 4 reboot reasons and line card subsystem type to store the last 6 reboot reasons. Applicable to management module and line card subsystem types only. In VSF stack conductor, standby and members to store the last 4 reboot reasons.

timestamp.description: The timestamp for each boot-reason, represented in human readable format.

capacities.description: This specifies the set of capacities.

psu_slots.description: Number of power supply slots in a system.

redundant_fantrays.description: Number of fan trays in a system that can be lost and not considered as fault: 0 = No fan tray redundancy 1 = N+1 fan tray redundancy 2 = N+2 fan tray redundancy and so on

control_plane_target_state.description: Defines the state of the data plane control state machine Valid values are: `undetermined`:    Management module state unknown or unnassigned role `not_ready`:       Management module role active and in ready state.                     All associated data planes in 'absent' state `running_active`:  Management module role active and in ready state.                     Any associated data plane in 'steady' state `reconfigure_port`:Management module role reconfigure for split port reconfiguration. `insert_remove`:   Any associated data plane updating connections. data_plane_state.description: Current data plane state of the subsystem row including all the possible initialization and failover phases. Valid values are: `uninitialized`:                  Subsystem is not yet initialized. `initializing_local_data_plane`:  Subsystem is performing initialization process. `waiting_for_control_plane`:      Subsystem is waiting to be connected to the control plane. `connecting_control_plane`:       Subsystem is connecting to the control plane for initialization or failover. `control_plane_connected`:        Subsystem has already established a connection to the control plane. `initialized`:                    Subsystem has completed its initialization process. `connecting_self_to_others`:      Subsystem is connecting to other ready subsystems. `first_run`:                      Subsystem is applying system configuration. `running`:                        Subsystem is available for all the system. `reconfiguring`:                  Subsystem is executing split port reconfiguration. `reconfigured`:                   Subsystem has completed split port reconfiguration. `recovery`:                       Subsystem is undergoing an error recovery. `remote_recovery:`                Subsystem is processing a recovery from a remote subsystem `enhanced_recovering`:            Subsystem is undergoing an enhanced recovery `disconnecting_self_from_others`: Subsystem's configuration is being removed from other ready subsystems. `warmbooting`:                    Subsystem is preparing failover caches `ready_for_failover`:             Subsystem is ready to apply failover caches. `sweeping`:                       Subsystem is applying sweep configuration. `error`:                          Subsystem is in failure condition, when it is connected to other subsystems. interface_group_applied_speed.description: The applied speed setting for each interface group used by this  subsystem.

interface_group_default_speed.description: The default speed setting for each interface group that does not  have a value configured in `interface_group_speed`. Note that not  all defined group and speed names are used on all subsystems. Only  groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info` are used on a  given subsystem.

interface_group_info.description: The set of link speeds that are valid for each interface group speed  setting. The values are comma-separated lists of speeds in megabits  per second, for example, `10000,25000`. Note that not all defined  group and speed names are available on all subsystems.

interface_group_speed.description: The allowed link speeds configuration for each interface group of a  subsystem.    Interface groups are blocks of ports for which only a subset of link  speeds are usable at the same time due to hardware limitations. For  example, a group of ports might support 10 Gbps and 25 Gbps  transceivers, but not at the same time. When configured for `25g`,  any ports in the group with a 10 Gbps transceiver inserted cannot  link.    Groups are configured with a name describing a subset of link  speeds. The speeds allowed by each name are defined by  `interface_group_info`. Groups with no configuration default to the  name defined in `interface_group_default_speed`. The currently  applied name is available in `interface_group_applied_speed`.    Note that not all defined group and speed names are available on all  subsystems. Only groups and speeds listed in `interface_group_info`  are used on a given subsystem. Any configured groups not listed are  not used by the subsystem and are ignored. Groups configured with a  speed setting that is not valid for the subsystem use the default  instead.

pac_gbp_init_status.description: This enum is used to represent the initialization status of a line card subsystem from the group based policy feature perspective. 'none':    subsystem is still initializing. 'success': group based policy is successfully applied on            the line card subsystem during initialization or there            is no group based policy on the line card subsystem. 'failure': group based policy is not successfully applied            on the line card subsystem during initialization.

part_number_cfg.description: User configurable part number for the subsystem.  When this column is empty:  + The subsystem is not explicitly configured yet and any compatible, supported subsystem is allowed to boot. + If an existing subsystem is physically replaced with a subsystem of a different part number, the interfaces associated with the existing subsystem will be removed prior to adding interfaces of the newly inserted subsystem.  When this column is configured with a part number:  + The subsystem is explicitly configured to only allow a subsystem with that specific part number to boot. + Physically replacing the existing subsystem with a subsystem of a different part number will require adjusting this column to match the new subsystem. Otherwise subsystem won't boot. + To configure the device for a new subsystem, the user can change this column with a different part number.  The interfaces associated with the existing subsystem will be removed and the interfaces of the specified subsystem part number will be created.

poe_persistency_disable.description: PoE persistency configuration for this subsystem. Persistent PoE provides the ability to continue power delivery during a soft reboot of the switch. This feature is applicable to subsystems of type `chassis` in non-modular switches, and to subsystems of type `line-card` in modular switches. This configuration is ignored on a non-PoE capable subsystems.

poe_power.description: Power fields for PoE from power supply for chassis subsystem.

available_power.description: Quantum of power, in Watts in the switch available for PoE power delivery. This power is available only for subsystems of type `chassis` as power supplies are associated with chassis subsystem.

drawn_power.description: Quantum of power, in Watts, actually drawn by all the Powered Devices connected to the chassis subsystem.

'failure': policy is not successfully applied            on the line card subsystem during initialization.

thermal_state.description: Temperature status of this subsystem: 'safe':     Normal operating temperature conditions.  All sensors             associated with this subsystem are within nominal             range. 'nodata':   Subsystem is initializing and awaiting temperature             state or there is no temperature data acquired for             the subsystem.  This is the default value set during             initialization. 'emergency': Temperature has reached a critical level that will              result in a hardware shutdown. 'critical': Temperature has reached a critical level and it is             recommended to take an immediate action. 'overtemp': Temperature has reached an over temperature condition             and it is recommended to take action if the             temperature does not return to the safe operating             conditions after a time.  The amount of time is             dependent upon the HW configuration. 'low':      Temperature has reached a low temperature condition             and it is recommended to take action if the             temperature does not return to the safe operating             conditions after a time.  The amount of time is             dependent upon the HW configuration. 'crit_low': Temperature has reached a low critical level and it             is recommended to take an immediate action. 'low_emergency': Temperature has reach a low critical level that will                  result in a hardware shutdown. Indicates whether the subsystem is within normal operating temperature ranges or if an action is required to prevent damage to the HW.

This feature is applicable to subsystems of type `chassis` in non-modular switches, and to subsystems of type `line-card` in modular switches. This configuration is ignored on a non-PoE capable subsystems.

power_consumed_average_period.description: The sampling period for average consumed power in seconds.

quick_poe.description: Quick PoE configuration for this subsystem. Quick PoE provides the ability for the switch (PSE) to power up connected PDs soon after a cold reboot. This feature is applicable to subsystems of type `chassis` in non-modular switches, and to subsystems of type `line-card` in modular switches. This configuration is ignored on non-PoE capable subsystems.

reset.description: Resets the subsystem when set to true.

selftest_disable.description: Specify *true* to disable and *false* to enable  for the respective sub system

accounting_fail_through.description: This determines whether to access the next remote AAA server in case accounting is not recorded with the current server, the accounting will be attempted with the next configured server. If true, the next server in line will be accessed. If false, accounting will not be attempted with the next server.

authorization_fail_through.description: This determines whether to access the next remote AAA server in case of failure with the current server, the authorization will be attempted with the next configured server. If true, the next server in line will be accessed. If false, authorization will not be attempted with the next server.

console_lockout_time.description: Lock out time (in seconds) of user for console access after the failure for the number of attempts mentioned in failed console login attempts. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

console_login_attempts.description: Maximum failed console login attempts. If no value is set, the default is no limit on console login attempts. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

dot1x_radius_server_group.description: RADIUS server group to use for 802.1x authentication.

dot1x_remote_auth_method.description: Remote authentication method to be used by  the 802.1x authenticator: `eap-radius`:  extensible authentication protocol.

eap_tls_fragment_size_towards_server.description: Maximum size in bytes of an EAP-TLS fragment encoded in a  single RADIUS request packet.

fail_through.description: This determines whether to access the next remote AAA server in case of an authentication failure from the current one If true, the next server in line will be accessed. If false, the authentication process will be aborted at the first instance of an authentication failure.

login_lockout_time.description: Length (in seconds) of user lockout after too many failed login attempts. This value has no effect unless max login attempts is set. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

mac_auth_address_format.description: The MAC address format to be used in the RADIUS request messages  for MAC authentication.  `no-delimiter`            : aabbccddeeff  `single-dash`             : aabbcc-ddeeff  `multi-dash`              : aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff  `multi-colon`             : aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff  `no-delimiter-uppercase`  : AABBCCDDEEFF  `single-dash-uppercase`   : AABBCC-DDEEFF  `multi-dash-uppercase`    : AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF  `multi-colon-uppercase`   : AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.

mac_auth_password.description: The password to be used for MAC authentication in  the RADIUS request messages.

mac_auth_radius_auth_method.description: The type of Radius authentication method to use for MAC authentication: `CHAP`: challenge-handshake authentication protocol over RADIUS. `PAP`:  password authentication protocol over RADIUS.

mac_auth_radius_server_group.description: RADIUS server group to use for MAC authentication.

max_login_attempts.description: Maximum failed login attempts. If no value is set, the default is no limit on login attempts. This value will not be honored if RADIUS or TACACS+ authentication is enabled.

portaccess_accounting_radius_server_grou.description: RADIUS server group that this device will send accounting updates to.

portaccess_local_accounting_enable.description: Enables local accounting for portaccess clients in the system.

privilege_elevation.description: Indicates whether the privilege elevation method is enabled for login access to the switch for adminstrator users.

radius_auth.description: Specifies encoding to be used for the user password for radius based authentication.

radius_dns_query_interval.description: Specifies the interval, in seconds, between DNS requests sent from the switch to the DNS server to resolve the RADIUS FQDN address. This is only applicable when `radius_dns_query_mode` is set to 'fixed'.

radius_dns_query_mode.description: Specifies the DNS query mode.  `backoff`: The DNS interval is determined by an exponential             backoff algorithm. The query interval starts at             1 second and is doubled after every 20 unsuccessful             retries until the interval reaches 60 seconds.             i.e., the query intervals would be 1, 2, 4, 8,             16, 32, 60 with 20 attempts at each interval until             it reaches 60.  `fixed`:   The DNS query is sent at a fixed interval defined             in `radius_dns_query_interval`.

radius_dns_refresh_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds to wait before the switch refreshes its DNS cache for RADIUS servers and Dynamic authorization clients configured with a FQDN address.

radius_passkey.description: Specifies the shared secret key between the RADIUS client and the RADIUS server.

radius_retries.description: Specifies the number of retries to radius server if there is no response.

radius_service_type_in_access_req.description: Specifies if the Service-Type attribute must be included  in RADIUS Access-Request packets.

radius_timeout.description: Specifies the timeout interval in seconds that the switch waits for response from the RADIUS server before declaring a timeout failure.

radius_tls_initial_connection_timeout.description: RADIUS over TLS initial connection timeout in seconds.

radius_tls_timeout.description: RADIUS over TLS server response timeout in seconds.

radius_tracking_max_retries.description: Specifies the Maximum number of requests to be sent for tracking on retry. If not specified, then 'radius_retries' will be used.

radius_tracking_password.description: Specifies the password to be passed in the Access-Request packet for RADIUS server tracking.

radius_tracking_time_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds between the status requests to the server.

radius_tracking_user_name.description: Specifies the user name to be passed in the Access-Request packet for RADIUS server tracking.

status_server_message_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds between consecutive status messages sent to the server.

tacacs_auth.description: Specifies encoding to be used for the user password for tacacs+ authentication.

tacacs_passkey.description: Specifies the shared secret key between the TACACS+ client and the TACACS+ server.

tacacs_single_connection_disable.description: Disable single-connection mode between switch and TACACS+ server.

tacacs_timeout.description: Specifies the timeout interval in seconds that the switch waits for response from the TACACS+ server before declaring a timeout failure.

tacacs_tracking_password.description: Specifies the password to be used in the authentication START packet for TACACS+ server tracking.

tacacs_tracking_time_interval.description: Specifies the time interval in seconds between the status requests to the server.

tacacs_tracking_user_name.description: Specifies the user name to be used in the authentication START packet for TACACS+ server tracking.

admin_password_set.description: Indicates whether admin password has ever been set.

all_user_copp_policies.description:
Reference Resource: [CoPP_Policy](#/CoPP_Policy)
List of all user-defined CoPP policies in the system. The existence of a policy in this list is not an indication that it has been applied.

applied_copp_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [CoPP_Policy](#/CoPP_Policy)
Current, successfully applied top-level default CoPP policy, as identified in the [CoPP_Policy](#/CoPP_Policy).

applied_domain_name.description: Domain name that is being applied to the system. It might be sourced either from user configuration or through dhcp messages. If none of these are present the key itself ceases to exist. If both static configuration of domain name and DHCP based domain name are available, DHCP takes precedence.

applied_hostname.description: Hostname that is being applied to the system. It might be sourced either from configuration 'hostname' attribute or from DHCP 'mgmt_intf_status.dhcp_hostname'. If both static configuration of hostname and DHCP based hostname are available, DHCP takes precedence.

timeout.description: ARP aging timeout in seconds. Defines how many seconds a MAC address remains active in the MAC address table.

available_profiles.description: Profiles that are available in the system.

bfd_detect_multiplier.description: The number of negotiated min_rx_intervals that can occur before a BFD session is considered to be down.

bfd_enable.description: Specifies whether the BFD protocol is enabled or not on the system.

bfd_min_echo_rx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can receive BFD control messages. Remote endpoints may send messages at a slower rate. The value 0 means that the system does not want to receive BFD echo packets. The range from [1-49] is invalid.

bfd_min_rx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can receive BFD control messages. Remote endpoints may send messages at a slower rate.

bfd_min_tx_interval.description: The shortest interval, in milliseconds, at which BFD sessions can transmit BFD control messages. Messages will actually be transmitted at a slower rate if the remote endpoints cannot receive them as quickly as specified.

bluetooth_mgmt_clients.description: Information about clients connected to the switch via Bluetooth.

connect_time.description: Time the client connected, represented in seconds since  1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

device_name.description: Name provided by the connected client.

ipv4_address.description: The IPv4 address assigned to the client.

bluetooth_mgmt_disable.description: Disables Bluetooth management. When disabled, Bluetooth adapters  inserted into the USB port of the switch will not be detected  and will not work. If the USB port is disabled via usb_disable,  then this setting will have no effect.

bluetooth_mgmt_status.description: Bluetooth wireless management information for the switch.

device_name.description: The device name of the switch. This name is broadcast for  the Bluetooth pairing process.

ipv4_address.description: The IPv4 address for managing the switch over Bluetooth.

mac_address.description: The MAC address of the Bluetooth adapter.

boot_id_sd_128.description: The unique 128-bit boot ID of the executing kernel calculated for the initial system boot. If the value of this column is modified it indicates the switch has been rebooted or there has been a failover. The boot ID stored here will update on failover events.

boot_time.description: Boot time of the machine, represented in seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. OVSDB integers are 64 bit, which means it will take some time until we roll over.

capabilities.description: * `4pair_poe_90w`: Supports full 4pair power upto 90W Power Over Ethernet. * `4pair_poe_power`: Supports 4pair power upto 60W Power Over Ethernet. * `6in4_tunnel`: Supports 6in4 tunnels. * `6in6_tunnel`: Supports 6in6 tunnels. * `aaa_test_server`: Supports AAA test server feature. * `accounting_failthrough`: Supports failthrough for accounting * `active_gw_ext_mac`: Increases the number of active gateway MACs which matches the outer MAC DA only. * `active_gw_l3_src_mac`: Supports use of the virtual gateway MAC address as the source MAC for routed traffic. * `active_gw`: Supports active-gateway. * `aif`: supports Advanced Intelligent Forwarding(AIF) * `allow_unsupported_transceiver`: Supports allow-unsupported-transceiver mode. * `always_on_poe`: Supports delivering POE power to the PDs during device warm-boot. * `arp_ignore_subnet_match`: Supports ARP response for request with Src IP in different subnet. * `arpmgr_dont_use_dp_hit`: arpmgr doesn't use dp_hit schema value from Neighbor table. * `authorization_failthrough`: Supports failthrough for authorization * `authorize_only`: Supports authorize only feature * `avb`: Supports MSRP & FQTSS features for Audio Video Bridging. * `bfd_dynamic_egress_id_supported`: supports dynamic egress object allocation for BFD sessions * `bfd_fastpath_idl_supported`: supports BFD Fastpath IDL * `bfd_ipv4_echo_asic_accelerated`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv4 echo packets with ASIC acceleration * `bfd_ipv4_echo_global_source_address`: supports a global BFD echo source IP address * `bfd_ipv4_single_hop_async_asic_accelerated`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv4 single hop async packets with ASIC acceleration * `bfd_ipv4_single_hop_async_sw_supported`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv4 single hop async packets handled by software * `bfd_ipv4_single_hop_loopback_sw_supported`: supports async single-hop BFD sessions for IPv4 loopbacks handled by software * `bfd_ipv4_single_hop_vxlan_sw_supported`: supports async single-hop BFD sessions for IPv4 VxLAN handled by software * `bfd_ipv6_echo_asic_accelerated`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv6 echo packets with ASIC acceleration * `bfd_ipv6_single_hop_6in6_sw_supported`: supports async single-hop BFD sessions for 6in6 tunnels handled by software * `bfd_ipv6_single_hop_async_asic_accelerated`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv6 single hop async packets with ASIC acceleration * `bfd_ipv6_single_hop_async_sw_supported`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv6 single hop async packets handled by software * `bfd_ipv6_single_hop_loopback_sw_supported`: supports async single-hop BFD sessions for IPv4 loopbacks handled by software * `bfd_ipv6_single_hop_supported`: supports TX/RX of BFD IPv6 single hop * `bfd_session_protocol_bgp`: BFD of BGP sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_hsc`: BFD of HSC sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_ospf`: BFD of OSPF sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_ospfv3`: BFD of OSPFv3 sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_pim`: BFD of PIM sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_pimv6`: BFD of PIMv6 sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_static_routes`: BFD of Static Routes sessions supported * `bfd_session_protocol_vrrp`: BFD of VRRP sessions supported * `bfd`: supports Bidirectional Forwarding Detection protocol * `bgp_dynamic_peer`: Supports Dynamic BGP Peer. * `bgp_evpn_mfabric`: supports evpn multifabric feature. * `bgp_tcpao`: Supports Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) TCP Authentication option. * `bgp`: Supports Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). * `bidir_pim_bsr`: Support BSR protocol for BIDIR-PIM * `boot_history_visibility`: supports boot history information. * `bridge_normal_is_a_bond`: Bridge Normal should be treated as bond to switch cpu rx traffic to kernel. * `centralized_dataplane`: Supports centralized dataplane model. * `checkpoint_diff_deep`: Supports deep diff on checkpoint diff operations. * `classifier_ace_aarp`: supports access control entries that match on AARP EtherType. * `classifier_ace_ah`: supports access control entries that match on AH protocol. * `classifier_ace_appletalk`: supports access control entries that match on AppleTalk EtherType. * `classifier_ace_arp`: supports access control entries that match on ARP EtherType. * `classifier_ace_count`: supports access control entries with hitcounts enabled. * `classifier_ace_deny`: supports access control entries that deny packets. * `classifier_ace_dscp`: supports access control entries that match on DSCP values. * `classifier_ace_dst_l4_port_eq`: supports access control entries that match the specified destination L4 Port value. * `classifier_ace_dst_l4_port_groups`: supports access control entries that match on destination L4 Port groups. * `classifier_ace_dst_l4_port_gt`: supports access control entries that match greater than specified destination L4 Port value. * `classifier_ace_dst_l4_port_lt`: supports access control entries that match less than specified destination L4 Port value. * `classifier_ace_dst_l4_port_range`: supports access control entries that match on destination L4 Port ranges. * `classifier_ace_ecn`: supports access control entries that match on ECN values. * `classifier_ace_esp_egress`: supports access control entries that match on the ESP flag for egress. * `classifier_ace_esp`: supports access control entries that match on the ESP flag. * `classifier_ace_est`: supports access control entries that match on established TCP connections. * `classifier_ace_fcoe_init`: supports access control entries that match on FCoE Initialization EtherType. * `classifier_ace_fcoe`: supports access control entries that match on FCoE EtherType. * `classifier_ace_frg_egress`: supports access control entries that match IP fragments on egress. * `classifier_ace_frg`: supports access control entries that match IP fragments. * `classifier_ace_gre`: supports access control entries that match on GRE protocol. * `classifier_ace_icmp_type_code`: supports access control entries that match on ICMP code value. *
