mac_notify_enable.description: Enable the transmission of SNMP traps for MAC changes on this system (global enable).

mac_notify_interval.description: A queue mechanism is needed in this trap to throttle to amount of notifications goind out to the client at one time. The default wait time between notification being sent is 30 seconds but the user can specify an amount of time from 0-120 seconds.

snmp_agent_port.description: The port on which the SNMP agent listens for SNMP requests. The default port is 161.

snmp_historical_counters_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable the collection of historical interface statistics.

snmp_security_level.description: Enforces minimal security level for the SNMPv3 users. If  SNMPv3 user is configured not in compliance with this  provisioning, it will be operationally disabled.  'authPriv'     : users must be configured for both authentication and encryption 'authNoPriv'   : users must be configured for authentication, but privacy is optional 'noAuthNoPriv' : no restrictions on users configuration

snmpv3_engine_id.description: The SNMPv3 engine id in a colon separated hexadecimal  notation. Example 80:00:00:09:05:01:04:03:21 If not specified, local MAC will be used

stats-update-interval.description: Update interval for the statistics, in milliseconds. This option will affect the update of `statistics`, `DHCP-Relay Statistics` columns in the `Port` table, `statistics` column in the `Interface` table.  Default value is 5000 ms.

system_contact.description: This key represents the system contact.

system_description.description: This key represents the system description.

system_location.description: This key represents the system location.

tftp_server_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable TFTP server and set to `false` to disable it. If not set, TFTP server would be enabled.

tftp_server_secure.description: Set this value to `true` to enable TFTP secure mode and set to `false` to disable it. If not set, TFTP secure mode would be enabled. This config is valid only if TFTP server is enabled.

udp_bcast_forwarder_enabled.description: Set this value to `true` to enable UDP-Broadcast-Forwarder functionality globally and set it to `false` to disable it. UDP-Broadcast-Forwarder is disabled by default. If the key is missing, the configuration is assumed to be disabled. UDP-Broadcast-Forwarder port level configuration is present in [UDP_Bcast_Forwarder_Server](UDP_Bcast_Forwarder_Server).

vrrp_enable.description: Set this value to `true` to enable VRRP functionality globally and set it to `false` to disable it. VRRP is disabled by default.

vrrp_snmp_trap.description: Set this value to `false` to disable VRRP SNMP traps.

password_complexity.description: If password_complexity is 'enable'd, then minimal complexity rules would be enforced on all new passwords. Existing passwords are not affected.

adjacent_char_type_count.description: Enforce maximum number of adjacent character set in the new password i.e the maximum number of adjacent characters from the character set allowed in the password. The character set includes uppercase, lowercase, numeric and special characters. Default is zero(disabled)

enable.description: Enable complexity verification for new passwords.

history_count.description: Enforce minimal number of previous passwords that cannot be reused.

lowercase_count.description: Enforce minimal number of lowercase characters in the new password.

minimum_length.description: Enforce minimal length of the new passwords.

numeric_count.description: Enforce minimal number of numeric characters in the new passwords.

position_changes.description: Enforce minimal number of position changes for the new password.

special_char_count.description: Enforce minimal number of special characters in the new password.

uppercase_count.description: Enforce minimal number of uppercase characters in the new password.

poe_notification_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for Power-Over-Ethernet (POE) related events.

poe_threshold.description: Set the threshold in percent at which the system will send an excess power consumption notification trap.

policy_in_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [Policy](#/Policy)
Global Policy configuration for ingress direction. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

policy_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'policy_in_cfg'. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'policy_in_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

cache_replace_mode.description: Replacement mode to be applied when cache limit is reached and more clients have to be added to the cache. The possible cache replace modes, are none - Specifies cache entry can't be overwritten till expiry (default) FIFO - Specifies oldest cache entry can be replaced with new entry

cache_timeout.description: The period of time in hours for which an authenticated client's information will be cached.

enable.description: Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated role information. Clients are assigned to their previously authenticated role.

persistent_storage_enable.description: Enables writing cached client information to the device's persistent storage unit.

persistent_storage_write_interval.description: Interval between consecutive cached client information writes to persistent storage file in seconds. Flash write occurs only if there is a change in cached client's information.

port_access_client_move_secure_enable.description: Enable an authenticated client to move to a new port only post a successful authentication on the new port.

port_access_client_moves_disable.description: Disable MAC move between secure ports.

port_access_event_log_client_enable.description: Enable port-access event logs for client.

port_security_enable.description: Specifies whether the port security is enabled or not  on the system. 'true': enables port security configuration globally.         Though port security is enabled globally, the         functionality is effective only if port security         is also enabled on the port. 'false': disables port security configuration on the system.

port_security_trap_disable.description: Disable SNMP trap generation for port security violations.

portaccess_auto_vlan_enable.description: Enables automatic creation of a VLAN for portaccess clients  if the VLAN is not already available in the system.

ftp.description: Specify ftp proxy configuration. Example: ftp://proxy.example.com:8080 ftp://username:password@proxy-server-address:port

http.description: Specify http proxy configuration. Example: http://proxy.example.com:8080 http://username:password@proxy-server-address:port

https.description: Specify https proxy configuration. Example: https://proxy.example.com:8080 https://username:password@proxy-server-address:port

pvlan_share_hw_resource_enable.description: Enables the Private VLAN hardware resource sharing model.

q_profile_default.description: Specifies the name of queue profile (see [name](#/Q_Profile)) for ports  that do not specify their own queue profile (see [Port](#/Port)).  When missing or when the name refers to an incomplete/invalid queue-profile,  the factory-default profile will be used (i.e. the row in [Q_Profile](#/Q_Profile)  with hw_default set true). Check the value of the queue-profile key in  [qos_status](#/System) to determine the currently operating  queue-profile.

qos_trust.description: Specifies the QoS Trust Mode for ports that do not specify their own Trust Mode (see [Port](Port) qos_config column).  `none` - no fields are inspected on arriving packets. The initial local-priority and color meta-data values are taken  from the PCP 0 entry of the PCP-to-local-priority mapping (see [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry)).  `cos` - will use the PCP of the outermost 802.1 VLAN tag to index the  COS Map entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values  of the packet. For untagged packets, the initial local-priority and color  meta-data values are taken from the PCP 0 entry of the PCP-to-local-priority  mapping. (see [QoS_COS_Map_Entry](QoS_COS_Map_Entry)).  `dscp` - will use the DSCP value of IP packets to index the DSCP Map entry to initialize the local-priority and color meta-data values of the packet.  For non-IP packets, what meta-data values are assigned is hardware dependent.  If the key is not specified, then the system will use 'none'.

qos_default.description: Specifies the schedule profile for ports that do not specify their own schedule profile (see [Port](#/Port) qos column). When missing, the [QoS](#/QoS) row with [hw_default](#/QoS) true will be used.

qos_pool_priorities_mapping_config.description:
Reference Resource: [Qos_Pool](#/Qos_Pool)
The PCP-to-lossless-pool mapping for interfaces with Priority-Based Flow Control(PFC) enabled.

radius_dynamic_authorization.description: Global configuration for RADIUS dynamic authorization feature.

enable.description: Specifies whether the Dynamic authorization is enabled.

tcp_port.description: TCP port number used by the dynamic authorization server.

udp_port.description: UDP port number used by the dynamic authorization server.

redistribute_active_routes_only.description: Enable redistributing the active routes that have been selected for forwarding into the target routing protocol.

reset.description: Resets the system when set to true.

resource_utilization_poll_disable.description: When set to *true* system resource data polling is disabled.

resource_utilization_poll_interval.description: Specifies the polling interval in seconds for system resource  data polling

access_mode.description: The REST API access mode.  read-only  - only allow read operations. read-write - allow both read and write operations.

router_id_static.description: This determines whether the system global router-ID is configured statically or selected by Routing Manager dynamically. The default value is false.

router_id_val.description: The system global router identifier. Any routing protocol may pick up this as router id, if it doesn't have a specific one configured. The router-ID may be an IPv4 address of the router. It can be any arbitrary 32bit number. However it MUST be non-zero and unique within the entire Autonomus System domain.

rpvst_enabled_vlans.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
The VLANs on which RPVST is enabled.

secure_mode.description: Will reboot, zeroize system, and set secure mode to enhanced when set to true

selftest_fail_mode.description: The selftest operation mode.   `fail-safe`  : When the mode is configured as fail-safe, the                 switch will not block interfaces post a system                 boot while selftest is in-progress. However, if                 the switch is MACsec capable and MACsec selftest                 is enabled, the MACsec capable interfaces will                 be operationally blocked until selftest is                 completes successfully on the respectiv                 interface. If selftest fails, the switch will                 continue to operate and not go down for a reboot.  `fail-secure`: When the mode is configured as fail-secure, the                 switch will keep all the interfaces on the system                 including the management interface (OOBM)                 operationally done until all the forms of                 selftest complete successfully. If any of the                 selftest fails, the switch will be automatically                 rebooted.

serviceos_password_prompt_enable.description: Specifies whether the ServiceOS password prompt is enabled or not in the system. This is only applicable for ServiceOS starting with version 01.03.0001, ignored otherwise.

snmp_communities.description: Community strings to be used by the system when communicating over SNMPv1/SNMPv2c.

aaa_server_status.description: Enable SNMP trap for AAA server status related notifications.

snmp_trap_link_status_if_mib.description: When set to true, IF-MIB trap will be sent when interface link state changes.

snmp_trap_link_status_rmon.description: When set to true, RMON trap will be sent when interface link state changes.

snmp_unique_req_id_enable.description: When set to true, SNMP unique request-id check will be enabled.

ssh_certificate_as_authkey_enable.description: When enabled, SSH will enforce that the authenticating username  is present in the authenticating certificate's Common Name,  or Subject Alternative Name User Principal Name.

ssh_ciphers.description: This option specifies the SSH ciphers to use in priority order.  The key represents the priority and the value is the cipher to  configure at that priority level. No configuration here means  that the default ciphers and priorities will be configured:   1. chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com   2. aes128-ctr   3. aes192-ctr   4. aes256-ctr   5. aes128-gcm@openssh.com   6. aes256-gcm@openssh.com

ssh_hostkey_algorithms.description: This option specifies the SSH host key algorithms that are offered  by SSH in priority order. The key represents the priority and the  value is the host key algorithm to configure at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default host key  algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1. ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   2. ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   3. ecdsa-sha2-nistp521   4. ssh-ed25519   5. rsa-sha2-256   6. rsa-sha2-512   7. ssh-rsa

ssh_kex_algorithms.description: This option specifies the SSH key exchange algorithms to use in  priority order. The key represents the priority and the value  is the key exchange algorithm to configure at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default key  exchange algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1.  curve25519-sha256   2.  curve25519-sha256@libssh.org   3.  ecdh-sha2-nistp256   4.  ecdh-sha2-nistp384   5.  ecdh-sha2-nistp521

ssh_login_grace_time.description: Specifies the SSH login grace time (in seconds) before a  connection being authenticated is timed out and disconnected.

ssh_macs.description: This option specifies the SSH Message Authentication Codes  (MACs) to use in priority order. The key represents the  priority and the value is the MAC to be configured at that  priority level. No configuration here means that the default  MACs and priorities will be configured:   1.  hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com   2.  hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com   3.  hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com   4.  hmac-sha2-256   5.  hmac-sha2-512   6.  hmac-sha1

ssh_maximum_authentication_attempts.description: Specifies the maximum number of SSH authentication attemps permitted per connection.

ssh_passkeyauthentication_enable.description: Controls whether ssh password based authentication is enabled. This value will not be honored if two-factor authentication is enabled.

ssh_pubkey_algorithms.description: This option specifies the SSH public key algorithms to use in  priority order. The key represents the priority and the value  is the public key algorithm to be configured at that priority  level. No configuration here means that the default public key  algorithms and priorities will be configured:   1.  rsa-sha2-256   2.  rsa-sha2-512   3.  ssh-rsa   4.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   5.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   6.  ecdsa-sha2-nistp521   7.  ssh-ed25519   8.  x509v3-rsa2048-sha256   9.  x509v3-ssh-rsa   10. x509v3-sign-rsa   11. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256   12. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp384   13. x509v3-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521

ssh_publickeyauthentication_enable.description: Controls whether ssh public key authentication is enabled. This value will not be honored if two-factor authentication is enabled.

ssh_server_allowlist_enable.description: Controls whether the ssh server allow-list is enabled. When enabled, only configured hosts can connect to SSH servers of the switch.

ssh_server_allowlist_ips.description: Custom ssh server allow-list containing configured IPv4s and IPv6s.

ssh_server_port.description: Server port for all SSH servers on all VRFs where ssh server is  enabled.

ssh_twofactorauthentication_enable.description: This column can have one of the following settings: 'password': This means that authentication can only succeed with             successful certificate and password authentication. 'radius-authorize-only': This setting means that authentication                   will be done with a certificate followed by an                   authorization request to a RADIUS server 'disabled': Neither of the above configurations are enabled.

stp_config.description: This represents information regarding stp global configuration.

bpdu_guard_timeout.description: Time in seconds until when a port configured for BPDU-guard will be disabled upon receiving an STP BPDU. If bpdu_guard_timeout is not set, port will be in the disabled state forever.

extended_sysid_disable.description: System ID is kept as zero in the Bridge ID if this value is 'true'

forward_delay.description: The forward delay time in seconds for all the instances.

hello_time.description: The hello time in seconds for all the instances.

ignore_pvid_inconsistency_enable.description: Ignores PVID inconsistencies and allow RPVST to run on mismatched links if this value if 'true'.

max_age.description: The maximum-aging time in seconds (The time a device waits without receiving spanning tree configuration messages before attempting a reconfiguration) for all the instances.

max_hop_count.description: The maximum hop count for all the instances.

mstp_config_name.description: The MSTP configuration name configured by user. Default value is system MAC address.

mstp_config_revision.description: The MSTP configuration revision number configured by user.

path_cost_type.description: The operational value of the path cost type either long or short.

priority.description: The priority value configured as a multiple of 4096 The lower a priority value, the higher the priority.

rpvst_mstp_interconnect_vlan.description: VLAN used to interconnect an RPVST domain to an MSTP domain. This is only applicable if spanning tree is enabled on this device and the mode is set to RPVST.

stp_enable.description: Global knob to enable or disable Spanning Tree Protocol. Spanning Tree Protocol is enabled if this value is 'True'.

stp_mode.description: Spanning tree mode. The possible spanning tree modes are mstp  - Specify spanning tree to run in MSTP mode. rpvst - Specify spanning tree to run in Rapid PVST mode

tx_hold_count.description: The value used by the STP transmit state machine to limit the maximum transmission rate of BPDUs within the hello interval.

target.description: URL of the TFTP server to which supportlogs will be sent.  URL format: 'tftp://{IP|HOST}[:PORT][;blocksize=VAL]/FOLDER/'.

supportlog_rotate_vrf.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF over which the remote TFTP server (to transfer supportlogs) is to be reached. If not specified, default VRF is used. This column value can be empty.

syslog_audit_format_native.description: Enable sending audit log messages to the syslog server in Linux format. If it is not enabled, then it sends in ArubaOS-CX defined log format.

syslog_remote_facility.description: Facility to be used when forwarding to remote syslog servers.

syslog_remotes.description:
Reference Resource: [Syslog_Remote](#/Syslog_Remote)
List of syslog servers to which syslog messages will be forwarded. [Syslog_Remote](#/Syslog_Remote)

tcp_synack_retries.description: Number of times SYN-ACK packets are resent in response to a TCP  SYN request.

threshold_profile_default.description:
Reference Resource: [Threshold_Profile](#/Threshold_Profile)
Specifies the threshold-profile name for ports that do not specify their own profile (see [Port](#/Port) threshold_profile column).

timezone.description: User configured Timezone. Time zone of the device in case sensitive Posix format - "US/Pacific","Asia/Singapore", "Etc/GMT". Please refer to the full list of supported time zones at `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones`.

tls_certified_algorithms_only.description: Specifies whether TLS crypto algorithms should be restricted to  only those algorithms certified to Common Criteria NDcPP requirements.

tls_check_key_usage.description: enable the key usage check on a peer cert received during TLS handshake for client-auth or server-auth usage.

trunk_dynamic_vlan_include.description: Set to enable or disable a trunk port from automatically transmitting or receiving traffic for dynamic VLANs i.e., MVRP and PortAccess VLANs.

ubt_client_vid.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
VLAN-ID assigned to clients whose traffic is being redirected to the UBT cluster. This is not set when the UBT mode is set to VLAN-extend.

ubt_mode.description: UBT VLAN mode configuration:  `vlan-extend`: Clients are assigned to their UBT-role based                 VLAN in the hardware datapath. This mode allows                 for UBT to support VLAN-tagged clients like VOIP                 phones.  `local-vlan` : Clients are assigned to a VLAN that is local to                 the switch and associated with their UBT-role                 based VLAN when client traffic reaches the                 controller. This mode allows for reducing the                 number of VLANs that need to be instantiated on                 the switch but can only support VLAN-untagged UBT                 clients. The 'ubt_client_vid' will be used to                 specify the local_vlan that UBT clients are                 assigned to.

unicast_gr_disabled.description: The unicast_gr_disabled flag is used to indentify whether the Unicast GR feature enabled or not

usb_disable.description: Disable USB port. When disabled, devices inserted into the  USB port of the switch will not be detected and will not work.

virtual_mac.description: Global virtual MAC configuration. An example usage would be  EVPN Symmetric IRB where EVPN advertises this MAC as the Router's MAC for all the EVPN Symmetric Routes.

vlan_client_presence_detect.description: If enabled, VNI mapped VLANs will be 'UP' only if there are authenticated clients on this VLAN or have some statically configured ports as members and those ports are 'UP'. When not set, VNI mapped VLANs will always be 'UP'.

vsx.description:
Reference Resource: [VSX](#/VSX)
VSX configuration and status. If not configured, VSX functionality is disabled.

vsx_trap_enable.description: Enables sending SNMP traps for VSX events.

ztp_force_provision.description: Force ZTP based provisioning to run, ignoring the status of any previous ZTP operation.

Reference Resource: [Tacacs_Server](#/Tacacs_Server)
IPV4/IPV6 address or FQDN of the TACACS+ server.

auth_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of authentication packets communicated with the server.

auth_accepts.description: Number of Auth-Reply packets received from this server with status pass.

auth_challenge.description: Number of Auth-Reply packets received from this server asking for additional information.

auth_rejects.description: Number of Auth-Reply packets received from this server with status fail.

auth_reply_malformed.description: Number of malformed Auth-Reply packets received  from this server.

auth_start.description: Number of Auth-Start packets sent to this server.

dropped_pkt.description: Number of TACACS+ packets dropped from this server on the authentication port.

pending_requests.description: Number of Auth-Start packets destined for this server that have not yet timed out or received a response.

round_trip_time.description: Time interval between Auth-Start and the most recent Auth-Reply from this server.

timeout.description: Number of timed out Auth-Start packets destined for this server.

unknown_types.description: Number of TACACS+ packets of unknown type received from this server on the authentication port.

auth_type.description: Specifies the server specific authentication method (pap/chap) to be used. If not set, the globally configured authentication method (pap/chap) will be used.

default_group_priority.description: Specifies the order in which a TACACS+ server is configured within TACACS+ default family group 'tacacs' By default all TACACS+ servers should be added to default group 'tacacs' Priority is assigned starting with 1 and incremental. Servers with equal priority in the default family group will undergo similar tie-breaker algorithm as mentioned for the user defined server group

group.description:
Reference Resource: [AAA_Server_Group](#/AAA_Server_Group)
Specifies the TACACS+ server-group that it belongs to. This column is used to identify the user defined AAA server group this TACACS+ server belongs to

last_tracking_attempted_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when the most recent reachability tracking request was sent to the TACACS+ server.

last_tracking_status_changed_time.description: Time in seconds since Epoch when TACACS+ Server status last changed from reachable to unreachable or vice versa.

passkey.description: Specifies the shared secret key between the TACACS+ client and the TACACS+ server.  If not set, the globally configured passkey will be used.

reachability_status.description: Specifies the reachability of Configured TACACS+ Server. 'reachable':    tracking for this server is enabled and the                 server is reachable. 'unreachable':  tracking for this server is enabled and the                 server is not reachable. An empty value means the reachability of this server is unknown.

tcp_port.description:
Reference Resource: [Tacacs_Server](#/Tacacs_Server)
Specifies the tcp port number used for exchanging TACACS+ messages between the client and server.

timeout.description: Specifies the server specific timeout interval that the switch waits for response from the TACACS+ server before declaring a timeout failure. If not set, the globally configured timeout will be used.

tracking_enable.description: Specifies whether tracking should be enabled for this server (server tracking has to be enabled globally as well).

tracking_statistics.description: Contains key-value pairs that report the number of TACACS+ authentication START & REPLY packets that were communicated with the server for tracking purpose. These statistics will be updated periodically based on the global configuration tacacs_tracking_time_interval value.

authentication_requests.description: Number of TACACS+ authentication START packets sent to this server for tracking.

authentication_responses.description: Number of TACACS+ REPLY packets received from this server in response to tracking START packets

user_group_priority.description: Specifies the order in which TACACS+ servers are configured within a user defined server group. Priority is assigned starting with 1 and incremental. If not set, it means this server is not part of a user defined group, this will be empty. Servers where priority is not configured will be reached out last Servers with equal priority in a group will be reached out as follows: Those belonging to vrf where vrf_name appears alphabetically earlier than the others are reached out first. If that's a tie, servers with address appearing alphabetically earlier than the others is reached out first. If that too is a tie, servers with smaller tcp port are reached out first

Reference Resource: [Temp_sensor](#/Temp_sensor)
References to the temperature sensors which are part of this subsystem.

fan_state.description: Recommended minimum fan setting based on current temperature: 'normal': normal fan speed recommended 'medium': medium fan speed recommended 'fast':   fast fan speed recommended 'max':    recommend using the maximum fan speed The fan control process chooses the worst-case sensor when determining this value.

location.description: Descriptive text for the physical location of the temperature sensor relative to the subsystem.

name.description:
Reference Resource: [Temp_sensor](#/Temp_sensor)
Logical name of the temperature sensor, including the subsystem name and numeric identifier of the temperature sensor.

status.description: Results of evaluation of the current temperature against the sensor's threshold values: 'absent':        Sensor is not present or not accessible 'uninitialized': Sensor is not initialized 'initializing':  Sensor is initializing 'warning':       Sensor has encountered a non-critical fault event 'fault':         Sensor has encountered a fault event 'low_emergency': Sensor temperature is below the lowest expected threshold and will result in hardware shutdown 'low_critical':  Sensor temperature is below the lowest expected threshold 'low':           Sensor temperature is below the normal expected range but above the lowest expected threshold 'normal':        Sensor temperature is within the expected range 'overtemp':      Sensor temperature is above the normal expected range but below the highest expected threshold 'critical':      Sensor temperature is above the highest expected threshold 'emergency':     Sensor temperature is above the highest expected threshold and will result in hardware shutdown 'min':           **Deprecated** 'max':           **Deprecated**

temperature.description: Current temperature reading, in millidegrees Celsius.

type.description:
Reference Resource: [Time_Series](#/Time_Series)
Time series associated with the monitor. The possible time series are: 'Rate': When the monitored URI is wildcarded,this function finds the rate. 'Raw' : Regular raw data points in the time series. 'Count': This counts the number of distinct time-series that have been generated and implicitly reflects the 'count' of data points collected every scrape interval. 'Sum': When the monitored URI is wildcarded, this function sums over the current values of 'all' resources pointed to by expanding on the wildcard. 'Min/Max': When the monitored URI is wildcarded,these functions return the min/max of the current value of 'all' currently present resource pointed to by expanding on the wildcard. 'Average': This function performs an average over the current value of 'all' currently present resources pointed to by expanding on the wildcard. 'CountOverTime', 'SumOverTime', 'MinOverTime', 'MaxOverTime', 'AverageOverTime': When the keyword 'OverTime' follows one of the aggregators defined above,the function behaves in a similar way but performs its aggregation 'over' the specified time in the past instead of over the current value only. 'Count_Rate', 'Count_CountOverTime', 'Count_Sum', 'Count_SumOverTime', 'Count_Min', 'Count_MinOverTime', 'Count_Max', 'Count_MaxOverTime', 'Count_Average', 'Count_AverageOverTime', 'Sum_Rate', 'Sum_Count', 'Sum_CountOverTime', 'Sum_SumOverTime', 'Sum_Min', 'Sum_MinOverTime', 'Sum_Max', 'Sum_MaxOverTime', 'Sum_Average', 'Sum_AverageOverTime', 'Min_Rate', 'Min_Count', 'Min_CountOverTime', 'Min_Sum', 'Min_SumOverTime', 'Min_MinOverTime', 'Min_Max', 'Min_MaxOverTime', 'Min_Average', 'Min_AverageOverTime', 'Max_Rate', 'Max_Count', 'Max_CountOverTime', 'Max_Sum', 'Max_SumOverTime', 'Max_Min', 'Max_MinOverTime', 'Max_MaxOverTime', 'Max_Average', 'Max_AverageOverTime', 'Average_Rate', 'Average_Count', 'Average_CountOverTime', 'Average_Sum', 'Average_SumOverTime', 'Average_Min', 'Average_MinOverTime', 'Average_Max', 'Average_MaxOverTime', 'Average_AverageOverTime': Nested Aggregate Functions are when we combine functions to obtain the combined effect of the two functions, for example Sum(Rate(resource)) will initially compute the Rate then the Sum of the switch resource.

min_version.description: The minimum TLS version allowed:  'TLS1_2': TLS version 1.2 and above allowed.  'TLS1_3': TLS version 1.3 and above allowed.

tls1_2_cipher_suites.description: A map of TLS 1.2 cipher suites allowed and their priority  order. The map key is a priority level with priority_1  being the highest priority. The mapped value is a cipher suite  name. When a priority level is not configured, it maps to  its default cipher suite, as indicated below:    priority_1. TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.    priority_2. TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.    priority_3. TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.    priority_4. TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.    priority_5. TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.    priority_6. TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.  If users want to leave a priority level not mapping to any  cipher suite, not even the default suite, they should set the  priority level to map to 'NONE' explicitly. If two priority  levels are set to map to the same cipher suite, the cipher suite  will be assigned the higher priority level, and the lower  level will effectively map to 'NONE'.

tls1_3_cipher_suites.description: A map of TLS 1.3 cipher suites allowed and their priority  order. The map key is a priority level with priority_1  being the highest priority. The mapped value is a cipher suite  name. When a priority level is not configured, it maps to  its default cipher suite, as indicated below:    priority_1. TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.    priority_2. TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.    priority_3. TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256.    priority_4. TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256.    priority_5. TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256.  If users want to leave a priority level not mapping to any  cipher suite, not even the default suite, they should set the  priority level to map to 'NONE' explicitly. If two priority  levels are set to map to the same cipher suite, the cipher suite  will be assigned the higher priority level, and the lower  level will effectively map to 'NONE'.

tls_kex_algorithms.description: A map of TLS key exchange algorithms allowed and their  priority order. The map key is a priority level with  priority_1 being the highest priority. The mapped value is  an algorithm name. When a priority level is not configured,  it maps to its default algorithm, as indicated below:    priority_1. secp521r1.    priority_2. secp384r1.    priority_3. secp256r1.    priority_4. X25519.    priority_5. X448.    priority_6. ffdhe8192.    priority_7. ffdhe6144.    priority_8. ffdhe4096.    priority_9. ffdhe3072.    priority_10. ffdhe2048.  If users want to leave a priority level not mapping to any  algorithm, not even the default algorithm, they should set the  priority level to map to 'NONE' explicitly. If two priority  levels are set to map to the same cipher suite, the cipher suite  will be assigned the higher priority level, and the lower  level will effectively map to 'NONE'.

Get traceroute result to a destination.

inherit_rules.description:
Reference Resource: [User_Group](#/User_Group)
Provides the ability to inherit RBAC rules from another user group when performing local authorization. RBAC rules will be `prepended` to the rules configured for the current user group.

name.description:
Reference Resource: [User_Group](#/User_Group)
Name of the user group. Built-in user groups are as follows: `administrators`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 15. Members have access to: All the CLI commands and bash shell. All the REST Methods through REST APIs. `operators`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 1. Members have access to: All "show" CLI commands (except those that display sensitive information). All "GET" requests through REST APIs. `auditors`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 19. Members have access to: All "show" CLI commands to display and copy security logs. All "GET" requests for security logs through REST APIs. Only users belonging to the above three default groups will be allowed access to REST APIs.

origin.description: Indicator of whether the user group is built-in (system-defined) or configured. Unlike user configured user groups, built-in user groups cannot be modified or deleted. Users belonging to configured user groups won't have access to REST APIs.

rbac_rules.description:
Reference Resource: [RBAC_Rule_Entry](#/RBAC_Rule_Entry)
Role Based Access Control rules applicable to a user group. When local authorization is added to AAA authorization list, these rules will be traversed in an ascending order of the sequence number to find a rule that matches the user operation on the switch. The matching rule determines whether the user operation is allowed or denied. If no rule matches, user operation will be denied.

delete_macs_rejected.description:
Reference Resource: [MAC](#/MAC)
List of MACs rejected and rejection reason for delete request in delete_macs_requested.

delete_macs_requested.description:
Reference Resource: [MAC](#/MAC)
Key is reference to Dynamic MACs rows requested to be deleted on this VLAN. Eventually these MACs will be cleared from the system and delete_macs_requested will revert to an empty list. If the value is true, the MAC will be force deleted if the MAC was not learnt through data plane

description.description: User provided description of this VLAN.

dhcpv4_snooping_enable.description: Enables DHCPv4 Snooping feature on the VLAN. DHCPv4 Snooping is active on the Ports of the VLAN only if the feature is enabled on the VLAN and globally.

dhcpv4_snooping_guard_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCPv4_Snooping_Guard_Policy](#/DHCPv4_Snooping_Guard_Policy)
DHCPv4 Guard Policy for VLAN.

dhcpv4_snooping_ip_binding_disable.description: Disables learning of DHCPv4 Snooping binding entries. Only policy based packet inspection is performed.

dhcpv6_snooping_allow_bindings_on_truste.description: Allow binding entries to be learned on trusted port.

dhcpv6_snooping_enable.description: Enables DHCPv6 Snooping feature on the VLAN. DHCPv6 Snooping is active on the Ports of the VLAN only if the feature is enabled on the VLAN and globally.

dhcpv6_snooping_guard_policy.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCPv6_Snooping_Guard_Policy](#/DHCPv6_Snooping_Guard_Policy)
DHCPv6 Guard Policy for VLAN.

dhcpv6_dropped_due_to_access_list_error.description: Number of DHCPv6 server packets dropped on the VLAN due to access list error.

dhcpv6_dropped_due_to_prefix_list_error.description: Number of DHCPv6 server packets dropped on the VLAN due to prefix list error.

dhcpv6_dropped_due_to_server_preference_.description: Number of DHCPv6 server packets dropped on the VLAN due to server preference error.

dhcpv6_forwarded.description: Number of DHCPv6 server packets forwarded on the VLAN where DHCPv6 Guard Policy is enabled.

dhcpv6_received.description: Number of DHCPv6 server packets received on the VLAN, where DHCPv6 Guard Policy is enabled.

dhcpv6_snooping_ip_binding_disable.description: Disables learning of DHCPv6 Snooping binding entries. Only policy based packet inspection is performed.

flood_enabled_subsystems.description:
Reference Resource: [Subsystem](#/Subsystem)
Reference to a list of [Subsystem](#/Subsystem) where VLAN flooding is programmed for this VLAN.

id.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
The ID of this VLAN. Non-internal VLANs must have an 'id' between 1 and 4094 to be effectively instantiated.

internal_usage.description: The key-value pairs that represent how this VLAN is used internally by the system.

l3port.description: VLAN is used internally by ASIC to configure L3 behavior of the port. The value is the port name that uses this VLAN.

ubt.description: VLAN is used internally by UBT to assign to the tunneled clients. The value is 'ubt'.

ipv4_source_lockdown_enable.description: Enables the IP Lockdown feature on the VLAN. When set, IPv4 traffic from clients on ports of this VLAN will be forwarded only when there is an associated IP binding entry.

ipv6_destination_guard_enable.description: Enables IPv6 destination guard feature on the VLAN. IPv6 destination guard is active on the Ports of the VLAN only if the both DHCPv6 snooping and ND snooping features are enabled on the VLAN and globally.

dropped_statistics.description: Number of unknown destination IPv6 packets dropped

ipv6_source_lockdown_enable.description: Enables the IP Lockdown feature on the VLAN. When set, IPv6 traffic from clients on ports of this VLAN will be forwarded only when there is an associated IP binding entry.

macs_invalid.description: If `true`, indicates that MACs on this VLAN are invalid. This might be set by any agent of the system that decides that MACs are indeed invalid. Eventually those MACs will be cleared from the system and macs_invalid will revert to `false`.

mgmd_counters.description: Statistics for the VLAN. This field value could either be empty or explicitly set to 0 to indicate that the counter is 0.

igmp_acl_pkt_dropped_counter.description: Number of IGMP  packets dropped by ACL filter.

igmp_fast_leave_counter.description: Number of IGMP fast leaves happened on the VLAN.

igmp_forced_fast_leave_counter.description: Number of IGMP forced fast leaves happened on the VLAN.

igmp_membership_timeout_counter.description: Number of IGMP membership timeouts on the VLAN.

igmp_rx_bad_checksum_counter.description: Number of IGMP packets received with bad checksum on the VLAN.

igmp_rx_malformed_pkt_counter.description: Number of malformed IGMP packets received on the VLAN.

igmp_rx_mgmd_disabled_vlan_counter.description: Number of IGMP packets received on the VLAN where IGMP is not enabled.

igmp_rx_unknown_msg_type_counter.description: Number of unknown IGMP types received on the VLAN.

igmp_rx_v1_all_host_query_counter.description: Number of IGMPv1 all host query packets received on the VLAN.

igmp_rx_v1_member_report_counter.description: Number of IGMPv1 membership reports received on the VLAN.

igmp_rx_v2_all_host_query_counter.description: Number of IGMPv2 all host query packets received on the VLAN.

mld_tx_v2_group_specific_query_counter.description: Number of MLDv2 group specific query packets transmitted on the VLAN.

mgmd_dynamic_group_count.description: Count of dynamic groups in both the exclude and include mode on the VLAN.

igmp_exclude_mode.description: Count of dynamic IGMP groups in the exclude mode on the VLAN.

igmp_include_mode.description: Count of dynamic IGMP groups in the include mode on the VLAN.

mld_exclude_mode.description: Count of dynamic MLD groups in the exclude mode on the VLAN.

mld_include_mode.description: Count of dynamic MLD groups in the include mode on the VLAN.

mgmd_enable.description: Enable or disable IGMP/MLD on the VLAN. By default, IGMP/MLD is disabled on the VLAN.

name.description: User configurable VLAN name.

allow_bindings_on_trusted_ports.description: Allow binding entries to be learned on trusted port.

enable.description: Enables ND Snooping feature on the VLAN. ND Snooping is active on ports of the VLAN only if the feature is enabled at the system level and on the VLAN. This enables nd_guard and ra_guard by default.

nd_guard_enable.description: Enables ND-Guard feature on the VLAN. This takes effect only when Global and VLAN level ND Snooping is also enabled.

ra_drop_enable.description: Enables RA-drop feature on the VLAN. When enabled, RA packets received on the VLAN will be dropped regardless of whether they are received on ND Snooping 'trusted' or 'untrusted' ports. This takes effect only when ND Snooping is also enabled on the VLAN.

ra_guard_enable.description: Enables RA-guard feature on the VLAN. When enabled, RA(Router Advertisement) and RR(Router Redirect) packets received on the VLAN will be dropped on untrusted ports. This takes effect only when Global and VLAN level ND Snooping is also enabled.

ra_guard_log.description: Enables logging of RA(Router Advertisement)  and RR(Router Redirect) dropped packets. This takes effect only when ra_guard is enabled.

nd_snooping_prefix.description: List of network prefix ranges allowed on the VLAN. An ND packet with a source IP not matching any of the prefixes configured here will be dropped. If this is empty, source IP prefix validation is not performed.

oper_state_reason.description: Human readable reason for the operational state of this VLAN. error: Operational state is down due to an unknown reason. ok: Operational state is up for the VLAN. admin_down: VLAN is administratively down. no_member_port: No port is member of the VLAN. no_member_forwarding: No port is forwarding. private_vlan_violation: Private VLAN violation. pvlan_primary_down: Primary VLAN is operationally down.

Ignored if configured on VLANs with type = 'internal'. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

pvlan_association.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
Specifies the Primary VLAN associated with this secondary VLAN This is applicable to Secondary VLANs only. When pvlan_association is not set and pvlan_type is set, then considered as misconfiguration and brought down the VLAN.

pvlan_type.description: Specifies the VLAN's type in the context of Private VLAN. When not set, it will work as regular VLAN.

pvlan_violation_reason.description: Human readable reason for why Private vlan violation occurred  on the VLAN. The value will be populated only when there is a PVLAN misconfiguration. pvlan_default_vlan_join: Default VLAN is not allowed to join Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_erps_inst_pvlans_mismatch: ERPS instances must match for all VLANs in a Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_invalid_primary_association: Secondary VLAN is associated with an invalid Primary VLAN. pvlan_mstp_inst_pvlans_mismatch: MSTP instances must match for all VLANs in a Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_mvrp_cfg_both_present: MVRP and Private-VLAN are mutually exclusive features. pvlan_no_primary_association: No Primary VLAN has been configured for Secondary VLAN. pvlan_primary_vlan_limit_exceeded: Maximum number of Primary VLANs reached. pvlan_rpvst_cfg_both_present: RPVST and Private-VLAN are mutually exclusive features. pvlan_secondary_vlan_limit_exceeded: Maximum number of secondary VLANs reached. pvlan_smartlink_group_pvlans_mismatch: Smartlink groups must match for all VLANs in a Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_vt_cfg_both_present: VLAN translation and PVLAN are mutually exclusive features. secondary_vlan_svi_present: VLAN is a secondary VLAN with SVI configured. pvlan_primary_has_association: VLAN is a primary VLAN but associated to another VLAN.

ra_guard_policy.description:

RA Guard policy associated with this VLAN. RR/RA packets received on this VLAN will be inspected and permitted per the policy specification.

ra_dropped_due_to_access_list_error.description: Number of RA packets dropped on the VLAN due to access list error.

ra_dropped_due_to_hop_limit_error.description: Number of RA packets dropped on the VLAN due to hop limit error.

ra_dropped_due_to_manage_flag_error.description: Number of RA packets dropped on the VLAN due to manage flag error.

ra_dropped_due_to_other_flag_error.description: Number of RA packets dropped on the VLAN due to other flag error.

ra_dropped_due_to_prefix_list_error.description: Number of RA packets dropped on the VLAN due to prefix list error.

ra_dropped_due_to_router_preference_erro.description: Number of RA packets dropped on the VLAN due to router preference error.

ra_forwarded.description: Number of RA packets forwarded on the VLAN where RA Guard Policy enabled.

ra_received.description: Number of RA packets received on the VLAN, where  RA Guard Policy is enabled.

mgmd_dynamic_group_count.description: Count of dynamic groups in both the exclude and include mode on the VLAN.

igmp_exclude_mode.description: Count of dynamic IGMP groups in the exclude mode on the VLAN.

igmp_include_mode.description: Count of dynamic IGMP groups in the include mode on the VLAN.

mld_include_mode.description: Count of dynamic MLD groups in the include mode on the VLAN.

mgmd_enable.description: Enable or disable IGMP/MLD on the VLAN. By default, IGMP/MLD is disabled on the VLAN.

List of [Port](#/Port) in forward mode for IGMP. Instruct the device to forward incoming multicast packets received on the specified ports.

Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
The list of ports on which PIM routers are detected along with its expiry time in seconds. The expiry time is the time to expiry added with the system bootup time. The addition of system uptime ensures that the timer values don't need to be updated every clock tick.

mgmd_igmp_static_group_ports.description:

Specifies the list of ports for which Static join is configured for specific IPv4 multicast group and source address.

mgmd_igmp_static_groups.description: The list of IGMP static group IP addresses. The entries are stored in the Source_Group format.

mgmd_mld_block_ports.description:

mgmd_mld_static_group_ports.description:

mgmd_mld_version.description: The MLD protocol version to use. When IGMP snooping is disabled, this field would be empty.

mgmd_oper_version.description: MGMD protocol could run in a version different from the configured version. This happens when there is both VLAN and interface VLAN entries with MGMD snooping and MGMD enabled respectively. The version would be negotiated to the lower of the configured versions in both of them. The operational version for both the IGMP snooping and MLD snooping on the VLAN.

mgmd_querier_port.description:
Reference Resource: [Port](#/Port)
[Port](#/Port) on which querier is detected.

mgmd_querier_timer_info.description: Timer parameters learned from the querier in seconds. The querier detected and querier expiry time values are added with the system bootup time. The addition of system uptime ensures that the timer values don't need to be updated every clock tick.

igmp_querier_expiry_time.description: The time when the IGMP querier would be considered unavailable.

igmp_querier_query_interval.description: Query interval present in the IGMP querier's query packet.

Ingress ACL to filter processing of MGMD reports and leave messages received from hosts. When this is not configured, all MGMD reports and leave messages will be processed.

name.description: User configurable VLAN name.

allow_bindings_on_trusted_ports.description: Allow binding entries to be learned on trusted port.

enable.description: Enables ND Snooping feature on the VLAN. ND Snooping is active on ports of the VLAN only if the feature is enabled at the system level and on the VLAN. This enables nd_guard and ra_guard by default.

nd_guard_enable.description: Enables ND-Guard feature on the VLAN. This takes effect only when Global and VLAN level ND Snooping is also enabled.

ra_drop_enable.description: Enables RA-drop feature on the VLAN. When enabled, RA packets received on the VLAN will be dropped regardless of whether they are received on ND Snooping 'trusted' or 'untrusted' ports. This takes effect only when ND Snooping is also enabled on the VLAN.

ra_guard_enable.description: Enables RA-guard feature on the VLAN. When enabled, RA(Router Advertisement) and RR(Router Redirect) packets received on the VLAN will be dropped on untrusted ports. This takes effect only when Global and VLAN level ND Snooping is also enabled.

ra_guard_log.description: Enables logging of RA(Router Advertisement)  and RR(Router Redirect) dropped packets. This takes effect only when ra_guard is enabled.

nd_snooping_prefix.description: List of network prefix ranges allowed on the VLAN. An ND packet with a source IP not matching any of the prefixes configured here will be dropped. If this is empty, source IP prefix validation is not performed.

oper_state_reason.description: Human readable reason for the operational state of this VLAN. error: Operational state is down due to an unknown reason. ok: Operational state is up for the VLAN. admin_down: VLAN is administratively down. no_member_port: No port is member of the VLAN. no_member_forwarding: No port is forwarding. private_vlan_violation: Private VLAN violation. pvlan_primary_down: Primary VLAN is operationally down.

policy_in_applied.description:
Reference Resource: [Policy](#/Policy)
Current, successfully applied ingress Policy to this VLAN, as identified in the [Policy](#/Policy)

policy_in_cfg.description:

Ingress Classifier Policy, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to this VLAN, as identified in the [Policy](#/Policy). Ignored if configured on VLANs with type = 'internal'. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

policy_in_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'policy_in_cfg' column. This value is changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'policy_in_cfg' value. Ignored if configured on VLANs with type = 'internal'. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

policy_in_conform_rate.description: This is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. It is available at [Policy](#/Policy).

policy_in_data_plane_states.description:

Application status for each data_plane (line card).

policy_in_statistics.description: This is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. It is available at [Policy](#/Policy).

policy_in_status.description: The status of the last version of the 'policy_in_cfg', that has been processed.

code.description: Numeric error code.  Expected to be 0 when state is 'applied'

message.description: Detailed reason for error state.  Expected empty when state is 'applied'

version.description: The version of policy_in_cfg that corresponds to this status.

pvlan_association.description:
Reference Resource: [VLAN](#/VLAN)
Specifies the Primary VLAN associated with this secondary VLAN This is applicable to Secondary VLANs only. When pvlan_association is not set and pvlan_type is set, then considered as misconfiguration and brought down the VLAN.

pvlan_type.description: Specifies the VLAN's type in the context of Private VLAN. When not set, it will work as regular VLAN.

pvlan_violation_reason.description: Human readable reason for why Private vlan violation occurred  on the VLAN. The value will be populated only when there is a PVLAN misconfiguration. pvlan_default_vlan_join: Default VLAN is not allowed to join Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_erps_inst_pvlans_mismatch: ERPS instances must match for all VLANs in a Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_invalid_primary_association: Secondary VLAN is associated with an invalid Primary VLAN. pvlan_mstp_inst_pvlans_mismatch: MSTP instances must match for all VLANs in a Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_mvrp_cfg_both_present: MVRP and Private-VLAN are mutually exclusive features. pvlan_no_primary_association: No Primary VLAN has been configured for Secondary VLAN. pvlan_primary_vlan_limit_exceeded: Maximum number of Primary VLANs reached. pvlan_rpvst_cfg_both_present: RPVST and Private-VLAN are mutually exclusive features. pvlan_secondary_vlan_limit_exceeded: Maximum number of secondary VLANs reached. pvlan_smartlink_group_pvlans_mismatch: Smartlink groups must match for all VLANs in a Private-VLAN domain. pvlan_vt_cfg_both_present: VLAN translation and PVLAN are mutually exclusive features. secondary_vlan_svi_present: VLAN is a secondary VLAN with SVI configured. pvlan_primary_has_association: VLAN is a primary VLAN but associated to another VLAN.

enable.description: Enables ND Snooping feature on the VLAN. ND Snooping is active on ports of the VLAN only if the feature is enabled at the system level and on the VLAN. This enables nd_guard and ra_guard by default.

nd_guard_enable.description: Enables ND-Guard feature on the VLAN. This takes effect only when Global and VLAN level ND Snooping is also enabled.

ra_drop_enable.description: Enables RA-drop feature on the VLAN. When enabled, RA packets received on the VLAN will be dropped regardless of whether they are received on ND Snooping 'trusted' or 'untrusted' ports. This takes effect only when ND Snooping is also enabled on the VLAN.

ra_guard_enable.description: Enables RA-guard feature on the VLAN. When enabled, RA(Router Advertisement) and RR(Router Redirect) packets received on the VLAN will be dropped on untrusted ports. This takes effect only when Global and VLAN level ND Snooping is also enabled.

ra_guard_log.description: Enables logging of RA(Router Advertisement)  and RR(Router Redirect) dropped packets. This takes effect only when ra_guard is enabled.

nd_snooping_prefix.description: List of network prefix ranges allowed on the VLAN. An ND packet with a source IP not matching any of the prefixes configured here will be dropped. If this is empty, source IP prefix validation is not performed.

vsx_sync.description: Controls which attributes should be synchronized between VSX peers. 'all_attributes_and_dependents': the entire VLAN should be synchronized.

dns_domain_list.description: Domain list names to be used for address resolution, keyed by the  resolution priority order. This column value can be empty.

effective_source_ip.description: Source IP that is being used by various protocols for outgoing packets. IP addresses are selected using following priority: 1. configured 'source_ip' 2. IP of the configured 'source_interface'

all.description: Provides the configuration for supported protocols for which source ip is not configured. This configuration takes care of only IPv4 communication

all_ipv6.description: Provides the configuration for supported protocols for which source ip is not configured. This configuration takes care of only IPv6 communication.

central.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv4 packets for HPE ANW Central. If not present, the key "all" provides the source IP address for outgoing IPv4 packets for HPE ANW Central. Otherwise, regular routing rules take place.

central_ipv6.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv6 packets for HPE ANW Central. If not present, the key "all" provides the source IP address for outgoing IPv6 packets for HPE ANW Central. Otherwise, regular routing rules take place.

dhcp_relay_ipv6.description: Provides source ipv6 for outgoing dhcpv6_relay IPv6 packets. If not present, the key "all" provides the source ipv6 for outgoing dhcpv6_relay IPv6 packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

dns.description: Provides effective source interface for outgoing IPv4 DNS packets. If not present, the key "all", provides the source interface for outgoing IPv4 DNS packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

dns_ipv6.description: Provides effective source interface for outgoing IPv6 DNS packets. If not present, the key "all", provides the source interface for outgoing IPv6 DNS packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

http_ipv6.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv6 http packets. If not present, the key "all_ipv6" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv6 http packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

ipsla.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv4 IP SLA packets. If not present, the key "all" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv4 IP SLA packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

ntp.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv4 NTP packets. If not present, the key "all" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv4 NTP packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

ntp_ipv6.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv6 NTP packets. If not present, the key "all_ipv6" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv6 NTP packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

ptp.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv4 PTP packets. If not present, the key "all" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv4 PTP packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

radius.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv4 radius packets. If not present, the key "all" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv4 radius packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

radius_ipv6.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv6 radius packets. If not present, the key "all_ipv6" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv6 radius packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

sflow_ipv6.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv6 sflow packets. If not present, the key "all_ipv6" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv6 sflow packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

simplivity.description: Provides source ip for outgoing IPv4 SimpliVity protocol packets, If not present, the key "all" provides the source ip for outgoing IPv4 SimpliVity protocol packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

snmp_response.description: Provides effective source IP for the outgoing IPv4 SNMP response. If not present, the key "all" provides the source IP for outgoing SNMP Trap packets. Otherwise regular routing rules take place.

mgmd_dynamic_groups_joined_count.description: Total number of dynamic Groups joined.  This field value could either be empty or explicitly set to 0 to indicate that the number of dynamic groups joined is 0.

mgmd_groups_joined_count.description: Number of exclude and include Groups joined.  This field value could either be empty or explicitly set to 0 to indicate that the number of include/exclude joined groups is 0.

igmp_exclude_groups.description: Number of groups in Exclude mode for IGMP.

igmp_include_groups.description: Number of groups in Include mode for IGMP.

mld_exclude_groups.description: Number of groups in Exclude mode for MLD.

msdp_router.description:

Multicast Source Discovery Protocol Router. If this is not set, MSDP will be disabled on this VRF.

multicast_multipath_hash.description: Hashing algorithm to be used to decide the nexthop when multiple equal cost paths exist to reach a given source address. aclv4_control_plane_status.description: The status of the last version of 'aclv4_control_plane_cfg' column that has been processed.

code.description: Numeric error code. Expected to be 0 when state is 'applied'

message.description: Detailed reason for error state. Expected empty when state is 'applied'

version.description: The version of aclv4_control_plane_cfg that corresponds to this status.

enable.description: When set to `true`, enables inbound HTTPS features including REST API and Web-UI. By default, https_server is enabled on 'mgmt' VRF, disabled on others.

mgmd_dynamic_groups_joined_count.description: Total number of dynamic Groups joined.  This field value could either be empty or explicitly set to 0 to indicate that the number of dynamic groups joined is 0.

msdp_router.description:
Reference Resource: [MSDP_Router](#/MSDP_Router)
Multicast Source Discovery Protocol Router. If this is not set, MSDP will be disabled on this VRF.

multicast_multipath_hash.description: Hashing algorithm to be used to decide the nexthop when multiple equal cost paths exist to reach a given source address. S-hash : This method uses only the source address to compute the hash to pick the nexthop. S-G-hash : This method uses source and group address in the hash calculation. If not set, the global configuration specified for the system will be used. If set, then it overrides the globally configured value.

snmp_engine_boot_count.description: Represents SNMP engine boot count. This column holds the value of number of times the SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) agent is restarted. The min value is 1 and it will increment every time SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) agent is restarted

snmp_engine_up_time.description: SNMP engine uptime in seconds since epoch.

snmp_status.description: This represents SNMP operational status on a VRF.  up - indicates that SNMP is operating on this VRF. down - indicates that SNMP is not operating on this VRF.

authentication_failure.description: Enable sending of SNMP authentication failure traps.

coldstart.description: A coldstart trap will be sent when the switch reboots.

warmstart.description: A warmstart trap will be sent when there is user intervention to enable or disable SNMP service on the switch.

ssh_enable.description: If the value is `true`, then SSH server is enabled on this VRF.

ssh_server_status.description: The running status of the SSH server.

namespace_ready.description: Indicates whether Linux namespace exists for this VRF. If not set, the assumed value is false.

table_id.description: Kernel table_id assigned for routing table of this VRF.

telnet_server_enable.description: If the value is `true`, then TELNET server is enabled on this VRF.

type.description: The VRF type, one of:  + __`user`__:  An ordinary VRF created by user referred to as ``user VRFs'' since they are generally connected to data ports. + __`default`__:  default VRF for all routed interfaces + __`management`__: A management VRF that contains out of band management (mgmt) interface only.

parameters.name: VRF.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF identifier. Should be alphanumeric. VRF names must be unique.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Columns to display.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Depth to traverse.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Select configuration, status and/or statistics. Default is all categories.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter rows by attribute values.  Format: attribute:value

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Count the number of rows found.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Entity-tag value for representation comparison (see RFC 7232 - Conditional Requests - section 3.2)

aclv4_control_plane_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv4 ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to control plane traffic, as identified in the ACL. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv4_control_plane_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv4_control_plane_cfg' column. This value should be changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv4_control_plane_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv6_control_plane_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv6 ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to control plane traffic, as identified in the ACL. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv6_control_plane_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv6_control_plane_cfg' column. This value should be changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv6_control_plane_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

bgp_routers.description:
Reference Resource: [BGP_Router](#/BGP_Router)
BGP routers keyed by ASN value.

default_loose_nexthop_resolution_ipv4.description: If the value is `false`, then default route shall not be  used in recursive routes resolution of IPv4 routes.

default_loose_nexthop_resolution_ipv6.description: If the value is `false`, then default route shall not be  used in recursive routes resolution of IPv6 routes.

dhcp_server.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCP_Server](#/DHCP_Server)
DHCPv4 Server in the VRF.

dhcpv4_snooping_authorized_servers.description: When configured, switch forwards DHCPv4 reply packets on trusted ports only if packet is from one of the authorized servers.

dhcpv6_server.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCPV6_Server](#/DHCPV6_Server)
DHCPv6 Server in the VRF.

dhcpv6_snooping_authorized_servers.description: When configured, switch forwards DHCPv6 reply packets on trusted ports only if packet is from one of the authorized servers.

dns_domain_list.description: Domain list names to be used for address resolution, keyed by the  resolution priority order. This column value can be empty.

dns_domain_name.description: Domain name used for name resolution by the DNS client, if `dns_domain_list` is not configured. If both the configurations are not present, name resolution is performed with empty domain suffix. This column value can be empty.

dns_host_v4_address_mapping.description: List of static host address configurations and the IPv4 address associated with them.

dns_host_v6_address_mapping.description: List of static host address configurations and the IPv6 address associated with them.

dns_name_servers.description: Name servers to be used for address resolution, keyed by the  resolution priority order

evpn_export_route_targets.description: BGP route targets, formatted as ASN:NN or A.B.C.D:NN, to be sent with the EVPN routes exported from the VRF. Option 'auto' to export auto-generated route-targets from the VRF.

evpn_import_route_targets.description: BGP route targets, formatted as ASN:NN or A.B.C.D:NN, to be matched to the EVPN routes being imported into the VRF. Option 'auto' to import based on auto-generated route-targets into the VRF.

enable.description: When set to `true`, enables inbound HTTPS features including REST API and Web-UI. By default, https_server is enabled on 'mgmt' VRF, disabled on others.

l3vpn_only_enable.description: If the value is `true`, then only L3VPN support is enabled for this VRF.

msdp_router.description:
Reference Resource: [MSDP_Router](#/MSDP_Router)
Multicast Source Discovery Protocol Router. If this is not set, MSDP will be disabled on this VRF.

multicast_multipath_hash.description: Hashing algorithm to be used to decide the nexthop when multiple equal cost paths exist to reach a given source address. S-hash : This method uses only the source address to compute the hash to pick the nexthop. S-G-hash : This method uses source and group address in the hash calculation. If not set, the global configuration specified for the system will be used. If set, then it overrides the globally configured value.

rd.description: Route distinguisher in ASN:nn format or IP:nn format. This is optional.

Reference Resource: [VRF](#/VRF)
VRF identifier. Should be alphanumeric. VRF names must be unique.

aclv4_control_plane_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv4 ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to control plane traffic, as identified in the ACL. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv4_control_plane_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv4_control_plane_cfg' column. This value should be changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv4_control_plane_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

aclv6_control_plane_cfg.description:
Reference Resource: [ACL](#/ACL)
IPv6 ACL, potentially in flight, desired to be applied to control plane traffic, as identified in the ACL. An empty column value indicates that no list is applied for this type and direction.

aclv6_control_plane_cfg_version.description: The version of the 'aclv6_control_plane_cfg' column. This value should be changed to a random value each time any management interface modifies the 'aclv6_control_plane_cfg' value. An empty column value will indicate that the user does not want the system to process this configuration yet.

bgp_routers.description:
Reference Resource: [BGP_Router](#/BGP_Router)
BGP routers keyed by ASN value.

default_loose_nexthop_resolution_ipv4.description: If the value is `false`, then default route shall not be  used in recursive routes resolution of IPv4 routes.

default_loose_nexthop_resolution_ipv6.description: If the value is `false`, then default route shall not be  used in recursive routes resolution of IPv6 routes.

dhcp_server.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCP_Server](#/DHCP_Server)
DHCPv4 Server in the VRF.

dhcpv4_snooping_authorized_servers.description: When configured, switch forwards DHCPv4 reply packets on trusted ports only if packet is from one of the authorized servers.

dhcpv6_server.description:
Reference Resource: [DHCPV6_Server](#/DHCPV6_Server)
DHCPv6 Server in the VRF.

dhcpv6_snooping_authorized_servers.description: When configured, switch forwards DHCPv6 reply packets on trusted ports only if packet is from one of the authorized servers.

dns_domain_list.description: Domain list names to be used for address resolution, keyed by the  resolution priority order. This column value can be empty.

dns_domain_name.description: Domain name used for name resolution by the DNS client, if `dns_domain_list` is not configured. If both the configurations are not present, name resolution is performed with empty domain suffix. This column value can be empty.

dns_host_v4_address_mapping.description: List of static host address configurations and the IPv4 address associated with them.

dns_host_v6_address_mapping.description: List of static host address configurations and the IPv6 address associated with them.

dns_name_servers.description: Name servers to be used for address resolution, keyed by the  resolution priority order

evpn_export_route_targets.description: BGP route targets, formatted as ASN:NN or A.B.C.D:NN, to be sent with the EVPN routes exported from the VRF. Option 'auto' to export auto-generated route-targets from the VRF.

evpn_import_route_targets.description: BGP route targets, formatted as ASN:NN or A.B.C.D:NN, to be matched to the EVPN routes being imported into the VRF. Option 'auto' to import based on auto-generated route-targets into the VRF.

enable.description: When set to `true`, enables inbound HTTPS features including REST API and Web-UI. By default, https_server is enabled on 'mgmt' VRF, disabled on others.

l3vpn_only_enable.description: If the value is `true`, then only L3VPN support is enabled for this VRF.

msdp_router.description:
Reference Resource: [MSDP_Router](#/MSDP_Router)
Multicast Source Discovery Protocol Router. If this is not set, MSDP will be disabled on this VRF.

multicast_multipath_hash.description: Hashing algorithm to be used to decide the nexthop when multiple equal cost paths exist to reach a given source address. S-hash : This method uses only the source address to compute the hash to pick the nexthop. S-G-hash : This method uses source and group address in the hash calculation. If not set, the global configuration specified for the system will be used. If set, then it overrides the globally configured value.

active_advertise_interval.description: Specifies advertisement interval in milliseconds which is advertised by active router.

admin_enable.description: Set this value to `true`, to activate the VR instance.

auth_key.description: Authentication key to be used with VRRPv2 advertisements. This does not take effect if the VRRP version is VRRPv3. If not set, VRRP authentication is not operational on that VR.

auth_mode.description: Specifies the authentication mode to be used when exchanging VRRP packets.
